# @danitesler/ayywi 0.1.2 — full context for LLMs

> The AI-first design system (say "AY-wee": AI + UI). One CSS class contract for HTML, Vue, Svelte, Angular, server templates, plus typed React components, a linter and an MCP server.

Generated from source by scripts/build-manifest.mjs. Structured version: manifest/components.json. Query it live with the MCP server: `npx @danitesler/ayywi mcp`.

## How to use it

- Any framework / plain HTML: load `@danitesler/ayywi/css` and write the class names below.
- React: `import { Button } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react"` plus the CSS.
- Vue, Svelte, Angular, Solid, Lit: class names or helpers (`import { buttonClass } from "@danitesler/ayywi"`), and `import "@danitesler/ayywi/elements"` for interactive components (<ayy-toolbar>, <ayy-action-bar>, <ayy-menu>, <ayy-command>, <ayy-navbar>, <ayy-app-shell>, <ayy-toc>, <ayy-tree>, <ayy-pin-input>, <ayy-mentions>, <ayy-block-editor>, <ayy-inline-edit>, <ayy-combobox>, <ayy-tag-input>, <ayy-record-picker>, <ayy-transfer-list>, <ayy-date-picker>, <ayy-date-range>, <ayy-time-picker>, <ayy-date-time-picker>, <ayy-color-picker>, <ayy-icon-picker>, <ayy-shortcut-recorder>, <ayy-tabs>, <ayy-carousel>, <ayy-drag-drop>, <ayy-dialog>, <ayy-popover>, <ayy-tooltip>, <ayy-swipe>, <ayy-table>, <ayy-grid>).
- Plain HTML: `<link rel="stylesheet" href=".../dist/ayywi.min.css">` + `<script src=".../dist/elements.global.js" defer></script>` (also gives window.ayywi: toast, configureToaster, trackInputModality, getInputModality, setTheme, getTheme, getResolvedTheme, getColorScheme, setDensity, getDensity, setBrand, createBrand, brandCss, brandPresets, chartColors, chartTheme). Add `<link rel="stylesheet" href=".../dist/fonts.css">` before it for ayywi's fonts (Sora, Unbounded; system fonts otherwise), and `<script src=".../dist/theme-init.js"></script>` in <head> so a saved theme applies before the first paint.
- Copy-ready HTML and React examples: one page per component, `llms/<slug>.md` (llms/button.md, llms/table.md…), listed in llms.txt. This file has every component's API but no examples.
- Check your work: `npx @danitesler/ayywi lint`.

## Installing and updating

- Install from npm: `pnpm add @danitesler/ayywi` (or npm/yarn), then `npx @danitesler/ayywi init`. Import only from "@danitesler/ayywi" and its subpaths ("/react", "/elements", "/css", "/fonts.css", "/brands/*", "/fonts/*"). Never from "ayywi": that name is only the CLI. Never reach into node_modules/@danitesler/ayywi/dist by path.
- Never vendor ayywi: no copy of its dist/ in the repo, no .tgz, no file: or link: dependency in a committed package.json. A fresh clone must install with the package manager alone.
- To change ayywi while building an app, point the app's bundler at a local ayywi checkout only for that session (a Vite resolve.alias read from an AYYWI_DIR environment variable, with resolve.dedupe for react and react-dom), and run `pnpm build` in the checkout after each change. Never commit that link.
- Upgrade with `pnpm up @danitesler/ayywi`, then `npx @danitesler/ayywi init --force` so the skill, rules and AGENTS.md section match the installed version, and read the CHANGELOG between the two versions.
- When ayywi has no component or variant for something, compose it from ayywi pieces in the app, mark it with a `// ayywi-candidate: <what it is>` comment, and add it to ayywi itself when a second screen or app needs it. Never fork, copy or restyle an ayywi component inside the app.

## Rules

- Use existing ayywi classes/components and their variants before writing any custom CSS. Never rebuild one under your own name (a .x-chip, .x-card, a <button> styled by hand) or restyle one: your class next to its ayy- class sets only layout (margin, size, position). If nothing fits, compose ayywi pieces. Never add a second UI kit. Never write a raw native control (<button>, <select>, <input>, <textarea>, <table>, <dialog>, <details>) or a <div>/<span> with a click handler: each is an ayywi component. Before writing a screen, name the component for every piece by what it has to do (the Need → component map, or the MCP pick_component tool).
- Never hardcode colours (hex, rgb, hsl, named) — in stylesheets or in inline styles. Use var(--ayy-color-*) tokens; for tints use color-mix(in srgb, var(--ayy-color-text) N%, transparent) or the wash/line tokens.
- Use logical properties only: margin-inline-start, padding-inline, inset-inline-end, text-align: start, inline-size. Never left/right/margin-left/padding-right, so RTL works.
- Spacing, sizes, radius, type and motion come from tokens (--ayy-space-*, --ayy-size-*, --ayy-radius-*, --ayy-text-*, --ayy-weight-*, --ayy-leading-*, --ayy-control-*, --ayy-shadow-*, --ayy-ease-*, --ayy-duration-*). Control sizes follow data-density — don't hardcode heights.
- Theme with data-theme="dark|light|dark-contrast|light-gray" (or nothing = follow OS). Never write separate dark-mode colours; tokens already switch. To restyle, override semantic tokens rather than editing components.
- Brand a product with a generated brand, never hand-picked colours: `npx @danitesler/ayywi brand <#seed> --name <name>` (or createBrand()/setBrand() from "@danitesler/ayywi", or the MCP create_brand tool) makes the colour scale, primary, primary-fg and ring for every theme with contrast checked, plus fonts and corners (--shape pill|round|soft|sharp). Load its CSS and set data-brand. Colour beyond primary comes from --ayy-brand-50…950 (the scale) for illustrations and brand moments, never on navigation or page backgrounds.
- Every interactive element keeps its visible :focus-visible ring. Icon-only buttons need aria-label. Form controls need a label. State lives in native/ARIA attributes (disabled, checked, aria-selected, aria-current, aria-expanded, aria-invalid, aria-busy, open).
- Toolbar items and icon-only buttons get a Tooltip explaining their action on hover and keyboard focus, paired with a keyboard hint element (<Shortcut keys="..." /> in React, .ayy-shortcut in HTML) whenever a shortcut exists. Never use native title="" attributes.
- Every component's spec lists its states (default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled, selected, error, loading, plus its own such as open) and its sizes, in manifest/components.json, llms/<slug>.md and get_component. Reach a state only through the attribute or prop its spec names. Where a state says it doesn't apply, do what it says instead; never style a state a component doesn't have.
- Stateful styles need a @media (forced-colors: active) fallback (Windows High Contrast erases fills).
- Prefer animating transform and opacity (use a logical property like inset-inline-start only when the motion must follow text direction). Everything must still work under prefers-reduced-motion — base.css collapses ayy animations. Scroll-in motion comes from .ayy-reveal, not a script; nothing loops unless it shows a live state. Movement on :hover (lifts, zooms, spins) goes inside @media (hover: hover), because a tap leaves :hover stuck on touch screens.
- The frame is monochrome; colour comes from the content. Set --ayy-spot (to an --ayy-accent-* token) on the card or page that shows the content, and the spotlight, contents bar, icon tiles and .ayy-accent-text inside pick it up. Never tint the navbar, sidebar, buttons or page background per page.
- Websites follow one anatomy: .ayy-skip-link, a Navbar (with a NavbarToggle so its links fold into a menu on phones), then <main> at .ayy-container width (fading Separators between marketing sections), then the Footer. The page's call to action is a ring button (the navbar's repeats the same action); everything else outline or ghost.
- Apps (anything signed-in) follow one frame: .ayy-skip-link, then the App shell — a sidebar on wide screens; on phones an __bar (brand plus one or two actions) and a Bottom nav with the sidebar's top destinations, same icons and order (four and a More tab when there are more). Each screen in its main starts with a Page header: the one h1, a line of description, at most one primary button; on phones a screen pushed from a list starts with a Top bar (back, title, actions) instead, and a screen's one main create action can be a Floating action button. Lists of rows on phones get Swipe actions for their two or three most common actions, which are also reachable elsewhere. Settings open over the app in a near-full-screen Dialog (size="full") holding the App shell in settings mode (the Settings pattern: a Settings title and the sections in its sidebar; one section of Settings rows in its main; on phones the dialog fills the screen and the section list and a section are two screens), never in a small or side dialog; desktop apps add a Command palette on ⌘K. Never put a Navbar in an app.
- An app screen fills the main. Don't wrap it in .ayy-container or a max-inline-size — a max-inline-size on an example only sizes that example in the docs, it is not page layout. Long text (a description, .ayy-prose) may stop at --ayy-size-measure. Settings mode already centres its column; don't add a second cap.
- Every list, table and page has three more states: loading (Skeleton in the shape of the content with aria-busy; a Spinner or <Button loading> for an action), empty (an Empty state with the action that fills it) and error (an Alert with a retry for a failed load or save; FieldError next to a field).
- Data views use ayywi's own pieces: Chart (BarChart, LineChart, DonutChart, ScatterChart, HeatmapChart, FunnelChart and the rest), Bar list and Sparkline for charts, coloured from --ayy-chart-1… in order; filters as Chips (with counts) above the results and the active ones as removable chips; sortable Table columns with a .ayy-table__sort button and aria-sort on the <th>. With a chart library, colour it with var(--ayy-chart-N) (SVG) or chartColors() and chartTheme() (canvas); never its default palette.
- Pick form controls by the choice: a Segmented control for two to five short options, Choice cards when each option needs a sentence or a price (compact for time slots), a Select for a short list, a Combobox for many known values, a Transfer list to move items between available and chosen lists, a PIN input for verification codes or PINs, Mentions for inline @mentions or #references inside a textarea, a Rating for 1–5 star scores, a Number field for small counts, a Slider for a rough amount, a DatePicker or DatePickerGrid for a date near today (DateRange / DateRangePicker for a date span, TimePicker / TimePickerTrigger for stepped times, DateTimePicker / DateTimePickerTrigger for date and time, native type="date" for a birth date, type="time" for rapid typing), ColorSwatches for a fixed palette or ColorPicker for any custom colour, a Tag input for free-text tags or recipients, a Search bar to filter a list, a Shortcut recorder for key bindings, File upload for files.
- Don't write breakpoints for navigation or layout: App shell, Navbar and Pagination switch at 48rem on their own, and .ayy-grid and .ayy-split adapt to their container. If you truly need one, use 48rem (phone) or 64rem (tablet).
- Every <img> gets width and height (its real size) so nothing jumps while it loads. Product screenshots go in a Frame. Draw small product visuals as SVG with tokens instead of images with text baked in.
- No :dir() selectors — minifiers rewrite them into :lang() lists that ignore dir="rtl". Logical properties make direction checks unnecessary.
- Body text must fall back to system fonts — never remove the system-ui stack from --ayy-font-body (CJK/Arabic/Cyrillic rely on it).
- Icons come from Hugeicons (@hugeicons/core-free-icons): <Icon icon={Search01Icon} /> in React, iconSvg(Search01Icon) or the pasted SVG with class="ayy-icon" elsewhere. Don't add another icon set. Icons are decorative (aria-hidden) unless you give them a label; arrows that point along the reading direction take directional.
- In React import from "@danitesler/ayywi/react"; in other frameworks and plain HTML use the class names, the class helpers from "@danitesler/ayywi" (buttonClass…) and the custom elements from "@danitesler/ayywi/elements" (<ayy-app-shell>, <ayy-navbar>, <ayy-tabs>, <ayy-combobox>, <ayy-date-picker>, <ayy-date-range>, <ayy-time-picker>, <ayy-date-time-picker>, <ayy-color-picker>, <ayy-icon-picker>, <ayy-toolbar>, <ayy-action-bar>, <ayy-shortcut-recorder>, <ayy-command>, <ayy-tag-input>, <ayy-record-picker>, <ayy-pin-input>, <ayy-mentions>, <ayy-block-editor>, <ayy-transfer-list>, <ayy-inline-edit>, <ayy-swipe>, <ayy-drag-drop>, <ayy-dialog>, <ayy-menu>, <ayy-popover>, <ayy-tooltip>, <ayy-toc>, <ayy-tree>, <ayy-carousel>, <ayy-table>, <ayy-grid>).
- Run `npx @danitesler/ayywi lint` after UI changes and fix every finding it reports, warnings included: raw-control, bare-control, clickable-element and rebuilt-component mean an ayywi component was skipped.

## Need → component

Name the component for every piece of a screen before writing it. Each "Not" is what gets hand-built instead; `ayywi lint` flags it.

| Need | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| Run an action (save, create, delete, open) | Button: one primary per view, outline/ghost for the rest, destructive for delete, size icon + aria-label for icon-only; SplitButton + DropdownMenu when one default action has secondary alternatives. | <button> with your own classes or none, a <div>/<span> with onClick, a link styled as a button for an action |
| Choose one value from a list (theme, country, role, sort order) | Select for a list (it opens ayywi's own options list; touch screens keep the OS picker), Segmented control for two to five short options shown at once, Combobox for many values people type to find. | a raw <select>, a button that opens a hand-built <div> of choices, a Dropdown menu used as a picker |
| Choose between options that each need a sentence, an icon or a price (plans, delivery, time slots) | ChoiceGroup of ChoiceCards (compact for time slots, scroll for a day strip). | Cards with onClick and a selected class |
| Switch between views or ranges of the same content (list/grid, 7d/30d) | SegmentedControl, two to five options. | a row of buttons with aria-pressed or an active class |
| Show one of several panels of content | Tabs (TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent). | a Segmented control or buttons that swap panels |
| Turn a setting on or off (a toggle: notifications, dark mode, auto-save) | Switch when it applies at once; Checkbox in a form that's submitted, or to agree to something. | <input type="checkbox"> unstyled, a toggle drawn with divs |
| Pick one of a few options in a form | Radio group; a Segmented control when the options are short. | raw <input type="radio"> |
| Filter a list or tag things | Chips (checkbox, radio or ChipButton, with counts) above the results, the active ones as removable chips; Tag input for free-text tags or recipients. | pills built from <span>s or buttons with an active class |
| Move items between two lists (available vs assigned permissions, columns or members) | TransferList (<ayy-transfer-list> in HTML) with searchable Available and Selected panes and Move selected / Move all buttons. | two custom list boxes with hand-wired state and arrow buttons |
| Filter a list, table or feed (status tabs, faceted dropdowns, active chips) | FilterBar with quick filter tabs (FilterBarTabs), faceted dropdown triggers (FilterBarTrigger) with count badges, and active filter chips with a Clear all button. | a row of custom buttons with active classes, hand-built filter bars |
| Sort a list, table or feed by field and direction | Sorting with SortingTrigger opening a DropdownMenu of sort options, or sortable Table column headers. | a button that flips a state with no accessible label, hand-drawn sort arrows |
| Type text, an email, a number or a password | Field + Label + Input (Input group for an icon or a unit, Textarea for long text, Number field for small counts), FieldHint and FieldError under it. | a raw <input>/<textarea>, a placeholder instead of a label |
| Enter a verification code, OTP or PIN | PinInput (<ayy-pin-input> in HTML) inside a Field, with group for a split 3+3 code and mask for secret PINs. | six separate <input maxlength="1"> elements wired by hand or a single plain text input |
| Write or edit a rich document: notes, a page, a description with headings, lists, to-dos, images and embeds | BlockEditor (<ayy-block-editor> in HTML): Notion-style blocks with / for block types, Markdown shortcuts, a formatting bar, @ mentions and drag handles; store its value (blocks) or convert with blockEditorToMarkdown / blockEditorToHtml. | a <textarea> with a Markdown preview, execCommand on one big contenteditable, or a third-party rich text library |
| Mention people or reference issues inline in a comment (@user, #issue) | Mentions (<ayy-mentions> in HTML) wrapping a textarea and suggestion listbox. | contenteditable rich-text hacks or an unanchored dropdown under a textarea |
| Give or display a star rating or review score | Rating (interactive radio stars with optional half and clearable, or readOnly for fractional scores). | buttons or spans of ★ characters with custom click handlers |
| Search or filter by typing | Search bar to filter what's on screen, Combobox to pick a value, Command palette (⌘K) to jump anywhere. | an <input> with a hand-drawn magnifier |
| Pick a date or time | DatePicker or DatePickerGrid for one date near today; DateRange or DateRangePicker for a start and end span; TimePicker or TimePickerTrigger for discrete hours and minutes; DateTimePicker or DateTimePickerTrigger for combined date and time; Input type="date" for a birth date, type="time" for rapid keyboard entry. | a hand-built month grid or time dropdown |
| Pick an icon or emoji | IconPicker (<ayy-icon-picker>) in a Popover or a menu's submenu panel: search, a grid of Hugeicons and emoji, and a remove button. | a menu with one item per icon, a hand-built emoji grid |
| Pick a colour | ColorSwatches for a fixed set of choices, ColorSwatchCustom or ColorPicker for any custom colour with hue/alpha/hex. | a raw <input type="color">, coloured buttons |
| Set an amount or a range | Slider / SliderRange for a rough amount or a price range, Number field for exact small counts. | a raw <input type="range"> |
| Upload files | Dropzone (compact in a form), then a List divided of the files with a Progress each. | a raw <input type="file">, a dashed div |
| Drag and drop reordering, board or kanban | Sortable with SortableItem and DragHandle (or DragDropArea with DropTargets and <ayy-drag-drop> in HTML). | a third-party dnd library, raw HTML5 dragstart handlers |
| Record a keyboard shortcut or show one | Shortcut recorder to set one; Kbd / Shortcut to show one. | a <kbd> or <span> styled by hand |
| Show a code snippet, command or config file | CodeBlock with CodeBlockHeader, CodeBlockFilename, CodeBlockCopy, CodeBlockPre and CodeBlockCode (numbered for line numbers, .ayy-token-* for syntax tokens). | a raw <pre> with custom background and copy button |
| Show activity history, audit log or chronological events | Timeline of TimelineItems (TimelineMarker with pulse on live events, TimelineTime, TimelineTitle, TimelineBody; alternate for wide milestone pages). | divs with a border-left line and absolute dots |
| Show more actions behind a button (⋯, a user menu) | DropdownMenu of items; destructive item last. | a hand-built absolutely positioned <div> |
| Ask to confirm, or collect a few fields over the page | Dialog (DialogContent, title, body, footer with the primary action last). | window.confirm(), a fixed <div> with a backdrop |
| A side panel, drawer or bottom sheet | Dialog with side="end", "start" or "bottom". | a custom fixed div that slides in |
| Settings for an app | The Settings pattern: a full-size Dialog holding the App shell in settings mode, Settings groups of SettingsRow / SettingsLink. | a settings page with Tabs, a small dialog, rows built from divs |
| Small extra content on click (details, a mini form) | Popover. | a hand-positioned div |
| Explain an icon button on hover or focus | Tooltip (the button keeps its aria-label); add a Shortcut inside for its keyboard hint. | title="" or a CSS-only bubble |
| Confirm something happened, or offer undo | toast.success() / toast() with an action. | a hand-built fixed banner |
| Show a capture, video or file preview with quick corner actions | toast.card() or CardToast for screen captures, video thumbnails and quick actions. | a custom corner popup, fixed floating card without a toaster stack |
| Tell people about a problem or a state on the page | Alert (destructive with a retry for a failed load or save). | a coloured <div> |
| Show loading | Skeleton in the shape of the content (aria-busy on the region), Spinner for a small area, Button loading for an action, Progress for a known amount. | "Loading…" text, a hand-drawn spinner |
| Nothing to show yet, or no results | Empty state with the action that fills it (compact inside a card or table). | a centred muted paragraph |
| Group content in a box | Card with CardHeader / CardTitle / CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter; CardLink when the whole card opens something. | a <div> with a border, radius and padding |
| Rows of things (members, files, threads, settings) | List (ListLink for clickable rows, divided for settings-style rows); Settings for preference rows; Swipe actions on phones. | <ul>/<div> rows with your own borders and hover, <li onClick> |
| Records compared across columns | Table (sortable headers, a select column, TableRowActions with inline quick buttons and a ⋯ DropdownMenu), ActionBar when rows are selected, Pagination under it. | a raw <table>, a CSS grid of divs |
| Captures, recordings or pictures to open, with their details and actions on hover (a screenshot history, a media library) | Cards of the view type (Card view) in a .ayy-grid: CardViewMedia (a button or link that opens it) with CardViewImage letterboxed over a blurred copy, CardViewBadge for a recording's length, CardViewBody for title, details and badges, and grouped HoverActions with a ⋯ DropdownMenu. Use Grid instead when people select several. | a plain Card with CardMedia and an <img>, a hand-built gradient caption, absolutely positioned buttons that appear on hover |
| Icon actions over a picture, a video frame or a card (copy, annotate, pin, delete) | HoverActions in a corner (position) of the picture's box, reveal to show them on hover and focus, group to put them on one glass bar; each HoverAction has a label that is also its tooltip. | ghost buttons restyled with a translucent background, title="" tooltips, buttons that only appear on :hover with no keyboard way to reach them |
| Selectable cards of media assets, screenshots, social posts, projects or user records | Grid of GridItems (GridItemSelect checkbox, GridItemActions with inline quick actions and a ⋯ DropdownMenu, GridItemMedia for previews), ActionBar when items are selected. | Cards with custom onClick selection state or hand-built floating checkboxes |
| Run bulk actions on selected table rows or grid items (edit, duplicate, copy, archive, delete) | ActionBar (open when selection count > 0) with ActionBarSelection, ActionBarCount, ActionBarClose and ActionBarActions of ActionBarButtons (destructive last). | a hand-built fixed bottom bar or static buttons above the table |
| A number that matters (KPI) | Card + Stat + a status Badge, a Sparkline beside it. | big bold text in a div |
| A chart | BarChart (grouped, stacked, 100%, horizontal, with lines), LineChart (area, stacked, step), HistogramChart, WaterfallChart, ScatterChart (bubbles), DonutChart (pie), GaugeChart, RadarChart, HeatmapChart, FunnelChart, BarList, Sparkline, coloured from --ayy-chart-1… in order. | a chart library's default palette, divs as bars |
| A status, count or label on something | Badge (status variants). | a coloured <span> pill |
| Show live status, online presence or server health as a compact dot | StatusDot (neutral, success, warning, destructive, info variants; pulse for live activity). | a coloured <span> or <div> with border-radius: 50%, hand-drawn ping keyframes |
| A person or a team | Avatar (image with initials fallback), AvatarGroup. | a round <img> or initials in a div |
| Collapsible sections or FAQ | Accordion (single to keep one open). | a raw <details>, a div toggled by a button |
| A multi-step flow | Steps above the form, one primary Continue per step. | numbered circles drawn by hand |
| The frame of an app | App shell (sidebar, a bar and a Bottom nav on phones), each screen starting with a Page header. | a hand-built sidebar, header or bottom tab bar |
| The top of a website | Navbar with a NavbarToggle so links fold into a menu on phones. | a <header> of links with a hand-built burger menu |
| Where you are, or which page of results | Breadcrumb for nested pages, Pagination for pages of results. | links separated by slashes, numbered buttons |
| A screen pushed from a list on a phone | Top bar (back, title, actions). | a hand-built header with a back arrow |
| A screenshot or picture of the product | Frame around it. | an <img> with a border and shadow |
| Preview UI across responsive viewports with device switcher | Showcase with ShowcaseHeader, ShowcaseTitle, ShowcaseActions, ShowcaseStage, and ShowcaseViewport (desktop, tablet, mobile). | hand-built iframe wrappers or ad-hoc responsive preview containers |
| Light/dark switch | Dropdown menu of themes (radio items) that calls setTheme(); an icon trigger shows the current one. Inside settings, use the theme picker of the Appearance need instead. | a button that flips a class |
| Appearance settings: theme, density, text size, brand colour, corners, font, reduce motion, language or direction | In the Settings pattern's Appearance section: a Select with pictures for each choice: a SettingsScreen for Theme, Corners and Text direction, variant="rows" for Density, variant="brand" for Brand colour (a Custom option opens the colour picker), and "Aa" samples for Font and Text size; Switch for reduce motion (data-motion="reduce"); Select for language; a destructive SettingsLink to reset. Apply at once with setTheme(), setDensity(), setBrand(). | a theme Select or a plain radio list, hand-drawn theme thumbnails or screenshots, a raw <input type="color">, Choice cards with only text, a button opening a popover of choices, a Slider for text size, a SegmentedControl for direction, swatches in the row for brand colour |

## Patterns

Screens made of several components that every app builds the same way. Follow them instead of composing your own.

### Settings

Settings open in a large dialog over the app, the way they do in Notion and Claude. The sidebar lists the sections, the main area shows the one you picked, and on phones it goes full screen. Don't use a small or side dialog, or tabs inside a page.

Built from: App shell, Top bar, Settings, Switch, Select, Segmented control, Shortcut, Button, Dialog, Toast. Example: App shell → "Playground — one shell, every variation" (`get_component app-shell`, llms/app-shell.md).

**How**
1. Entry: a Settings link in the sidebar's AppShellFooter (an icon and "Settings"). On phones, the same link in the More drawer, or a settings icon button in the AppShellBar. Desktop apps also open it on ⌘, (Ctrl+, elsewhere).
2. Open: a Dialog with <DialogContent size="full" aria-labelledby="<the title's id>"> (class ayy-dialog--full) over the page the user was on, holding an AppShell with settings (class ayy-app-shell--settings). Its AppShellSidebar holds, in order: AppShellTitle ("Settings", with the id the dialog points at) and an AppShellNav aria-label="Settings" of AppShellGroups ("Account": profile, preferences, notifications; "Workspace" or "App": the app's own areas; "About" last). Its main is <AppShellMain as="div"> (the page keeps its one <main>). No AppShellBack, AppShellBar, BottomNav or brand: the dialog's close button is the way out.
3. Sections: the open section's AppShellLink has current (aria-current="page"); a link click switches the section in place. On wide screens settings open on the first section; on phones on the section list.
4. Section: the main starts with a TopBar (title = the section's name, its <h1>; onBack returns to the section list, backLabel = "Settings"; its back button shows on phones only), then one Settings group per topic (title, optional description) holding SettingsRows (a Switch, Select, SegmentedControl, Shortcut recorder or Button at the end) and SettingsLinks (rows that open a sub-page or run an action). The content column is --ayy-size-measure wide, centred; the shell does that.
5. Saving: switches, selects and segmented controls apply at once; confirm with a Toast only when the effect isn't visible. Free text (a name, a folder path) saves on blur or Enter. Anything that must be submitted together (a password change) is a Dialog opened from a SettingsLink.
6. Appearance: an Appearance section uses the same controls in every product (see settings/appearance). Theme, Density, Text size, Brand colour, Corners, Font and Text direction are each a Select with pictures (one per option, the chosen one before the text, each in the list): SettingsScreens for Theme (System, Light, Dark, Black, Light gray; setTheme()), Corners (each shape's radii) and Text direction (Auto, which follows the language, Left to right, Right to left; dir on the screen and on the app); SettingsScreen variant="rows" for Density (Auto, Compact, Comfortable, Touch; setDensity()); SettingsScreen variant="brand" with --ayy-color-primary for Brand colour (Default, a few palette colours and Custom, which opens the colour picker on a hidden <input type="color" data-value="custom"> after the select; setBrand()); and "Aa" samples for Font and for Text size (75% to 150%, setting the root font size). Reduce motion: a Switch that sets data-motion="reduce". Language: a Select. Reset appearance: a destructive SettingsLink in its own group.
7. Danger: Sign out, Reset and Delete account go last, in their own Settings group, as destructive SettingsLinks; destructive ones confirm in a Dialog.
8. Leave: the dialog's close button, Esc or a click on the backdrop. The dialog puts focus back on the Settings link the user came from.

**Phones**
- Below 48rem the dialog fills the screen and the settings shell is two screens, picked by aria-current: with no section current, the sidebar is the screen (a large "Settings" title, the sections as rows with chevrons); with one current, the section fills it and its TopBar's back returns to the list. Move focus to the section when it opens and back to its link when it closes.
- Settings rows wrap the control under the label when there isn't room; never shrink a control below its size.
- For a choice with more than five options on a phone, use a SettingsLink with the current value that opens a sub-page with a radio list, instead of a long Select.
- Touch density (data-density="touch") raises sidebar items and rows to 52px; nothing is sized by hand.

**Specs** (don't restyle these)
- **Sidebar item (.ayy-app-shell__link, in the app and in settings)**: --ayy-size-control-lg high (40px compact, 48px comfortable, 52px touch), padding-inline --ayy-space-3, a --ayy-size-icon-md (20px) icon then --ayy-space-2, --ayy-control-text-lg, medium weight, --ayy-radius-pill. Muted text; hover: --ayy-color-wash and the text colour; current (aria-current="page"): --ayy-color-wash-hover, the text colour, semibold. Items --ayy-space-0-5 apart. Groups: an uppercase --ayy-text-s label, and a hairline with --ayy-space-4 margin and --ayy-space-5 padding above every group after the first.
- **Settings group (.ayy-settings)**: A <section> labelled by its <h2> (--ayy-text-md, semibold), an optional muted --ayy-text-sm description, then the rows in a card: a 1px --ayy-color-line border, --ayy-radius-card, --ayy-color-surface. Groups are --ayy-space-6 apart. .ayy-settings--plain (no card) only in a sheet or dialog that already has a surface.
- **Settings row (.ayy-settings__row)**: At least --ayy-size-control-lg high, padding --ayy-space-3 block and --ayy-space-4 inline, --ayy-space-4 between the text and the control. Label --ayy-text-sm medium; hint --ayy-text-xs muted, one line. The control sits at the inline end. A 1px --ayy-color-hairline between rows only: none above the first or below the last.
- **Section header (.ayy-top-bar in the settings main)**: Sticky, the page colour with a hairline under it; title semibold (--ayy-text-xl in the dialog on wide screens, --ayy-text-md on phones), lined up with the content column. One <h1> per section.
- **Settings dialog (.ayy-dialog--full)**: Up to 72rem by 50rem, 4rem clear of the viewport on each axis, no padding: the settings shell fills it, the sidebar 15rem. The whole screen below 48rem, without border or radius. The close button sits in the top-end corner over the section's Top bar.

**Do**
- Use this pattern for every settings, preferences or account screen in an app, however few settings there are.
- Name sections with one noun (General, Appearance, Notifications, Shortcuts, Data, About) and give each a Hugeicons icon in the sidebar.
- Keep every setting's label short and put the why in its hint.
- Use the Appearance controls above for theme, density, text size, brand colour, corners, font, motion, language and direction, so these settings look and work the same in every product.

**Don't**
- Don't put settings in a small or side Dialog, a Popover or Tabs inside a page: they can't hold a growing list of sections, and they end up looking different in every app.
- Don't put the app's destinations, bar or bottom nav inside the settings dialog; its close button is the way out.
- Don't restyle sidebar items or settings rows (radius, padding, dividers) in app CSS: the specs above are the contract, and they follow density on their own.
- Don't add a Save button for settings that apply at once.

### Data explorer

A searchable, filterable, sortable view of records or media, with multi-select and bulk actions. It's built from a page header, a filter bar, a table or card grid with quick actions, and a floating action bar that appears while items are selected. It also covers the loading, empty and error states.

Built from: Page header, Filter bar, Search bar, Sorting, Chip, Table, Grid, Action bar, Dropdown menu, Pagination, Skeleton, Empty state, Alert. Example: Table → "Playground" (`get_component table`, llms/table.md).

**How**
1. Header: start the screen with a PageHeader (PageHeaderTitle as the one <h1>, PageHeaderDescription, and PageHeaderActions with at most one primary create Button and optional export/view controls).
2. Controls: place a FilterBar below the header. Its FilterBarMain holds FilterBarTabs (quick status tabs with counts), a FilterBarGroup of faceted FilterBarTriggers (opening DropdownMenus with DropdownMenuSelectedItem checkboxes), a SearchBar to filter by text, and a Sorting trigger (opening a DropdownMenu of sort fields and directions). When faceted filters are active, render FilterBarActive with ChipRemovable pills and a FilterBarClear button.
3. Records: render a Table (when comparing attributes across columns) or a Grid (when browsing media assets, screenshots, social posts or cards). Include a select-all Checkbox in the header/toolbar and a selection Checkbox on each row (TableCell select) or card (GridItemSelect).
4. Item actions: put 1–2 common inline icon Buttons (Edit, Copy) and a ⋯ DropdownMenu trigger (Duplicate, Archive, Delete last as destructive) inside TableRowActions (in a trailing TableCell actions) or GridItemActions (with reveal on desktop so actions show on hover, focus-within or selection).
5. Bulk actions: mount an ActionBar (open={selected.size > 0}) with ActionBarSelection (ActionBarCount + ActionBarClose for Esc/clear) and ActionBarActions of ActionBarButtons (Edit, Duplicate, Copy, Archive, and destructive Delete last).
6. States & paging: render Skeleton rows or cards with aria-busy="true" while loading, an EmptyState (with a "Clear filters" action when filters match nothing, or a primary create action when the collection is empty), an Alert variant="destructive" with a retry Button when loading fails, and Pagination below the table.

**Phones**
- FilterBarMain and FilterBarActive wrap naturally; when a chip strip sits alone on a phone, use ChipGroup scroll so it scrolls horizontally without wrapping into a tall block.
- Table scrolls horizontally inside .ayy-table-wrap; Grid drops columns automatically down to a single column below 48rem.
- Reveal actions (.ayy-table__row-actions--reveal and .ayy-grid__actions--reveal) stay visible on touch screens (@media (hover: none)) so every item's actions remain tappable without hover.
- The floating ActionBar stays anchored at the bottom of the viewport above safe areas; keep its action labels concise.

**Specs** (don't restyle these)
- **Filter bar (.ayy-filter-bar)**: Vertical stack (--ayy-space-2 gap) with --ayy-space-3 padding, 1px --ayy-color-line border, --ayy-radius-card, --ayy-color-surface (or .ayy-filter-bar--flush inside a card). Tabs sit in a wash track; faceted triggers use --ayy-size-control-md height (--ayy-size-control-sm in sm).
- **Table row & Grid card selection**: Selected table rows (tr[aria-selected="true"]) get --ayy-color-wash-hover; selected grid cards (.ayy-grid__item[aria-selected="true"]) get a 2px --ayy-color-text border, 1px ring and 4% text tint.
- **Item actions (.ayy-table__row-actions, .ayy-grid__actions)**: Inline-flex cluster (--ayy-space-1 gap). With --reveal, opacity is 0 at rest on hover-capable devices and 1 on row/card :hover, :focus-within, [aria-selected="true"], or when a menu trigger inside has [aria-expanded="true"].
- **Action bar (.ayy-action-bar)**: Fixed bottom-center pill (--ayy-space-6 from the bottom, z-index 40), --ayy-color-surface-raised, 1px --ayy-color-line-hover border, --ayy-radius-card, --ayy-shadow-lg. Selection count pill at the start, hairline divider, action buttons (--ayy-control-pad-md) with 8px gap.

**Do**
- Use this pattern for every table, directory, asset library, inbox list or record manager in an app.
- Keep the same actions in the per-item ⋯ DropdownMenu and the bulk ActionBar so single and multi-item workflows match.
- Distinguish an empty collection (offer the create button) from an empty filter result (offer "Clear filters").

**Don't**
- Don't build custom filter rows out of raw selects or unstyled buttons — use FilterBar, SearchBar and Sorting.
- Don't place static bulk action buttons above the table that sit disabled when nothing is selected — use the floating ActionBar.
- Don't hide row or card actions with display: none on hover, which removes them from keyboard Tab order and touch screens.

### Marketing page

A public website or landing page: a sticky header, a hero, feature and pricing sections, an FAQ and a footer. Sections are divided by soft separators, and the header folds into a menu on phones.

Built from: Navbar, Button, Badge, Card, Icon tile, Frame, Segmented control, List, Accordion, Separator, Footer. Example: Navbar → "Site header" (`get_component navbar`, llms/navbar.md).

**How**
1. Top of page: start <body> with an .ayy-skip-link pointing to #main (and an empty .ayy-scroll-progress div for long reads), followed by a Navbar (NavbarBrand, NavbarNav of NavbarLinks with current on the active page, NavbarActions with a theme DropdownMenu and one small ring Button for the primary CTA, and a NavbarToggle last).
2. Hero: inside <main id="main">, open with a hero section wrapped in .ayy-bg-grid and .ayy-container: a status or announcement Badge, a heading in .ayy-display or .ayy-h1 (with .ayy-gradient-text or .ayy-accent-text on the key phrase), an .ayy-lede intro paragraph (capped at --ayy-size-measure), a cluster with one ring Button and one outline Button, and the product visual inside a Frame.
3. Sections: separate major blocks with <Separator fade /> inside .ayy-container. Give each section an .ayy-eyebrow label, an .ayy-h2 heading, and an .ayy-lede description before its content grid, and add .ayy-reveal to blocks so they fade and lift in on scroll.
4. Features & spotlights: lay out features in an .ayy-grid of Cards (interactive and spotlight when clickable, with --ayy-spot set to a distinct --ayy-accent-* token per card) holding an IconTile, CardTitle and CardDescription.
5. Pricing & FAQ: build pricing with a SegmentedControl (Monthly / Yearly) above an .ayy-grid of plan Cards (the recommended plan gets featured and a Badge; perks use a List compact with check icons). Build the FAQ with an Accordion single centered at --ayy-size-measure.
6. Footer: close the page with a Footer containing FooterBrand (logo, tagline), FooterNav of FooterGroups (Product, Docs, Company, Legal), and FooterBottom (copyright and secondary links).

**Phones**
- Below 48rem the Navbar automatically hides inline links and opens them in a surface panel below the header when NavbarToggle is pressed; NavbarBrand and NavbarActions stay visible in the bar.
- .ayy-container switches its inline gutter from 24px to 16px below 64rem, and .ayy-display scales fluidly down to 44px on phones without custom media queries.
- Feature and pricing .ayy-grid layouts collapse to a single column automatically when the viewport is narrower than two --ayy-min tracks.

**Specs** (don't restyle these)
- **Site header (.ayy-navbar)**: Sticky top 0, --ayy-size-header (72px) tall, --ayy-color-glass backdrop with 16px blur, 1px --ayy-color-hairline bottom border. Inner row centred at --ayy-size-container (1400px) with 24px gutter (16px below 64rem).
- **Hero & section typography**: Hero title uses .ayy-display (fluid 2.75rem to 12.5rem, tight leading) or .ayy-h1 (3rem). Section titles use .ayy-eyebrow (14px, muted, sentence case) above .ayy-h2 (2.25rem) and .ayy-lede (1.125rem, --ayy-color-text-soft, max-inline-size --ayy-size-measure).
- **Primary call to action (.ayy-button--ring)**: Marketing pages use the ring variant for the primary CTA in the hero and repeat it (size sm) in NavbarActions; supporting actions use outline or ghost.
- **Footer (.ayy-footer)**: 1px --ayy-color-hairline top border, --ayy-space-12 block padding, inner content at --ayy-size-container width.

**Do**
- Use this anatomy for every landing page, marketing site, documentation home or portfolio.
- Keep the chrome (Navbar, Footer, page background) monochrome and let colour come from content via --ayy-spot (--ayy-accent-*) on cards, icon tiles and section highlights.
- Include a NavbarToggle in every Navbar so phone navigation works without custom CSS.

**Don't**
- Don't use a Navbar in a signed-in product or dashboard — use AppShell with BottomNav.
- Don't tint the Navbar, Footer or page background per section.
- Don't put more than one ring CTA button in the Navbar or hero.

## Conventions

- **classPrefix**: ayy-
- **naming**: BEM: .ayy-block, .ayy-block__element, .ayy-block--modifier. Modifiers combine: class="ayy-button ayy-button--outline ayy-button--sm".
- **state**: State lives in native/ARIA attributes (disabled, :checked, aria-selected, aria-invalid, [open], :popover-open) so every framework drives it the same way.
- **theming**: No attribute = follow OS (dark or light). data-theme="dark" | "light" | "dark-contrast" | "light-gray" forces a theme on any element and its subtree (.dark/.light classes work too). See "themes" for what each one does; every theme keeps text at WCAG AA. setTheme() switches and persists; getColorScheme() says "dark" or "light".
- **density**: Controls default to compact (touch on touch-first devices). data-density="compact" | "comfortable" | "touch" on any element resizes buttons, inputs, tabs, switches, checkboxes and menu items below it.
- **branding**: A brand is one seed colour plus optional fonts and a shape. createBrand() (or `npx @danitesler/ayywi brand`, or the MCP create_brand tool) turns it into an 11-step scale (--ayy-brand-50…950, the seed itself at its nearest step) and, for dark and for light themes, a primary, primary-fg and ring taken from the scale step nearest the seed that keeps 4.5:1 text on the button and 3:1 against every surface in every theme. Fonts get ayywi's fallbacks (system fonts for body text); shape pill | round | soft | sharp (or exact radius) sets --ayy-radius-control, -card and -button. brandCss() writes it in the ayywi.brand layer for [data-brand="<name>"]; setBrand(brand) adds it to the page and sets the attribute. Components never change, only tokens.
- **direction**: All layout uses logical properties; set dir="rtl" on any ancestor and components mirror. Icons that point along the reading direction (arrows) need directional (ayy-icon--directional) to mirror too.
- **elements**: Custom elements are light DOM (no shadow root): write the same ayy- markup inside them; they add behaviour. Vue: compilerOptions.isCustomElement = (t) => t.startsWith("ayy-"); Angular: CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA.
- **highContrast**: Every stateful component has a forced-colors (Windows High Contrast) style using system colours.
- **icons**: Hugeicons is the icon library: install @hugeicons/core-free-icons (an optional peer; ayywi renders its data, so there's still no runtime dependency). React: <Icon icon={Search01Icon} />. Elsewhere: iconSvg(Search01Icon), or the SVG pasted from hugeicons.com with class="ayy-icon" and no fixed colour attributes. Icons use currentColor and 1.25em (the text size); size sm/md/lg/xl is 16/20/24/32px (--ayy-size-icon-*).

## Global attributes

- `data-theme`: "dark" | "light" | "dark-contrast" | "light-gray" — force a theme on this element and its subtree. None = follow the OS (dark or light). dark-contrast is a pure-black theme (a #000000 page, #0a0a0a cards, white text); light-gray puts white cards and panels on a grey page.
- `data-density`: "compact" | "comfortable" | "touch" — control sizes for this subtree. None = compact, or touch on touch-first devices.
- `data-brand`: A brand's name — its colours, corners and fonts for this subtree, in every theme. Needs the brand's stylesheet (@danitesler/ayywi/brands/<name>.css, or brandCss() / `npx @danitesler/ayywi brand` output); setBrand() sets both. None = ayywi's monochrome default.
- `dir`: "rtl" mirrors every component (logical properties throughout).
- `data-motion`: "reduce" — turns ayywi's animations and transitions off for this subtree, as prefers-reduced-motion does; for an app's own Reduce motion setting. None = follow the OS.
- `data-ayy-input`: "keyboard" | "pointer" on <html>, set by trackInputModality() (started by @danitesler/ayywi/elements; React apps call it once at startup). Pointer hides focus rings, except on text fields, until the next Tab or arrow key; a tooltip then opens on hover only. None = the browser's own :focus-visible.

| font.signature | `--ayy-font-signature` | Caveat, Segoe Script, cursive |  | A handwritten accent for a personal touch. Decorative only, never for interface text. |
| font.mono | `--ayy-font-mono` | ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, Noto Sans Mono, monospace |  |  |
| text.xs | `--ayy-text-xs` | 0.8125rem |  | A small size that stays the same in every density. Prefer s, which grows with density. |
| text.s | `--ayy-text-s` | 0.8125rem |  | Small interface text that follows density: badges, table text, menus, captions and group labels. · density: comfortable 0.8125rem, touch 0.875rem |
| text.sm | `--ayy-text-sm` | 0.875rem |  | Descriptions, and body text in dense interfaces. |

| text.display | `--ayy-text-display` | clamp(2.75rem, 13vw, 12.5rem) |  | A hero title that scales smoothly from phone to wide screen. CSS only; platform exports skip it. |

| ease.out-expo | `--ayy-ease-out-expo` | 0.25, 1, 0.5, 1 |  | A fast start and a long, soft landing. For things arriving or lifting, like cards. |
| ease.menu | `--ayy-ease-menu` | 0.22, 1, 0.36, 1 |  | A smooth curve for panels that open and close: menus, dialogs and popovers. |

## Themes

- `dark` — The default: near-black background, white text.
- `light` — White background, near-black text.
- `dark-contrast` (built on dark) — Pure black dark theme with higher contrast: a #000000 page, #0a0a0a cards with a step up for popovers, white text and crisp highlights. Every text colour still meets WCAG AA. Overrides of dark: `--ayy-color-bg` #000000, `--ayy-color-surface` #0a0a0a, `--ayy-color-surface-raised` #141414, `--ayy-color-text` #ffffff, `--ayy-color-muted` #939393, `--ayy-color-border` #262626, `--ayy-color-ring` #ffffff, `--ayy-color-primary` #ffffff, `--ayy-color-primary-fg` #000000, `--ayy-color-destructive` #f87171, `--ayy-color-info` #5b9dff, `--ayy-color-ai-active` #b98cff, `--ayy-color-glow` #ffffff, `--ayy-color-glass` #000000bf, `--ayy-color-overlay` #000000bf.
- `light-gray` (built on light) — Light on a grey page: white cards, panels and popovers stand out from a #ebebeb background, and text stays at full strength. More separation between surfaces than the all-white theme; every text colour still meets WCAG AA. Overrides of light: `--ayy-color-bg` #ebebeb, `--ayy-color-surface` #ffffff, `--ayy-color-muted` #636363, `--ayy-color-destructive` #991b1b, `--ayy-color-info` #1e40af, `--ayy-color-ai` #636363, `--ayy-color-glass` #ebebebc7.

## Brands

Shipped as `@danitesler/ayywi/brands/<name>.css`; make your own with `npx @danitesler/ayywi brand <#seed> --name <name>`.

- `violet` — Example brand: violet buttons, checks and focus rings, softer button and card corners. Load @danitesler/ayywi/brands/violet.css and set data-brand="violet" on any element (or setBrand("violet")). Made from: `{"name":"violet","color":"#7c3aed","radius":{"button":"10px","card":"20px"}}`

## Public custom properties

- `--ayy-spot`: The content's accent colour, inherited by everything inside (usually an --ayy-accent-* token). Set it on a card or page: it lights card spotlights, the active contents item, icon tiles, the scroll-progress bar and .ayy-accent-text.
- `--ayy-mx`: Card spotlight pointer X in px (set by React Card or @danitesler/ayywi/elements).
- `--ayy-my`: Card spotlight pointer Y in px (set by React Card or @danitesler/ayywi/elements).
- `--ayy-dot`: Badge status-dot colour override.
- `--ayy-value`: A unitless number 0–100: the Progress bar's or ring's value, a Slider's position, a chart bar's height or tick's position, a ring slice's length, a heatmap cell's shade, a funnel step's or bar-list row's length.
- `--ayy-start`: Where a chart bar starts (a waterfall's floating bar) or a ring slice begins, 0–100 of the scale or the ring (default 0).
- `--ayy-x`: A scatter dot's, chart label's, line hover strip's or ring tooltip's position along the plot, 0–100 from the inline start.
- `--ayy-count`: How many hover strips a line or area chart has (one per label), on its __hits.
- `--ayy-y`: A scatter dot's or chart label's height in the plot, 0–100 from the floor.
- `--ayy-z`: A bubble's size, 0–100 (100 = the largest; pass the share of the square root so areas stay honest).
- `--ayy-columns`: How many columns of cells a heatmap has (default 7).
- `--ayy-chart-color`: Colour of a chart bar, series, slice, legend item, heatmap, funnel, bar list or sparkline, instead of the next --ayy-chart-* token.
- `--ayy-chart-height`: Height of a chart's plot (default 12rem); the width of a donut, pie or gauge (12rem) or a radar (16rem).
- `--ayy-from`: Start of a slider range's fill, 0–100 (kept in sync by React and @danitesler/ayywi/elements).
- `--ayy-to`: End of a slider range's fill, 0–100.
- `--ayy-sidebar-w`: App shell sidebar width (default 15rem), set on the .ayy-app-shell. An __resize handle sets it in px while dragging; start the next session with the saved value.
- `--ayy-detail-w`: App shell detail pane width (default 22rem), set on the .ayy-app-shell. The detail __resize handle sets it in px.
- `--ayy-check-color`: A checkbox's colour, set on the .ayy-checkbox (a token: var(--ayy-accent-brand)…): the border when empty, the fill when checked.
- `--ayy-check-fg`: The tick on a checkbox with --ayy-check-color, when primary-fg doesn't read on that colour.
- `--ayy-progress-color`: Progress bar and ring fill colour override.
- `--ayy-swatch`: A swatch's colour, set on the .ayy-swatch (a token: var(--ayy-chart-1), var(--ayy-accent-brand)…).
- `--ayy-table-bg`: What a table sits on, which its pinned columns and sticky header paint so rows don't show through them. Default the page colour; set it on the table when it sits on another surface (var(--ayy-color-surface) in a card).
- `--ayy-table-truncate`: Widest a table's .ayy-table__truncate text gets before it ends in … (default 16rem).
- `--ayy-swipe-bg`: Background of a swipe row's content, which must hide the action trays under it. Default the page colour; set it to the surface the list sits on (var(--ayy-color-surface) in a card).
- `--ayy-gap`: Gap for .ayy-stack / .ayy-cluster / .ayy-grid / .ayy-spread / .ayy-split and the carousel track.
- `--ayy-min`: Narrowest column of .ayy-grid (default 16rem) before it drops a column; the aside width of .ayy-split (default 18rem).
- `--ayy-ratio`: A picture's shape, width ÷ height (1.6, or 1440 / 900), set on a card toast or a view Card's .ayy-card__view-media: the card follows it, within its own minimum and maximum height. Default 16 / 10.
- `--ayy-slide`: Width of each carousel slide (default min(22rem, 85%)).

## Utility classes

- `.ayy-h1`: Heading 1 style (48px, heading font).
- `.ayy-h2`: Heading 2 style (36px).
- `.ayy-h3`: Heading 3 style (28px).
- `.ayy-h4`: Heading 4 style (22px).
- `.ayy-h5`: Heading 5 style (18px).
- `.ayy-h6`: Heading 6 style (16px, semibold).
- `.ayy-lede`: Intro paragraph, 18px soft text.
- `.ayy-lead`: Intro paragraph (alias of .ayy-lede), 18px soft text.
- `.ayy-body`: Body paragraph style (14px).
- `.ayy-small`: Small text style (13px).
- `.ayy-xs`: Extra-small text style (13px).
- `.ayy-callout`: A short note set apart from the text (a tip, caveat or aside): wash background, accent bar on the inline start, 14px.
- `.ayy-muted`: Muted text colour.
- `.ayy-faint`: Soft text colour (var(--ayy-color-text-soft)).
- `.ayy-eyebrow`: Small muted label above a heading, in the same style as the app shell's group names.
- `.ayy-signature`: Handwritten accent font.
- `.ayy-mono`: Monospace font.
- `.ayy-tabular`: Tabular numbers (tabular-nums font variant).
- `.ayy-display`: Hero title: heading font at the fluid display size (44px on a phone to 200px), tight leading.
- `.ayy-text-outline`: Hollow letters stroked in the text colour. For big display words and numbers; combine with .ayy-muted to dim.
- `.ayy-accent-text`: Text in the local accent (--ayy-spot), darkened on light themes so accent tokens keep 4.5:1.
- `.ayy-gradient-text`: Text clipped to a gradient from text colour to accent/soft text.
- `.ayy-link`: Inline text link: underlined, text colour, focus ring.
- `.ayy-text-highlight`: Subtle inline text highlight with clean underline. Mark elements take this by default.
- `.ayy-code`: Inline code: monospace at 0.85em, hairline border, wash background and tight padding. For token names, file paths and shortcuts in running text.
- `.ayy-prose`: Long-form reading (articles, case studies): 18px soft text at a readable measure; styles the headings, lists, links, quotes, code and images inside.
- `.ayy-container`: Centred page width (--ayy-size-container, 1400px) with a 24px gutter, 16px on tablets and phones.
- `.ayy-grid`: Responsive grid: as many columns of at least --ayy-min (16rem) as fit; gap via --ayy-gap (16px).
- `.ayy-stack`: Vertical flex stack; gap via --ayy-gap (default 12px). Children lose their block margins (true of every layout helper), so a <p> or heading inside needs no margin reset.
- `.ayy-cluster`: Wrapping horizontal row; gap via --ayy-gap (default 8px).
- `.ayy-spread`: Wrapping row with its items pushed to both ends: a title and its meta, a label and a value, a toolbar's filters and actions. Gap via --ayy-gap (default 8px).
- `.ayy-split`: Main content (first child) and an aside (last child) side by side; the aside drops below once the main would be narrower than 60%. Aside width via --ayy-min (default 18rem). No media query, so it adapts to the box it's in.
- `.ayy-center`: Centered layout container aligning items horizontally and vertically.
- `.ayy-bleed`: Bleeds out into container gutter by negative gap margin.
- `.ayy-divider`: Hairline horizontal divider.
- `.ayy-surface`: Surface background container with default text color.
- `.ayy-glass`: Translucent frosted-glass backdrop with blur.
- `.ayy-dot-grid`: Decorative ambient dot grid pattern.
- `.ayy-glow`: Glow box shadow on featured cards or elements.
- `.ayy-sr-only`: Visually hidden, still read by screen readers.
- `.ayy-truncate`: One line, cut with an ellipsis (also inside a flex row).
- `.ayy-clamp-2`: Multi-line text clamp to 2 lines with ellipsis.
- `.ayy-clamp-3`: Multi-line text clamp to 3 lines with ellipsis.
- `.ayy-scroll`: Thin, quiet scrollbars on a scroll container.
- `.ayy-skip-link`: "Skip to content" link: hidden above the viewport until it gets keyboard focus. Make it the first thing in <body>.
- `.ayy-bg-grid`: Decorative ambient grid behind a hero or closing section, fading out towards the edges. Sets position: relative.
- `.ayy-scroll-progress`: Reading-progress bar fixed to the top of the viewport, in --ayy-spot. Put an empty aria-hidden <div> with it at the start of <body>. CSS scroll timelines only; hidden where unsupported.
- `.ayy-reveal`: Fades and lifts the element in as it scrolls into view. CSS only; off under reduced motion.

## Components by category

- **Actions** (Things people click to do something.): Button, Hover actions, Toolbar, Action bar, Dropdown menu, Command palette, Floating action button
- **Navigation** (Getting around a site and a page.): Navbar, App shell, Bottom nav, Top bar, Footer, Breadcrumb, Pagination, Steps, Table of contents, Tree
- **Forms** (Inputs, choices and their labels.): Field, Input, PIN input, Search bar, Filter bar, Sorting, Textarea, Mentions, Block editor, Inline edit, Select, Combobox, Tag input, Record picker, Transfer list, Date & time picker, Color picker, Icon picker, Checkbox, Radio, Segmented control, Chip, Color swatch, Choice card, Slider, Number field, Rating, File upload, Switch, Shortcut, Settings
- **Layout** (Containers and ways to organise content.): Page header, Showcase, Card, Tabs, Accordion, Carousel, Separator, Drag and drop
- **Overlays** (Content that floats above the page.): Dialog, Popover, Tooltip
- **Feedback** (Status, progress and messages.): Alert, Toast, Progress, Progress ring, Spinner, Skeleton, Empty state
- **Data display** (Values, people and records.): Badge, Status dot, Keyboard hint, Text highlight, Avatar, Icon, Icon tile, Stat, List, Property list, Swipe actions, Timeline, Frame, Chat, Code block, Table, Grid, Chart

## Button

Category: Actions. The control for starting an action, like saving, submitting or opening something. It comes in a few weights, from a strong primary button to quieter ones for secondary actions. Also called: button, btn, icon-button, icon-btn, cta, split-button, button-group.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-button` — Root. Alone it is the primary button.
- `.ayy-button--secondary` — Quiet filled button for secondary actions.
- `.ayy-button--outline` — Bordered, transparent. Neutral alternative to secondary.
- `.ayy-button--ghost` — No border or fill until hover. Toolbars, icon buttons.
- `.ayy-button--destructive` — Tinted red. Irreversible actions.
- `.ayy-button--link` — Looks like a text link.
- `.ayy-button--ring` — Showcase call to action: quiet fill inside a gradient ring that spins on keyboard focus and mouse hover (not after a tap). For marketing and portfolio pages; one per view.
- `.ayy-button--sm` — Small control step: --ayy-size-control-sm tall (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), --ayy-control-text-sm, --ayy-size-icon-sm (16px) icon, 6px gap.
- `.ayy-button--lg` — Large control step: --ayy-size-control-lg tall (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), --ayy-control-text-lg, --ayy-size-icon-md (20px) icon, 8px gap. Matches large App shell links.
- `.ayy-button--icon` — Square at the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), for a single 16px icon.
- `.ayy-button--icon-sm` — Square at the sm control height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), for a single 16px icon.
- `.ayy-button--icon-lg` — Square at the lg control height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), for a single 20px icon beside a large button.
- `.ayy-button--block` — Fills its container's width: a card footer, a phone form, a dialog's only action.
- `.ayy-button--start` — Icon and label sit at the inline start of a wide button, laid out like an App shell row of the same size: the icon is centred in a square as wide as the button is high, so a sm, md or lg button lines up with a sm, md or lg menu item. Use with block.
- `.ayy-button--end` — Icon and label sit at the inline end of a wide button, with the same edge spacing as --start (mirrored). Use with block. Centered is the default, no class.
- `.ayy-button-split` — Group joining a main action .ayy-button and a trailing icon .ayy-button (opening a menu) into a single split button with a shared seam.
- `.ayy-button-split--block` — Full-width split button: the main action stretches and the menu trigger stays square.

**States**
- `hover` (`:hover`)
- `pressed` (`:active`)
- `focus` (`:focus-visible`)
- `disabled` (`:disabled on <button>, aria-disabled="true" on <a>`)
- `loading` (`aria-busy="true" with an aria-hidden .ayy-spinner as the first child (React: loading)`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — Control sm step: --ayy-size-control-sm tall (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), --ayy-control-pad-sm inline padding, --ayy-control-text-sm (13/13/14px), --ayy-size-icon-sm (16px) icon, 6px gap.
- `md` (default) — Control md step: --ayy-size-control-md tall (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), --ayy-control-pad-md inline padding, --ayy-control-text-md (13/13/14px), --ayy-size-icon-sm (16px) icon, 8px gap.
- `lg` — Control lg step: --ayy-size-control-lg tall (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), --ayy-control-pad-lg inline padding, --ayy-control-text-lg (14/15/16px), --ayy-size-icon-md (20px) icon, 8px gap. Matches lg App shell links.
- `icon` — Square at the md control height (32/40/44px) with a 16px icon (needs aria-label).
- `icon-sm` — Square at the sm control height (28/32/40px) with a 16px icon.
- `icon-lg` — Square at the lg control height (36/44/48px) with a 20px icon.
- Density — Height, inline padding and label size follow data-density across all steps (sm/md/lg); icons stay fixed at 16px (sm/md) and 20px (lg).
- Width — Hugs its label. block (ayy-button--block) fills its container: a phone form, a card footer, a dialog's only action.

**React** — `import { Button, SplitButton } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Button>` renders <button>. Props: `variant` "primary" | "secondary" | "outline" | "ghost" | "destructive" | "link" | "ring"; `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "icon" | "icon-sm" | "icon-lg"; `type` Defaults to "button" (not "submit").; `block` boolean — full width (ayy-button--block).; `align` "start" | "center" | "end" — where the icon and label sit in a wide button; center is the default.; `loading` boolean — a Spinner before the label and aria-busy="true"; clicks and form submits are ignored while it's set. Stays focusable.; `tooltip` ReactNode | boolean — custom tooltip text or element; icon-only buttons show their aria-label on hover by default (pass false to disable).; `tooltipSide` "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end" — placement of the tooltip (default "top").; `...rest` All native <button> attributes.
- `<SplitButton>` renders <div role="group" class="ayy-button-split">. Props: `block` boolean — full width (ayy-button-split--block); the main action grows, the menu trigger stays square.; `...rest` All native <div> attributes.

**Accessibility**
- Icon-only buttons need aria-label and should always have a visible Tooltip on hover/focus.
- In a SplitButton, give the trailing menu trigger an explicit aria-label naming what it opens ("More deploy options").
- Use disabled on <button>; on <a> use aria-disabled="true" (the class handles both).
- Visible focus ring on :focus-visible is built in — never remove it.
- While it works, set aria-busy="true" and put an aria-hidden .ayy-spinner first inside (React: loading). Don't disable it: focus would jump away.

**Do**
- Use a button for any action the user can take: submit, open, save, delete.
- Use a SplitButton when a primary action has closely related alternatives in a DropdownMenu ("Deploy" + "Deploy to preview").
- Apply buttonClass() to an <a> when a link should look like an action.
- Always pair icon-only buttons (size="icon*", without a text label) with a Tooltip so sighted mouse and keyboard users can identify the action.
- Keep one primary button per view or section; make everything else secondary, outline or ghost.
- On a marketing or portfolio page, the one call to action can be ring instead of primary, with an outline button beside it.
- Put the icon (<Icon> or an .ayy-icon <svg>) before the label; the button sizes it (16px on sm/md, 20px on lg).

**Examples**: Variants, Sizes, With icon & icon-only, Split button, Loading with spinner, Wide button alignment, Link styled as a button, Ring call to action. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/button.md.

## Hover actions

Category: Actions. Small buttons that appear over a picture, a video or a card when someone points at it, for quick actions like copy, annotate or pin. They stay out of the way until needed, and a tooltip names each one. Also called: hover-actions, hover-action, overlay-actions, media-actions, quick-actions.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-hover-actions` — Row of hover actions. In the normal flow unless a position modifier floats it in a corner of the positioned parent.
- `.ayy-hover-actions--top-start` — Floats in the top start corner of the positioned parent.
- `.ayy-hover-actions--top-end` — Floats in the top end corner.
- `.ayy-hover-actions--bottom-start` — Floats in the bottom start corner.
- `.ayy-hover-actions--bottom-end` — Floats in the bottom end corner.
- `.ayy-hover-actions--group` — One glass bar (blurred, hairline border, pill corners) holds the buttons, which drop their own backgrounds.
- `.ayy-hover-actions--reveal` — Hidden until the element it sits directly in is hovered, has focus inside, carries data-hover or holds an open menu. Always shown on touch screens.
- `.ayy-hover-action` — Icon button at the small control size, frosted so it reads over a picture. Put an icon inside and an aria-label on it.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-hover-action:hover (pointer devices)`)
- `pressed` (`.ayy-hover-action:active`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-hover-action:focus-visible`)
- `disabled` (`:disabled on the button`)
- `revealed` (`.ayy-hover-actions--reveal inside a parent that is :hover, :focus-within, [data-hover] or :has([aria-expanded="true"])`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Buttons are --ayy-size-control-sm square: 28px compact, 32px comfortable, 40px touch. Icons stay 16px.
- Width — As wide as its buttons. Positioned rows sit 8px in from the corner of their parent.

**React** — `import { HoverActions, HoverAction } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<HoverActions>` renders <div class="ayy-hover-actions">. Props: `position` "top-start" | "top-end" | "bottom-start" | "bottom-end" — corner of the positioned parent; `group` boolean — one glass bar for all the buttons; `reveal` boolean — hidden until the parent is hovered or focused
- `<HoverAction>` renders <button class="ayy-hover-action"> inside a Tooltip. Props: `label` string (required) — accessible name and tooltip text; `hint` ReactNode — after the label in the tooltip, e.g. <Shortcut keys="Mod+C" />; `tooltip` boolean — false drops the tooltip (the label stays the accessible name). Default true; `side` "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end" — tooltip side. Default "bottom"; `children` ReactNode — the icon

**Accessibility**
- Every button needs an aria-label (React's label sets it); the icon is decorative.
- Revealed rows are still in the tab order: focusing a button shows the row, so keyboard users reach every action.
- Touch screens have no hover, so --reveal rows always show there; never hide the only way to do something behind hover.

**Do**
- Use hover actions for the few icon actions on a picture, a video frame or a media card: Copy, Annotate, Pin, Trim, and a ⋯ menu for the rest.
- Group them on one bar (group) when there are three or more in one corner; keep them separate when each corner holds one or two.
- Put a --reveal row directly inside the element whose hover should show it (the card, the picture's box).
- End a group with a ⋯ DropdownMenu for anything that doesn't earn its own button.

**Examples**: Separate, in the corners, Grouped on a glass bar. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/hover-actions.md.

## Toolbar

Category: Actions. A row or column of tools for one surface, like an editor, a canvas or a text selection. It's a single tab stop with arrow keys between the tools, and can be fixed, floating or vertical. Also called: toolbar, tool-bar, tool-rail, toolrail, tool-button, tool-btn, format-bar.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-toolbar` — Root, role="toolbar" with an aria-label ("Annotate"). A row of items with a small gap.
- `.ayy-toolbar--vertical` — A column (a side rail). Add aria-orientation="vertical" so the up and down arrows move.
- `.ayy-toolbar--floating` — A raised pill with a border and a shadow, floating over a canvas, a photo or a text selection.
- `.ayy-toolbar--scroll` — One line that scrolls sideways when the tools don't fit (phones).
- `.ayy-toolbar--sm` — Smaller buttons and icons (--ayy-size-control-sm), for a floating bar over text.
- `.ayy-toolbar__group` — Tools that belong together: role="group", with an aria-label when it has a name. With data-exclusive, <ayy-toolbar> keeps one of its aria-pressed buttons on (the current tool).
- `.ayy-toolbar__separator` — A hairline between groups: role="separator". Horizontal in a vertical toolbar.
- `.ayy-toolbar__spacer` — Takes the free space, pushing what follows to the far end (actions after tools). aria-hidden.
- `.ayy-toolbar__button` — A tool: <button type="button">. Square with only an icon (then it needs an aria-label), wider with an icon and a short label. Height follows data-density. aria-pressed for a tool that stays on, aria-expanded while its menu is open.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-toolbar__button:hover:not(:disabled) (devices that hover)`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-toolbar__button:focus-visible`)
- `disabled` (`.ayy-toolbar__button:disabled`)
- `selected` (`.ayy-toolbar__button[aria-pressed="true"]`)
- `open` (`.ayy-toolbar__button[aria-expanded="true"]`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — Buttons at the sm control height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), 16px icons.
- `md` (default) — Buttons at the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), 20px icons.
- Density — Button size follows data-density (above).
- Width — Hugs its buttons. vertical makes a column; scroll keeps one line that scrolls sideways on phones; a spacer pushes later items to the far end.

**Custom element** `<ayy-toolbar>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — 
- event `ayy-press`: { button, pressed } before a button's aria-pressed changes; preventDefault() keeps the old state.

**React** — `import { Toolbar, ToolbarButton, ToolbarGroup, ToolbarSeparator, ToolbarSpacer } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Toolbar>` renders <div role="toolbar" class="ayy-toolbar">. Props: `vertical` boolean — a column; sets aria-orientation="vertical"; `floating` boolean — a raised pill with a shadow; `scroll` boolean — one line that scrolls sideways; `size` "sm" | "md"
- `<ToolbarButton>` renders <button type="button" class="ayy-toolbar__button">. Props: `pressed` boolean — aria-pressed, for tools that stay on; omit for one-off actions; `tooltip` ReactNode | boolean — custom tooltip text or element; buttons with aria-label show their tooltip on hover by default; `tooltipSide` "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end" — placement of the tooltip (default "top")
- `<ToolbarGroup>` renders <div role="group" class="ayy-toolbar__group">. Props: 
- `<ToolbarSeparator>` renders <div role="separator" class="ayy-toolbar__separator">. Props: 
- `<ToolbarSpacer>` renders <div aria-hidden="true" class="ayy-toolbar__spacer">. Props: 

**Accessibility**
- role="toolbar" with an aria-label. Tab reaches it once (the last tool used, else the pressed one, else the first); Left/Right (Up/Down when vertical) move between tools, mirrored in RTL; Home/End jump to the ends. Disabled tools are skipped.
- Every icon-only tool needs an aria-label ("Rectangle"), and the name shouldn't change with its state — aria-pressed says whether it's on.
- Text fields and radio groups (swatches, a segmented control) inside keep their own arrow keys; the radio group is one stop.
- On is a wash tile with a hairline, not colour alone; High Contrast fills it with the system highlight.

**Do**
- Use a toolbar for the tools of one surface: an image or canvas editor, a text selection, a media viewer, a table's bulk actions.
- Put the tools that switch modes in a group where one is pressed (the current tool), then separators, then one-off actions (Undo, Redo), then a ToolbarSpacer and the labelled actions (Copy, Save).
- Use vertical for a side rail on wide screens and scroll on phones; floating over a canvas or next to a selection.
- Use PopoverTrigger asChild around an icon-only ToolbarButton with aria-label to open a subtoolbar; its label also supplies the tooltip. Give the popup Toolbar its own aria-label and use side=end beside a vertical rail.
- Put a Swatch group (size sm, track) in it for colours, and a DropdownMenu trigger (a ToolbarButton) for overflow.
- Wrap toolbar items in a Tooltip with a keyboard hint element (<Shortcut keys="..." /> in React, .ayy-shortcut in HTML) to show their action and shortcut on hover and focus.

**Examples**: Editor tools, undo and a labelled action, Floating formatting bar, Vertical rail. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/toolbar.md.

## Action bar

Category: Actions. A bar that appears at the bottom of the screen once someone selects rows or cards in a table, grid or list. It shows how many are selected and offers actions that apply to all of them, such as archive or delete. It goes away when the selection is cleared. Also called: action-bar, actionbar, bulk-actions, bulk-action-bar, selection-bar, batch-actions, multi-select-bar.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-action-bar` — Root floating pill bar, role="toolbar". Hidden until the open attribute is present, then animates in with a spring lift, and plays the same animation in reverse on exit.
- `.ayy-action-bar--fixed` — Pins the bar to the bottom center of the viewport instead of sticky inside its scroll container.
- `.ayy-action-bar__selection` — Start section grouping the selected count and the clear selection button.
- `.ayy-action-bar__count` — Tabular-numeral count of selected items (e.g. "3 selected").
- `.ayy-action-bar__close` — Icon button (×) that clears the current selection (also triggered by Escape).
- `.ayy-action-bar__separator` — Vertical hairline divider between the selection count and actions, or before destructive actions.
- `.ayy-action-bar__actions` — Scrollable group of bulk action buttons (role="group").
- `.ayy-action-bar__button` — Compact action button inside the bar, with an optional leading icon and label.
- `.ayy-action-bar__button--primary` — Primary bulk action button filled with the primary token.
- `.ayy-action-bar__button--secondary` — Secondary bulk action button with a wash fill and subtle border.
- `.ayy-action-bar__button--destructive` — Destructive bulk action button (e.g. Delete) in the destructive colour.
- `.ayy-action-bar__button--icon` — Square icon-only action button for common bulk actions (e.g. Copy, Archive, Delete).

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-action-bar__button:hover:not(:disabled), .ayy-action-bar__close:hover (devices that hover)`)
- `pressed` (`.ayy-action-bar__button:active:not(:disabled)`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-action-bar__button:focus-visible, .ayy-action-bar__close:focus-visible`)
- `disabled` (`.ayy-action-bar__button:disabled`)
- `open` (`.ayy-action-bar[open]; .ayy-action-bar__button[aria-expanded="true"]`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Buttons and the clear control follow --ayy-size-control-sm (28px compact, 32px comfortable, 40px touch) and --ayy-control-text-sm.
- Width — Hugs its buttons (fit-content) up to 100% of its container (or viewport when fixed), scrolling sideways if actions overflow on a phone.

**Custom element** `<ayy-action-bar>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — 
- event `ayy-clear`: Fired when the clear button or Escape clears the selection; call preventDefault() to keep it.

**React** — `import { ActionBar, ActionBarSelection, ActionBarCount, ActionBarClose, ActionBarSeparator, ActionBarActions, ActionBarButton } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<ActionBar>` renders <div role="toolbar" class="ayy-action-bar">. Props: `open` boolean — shows the bar with its entrance animation when true; `fixed` boolean — pins to the bottom center of the viewport; `label` string — aria-label for the toolbar (default "Bulk actions"); `onClear` () => void — called when the clear button or Escape is pressed
- `<ActionBarSelection>` renders <div class="ayy-action-bar__selection">. Props: 
- `<ActionBarCount>` renders <span class="ayy-action-bar__count">. Props: 
- `<ActionBarClose>` renders <button type="button" class="ayy-action-bar__close">. Props: `label` string — accessible label for the clear button (default "Clear selection"); `tooltip` ReactNode | boolean — custom tooltip text or element (defaults to label); `tooltipSide` "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end" — placement of the tooltip (default "top")
- `<ActionBarSeparator>` renders <div role="separator" class="ayy-action-bar__separator">. Props: 
- `<ActionBarActions>` renders <div role="group" class="ayy-action-bar__actions">. Props: 
- `<ActionBarButton>` renders <button type="button" class="ayy-action-bar__button">. Props: `variant` "default" | "primary" | "secondary" | "destructive"; `primary` boolean — shorthand for variant="primary"; `secondary` boolean — shorthand for variant="secondary"; `destructive` boolean — shorthand for variant="destructive"; `icon` boolean — square icon-only button without label padding (must provide aria-label); `open` boolean — aria-expanded when used as a DropdownMenuTrigger; `tooltip` ReactNode | boolean — custom tooltip text or element; icon buttons show their aria-label on hover by default; `tooltipSide` "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end" — placement of the tooltip (default "top")

**Accessibility**
- role="toolbar" with an aria-label ("Bulk actions"): one Tab stop, Left/Right arrow keys (mirrored in RTL) and Home/End move between the clear button and actions.
- Pressing Escape or clicking ActionBarClose clears the selection and dismisses the bar.
- Icon-only buttons inside the bar must have an aria-label (e.g. aria-label="Delete selected") and always be wrapped in a Tooltip.
- High Contrast mode borders the bar in CanvasText and highlights primary or open buttons with Highlight.

**Do**
- Use an Action bar with a selectable Table or Grid so bulk actions appear at the bottom as soon as one or more items are selected.
- Show the selected count first, followed by the clear button, a separator, and the actions with destructive Delete last.
