- When an Action bar has many actions, keep text labels for unique or context-specific actions (e.g. "Assign reviewer", "Change status") and use icon-only buttons (`icon`, `aria-label`) for universally recognized bulk actions (Duplicate, Copy link, Archive, Delete).
- Place an ActionBarSeparator between labelled buttons and icon buttons to visually divide distinct action groups.
- Always pair icon-only action buttons with a Tooltip so users can identify the action on hover and keyboard focus.
- Fold less common bulk actions into a DropdownMenu triggered from a trailing ActionBarButton.

**Examples**: Multi-select bulk actions, Many actions with icon buttons. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/action-bar.md.

## Dropdown menu

Category: Actions. A list of actions that opens from a button. It supports submenus and works fully from the keyboard. Also called: menu, dropdown, dropdown-menu, context-menu, menu-item, submenu, nested-menu, cascading-menu.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-menu` — On the element with popover and role="menu".
- `.ayy-menu--sub` — Submenu flyout panel.
- `.ayy-menu--static` — Static menu rendered inline in a page or window without popover behavior.
- `.ayy-menu__item` — Each action: a <button role="menuitem">.
- `.ayy-menu__row` — Split row: a wrapper holding a normal item and a __more button side by side, so the item runs its action and the button opens a menu for it.
- `.ayy-menu__more` — Square icon button at the end of a __row that opens the row's menu (role="menuitem", aria-haspopup="menu"; put its panel next to the row).
- `.ayy-menu__item--destructive` — Red item for destructive actions.
- `.ayy-menu__item--selected` — Selectable menu item with checkmark indicator.
- `.ayy-menu__item--sub` — Submenu parent row with an inline-end chevron.
- `.ayy-menu__item--expand` — Inline accordion row that expands its items below itself.
- `.ayy-menu__item--described` — Two-line row with an aligned label and soft description.
- `.ayy-menu__item-text` — Text container for a described row's label and description.
- `.ayy-menu__description` — Soft description text under a described row's label.
- `.ayy-menu__value` — Muted text or badge before the chevron or shortcut.
- `.ayy-menu__chevron` — Chevron icon pointing towards the inline end or down when expandable.
- `.ayy-menu__group--inline` — Indented role="group" of items revealed by an expandable row.
- `.ayy-menu__shortcut` — Keyboard shortcut keys at the end of an item, as keycaps (an .ayy-shortcut of .ayy-kbd, adapted to the device).
- `.ayy-menu__label` — Small muted group label, in the same style as the app shell's group names.
- `.ayy-menu__separator` — Divider (role="separator").

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-menu__item:hover, .ayy-menu__more:hover`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-menu__item:focus (arrow keys) / :focus-visible`)
- `disabled` (`.ayy-menu__item:disabled or [aria-disabled="true"]`)
- `selected` (`.ayy-menu__item[aria-checked="true"], .ayy-menu__item[aria-selected="true"], or .ayy-menu__item--selected`)
- `open` (`:popover-open or [aria-expanded="true"] on a parent row or split row's __more`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Items are the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch) with control md text.
- Width — At least 11rem, at most 20rem (or the viewport minus 1rem); grows with its longest item.

**Custom element** `<ayy-menu>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — A trigger <button> and a [popover] element with role="menu" containing .ayy-menu__item buttons, optional submenu panels, split rows (.ayy-menu__row with a .ayy-menu__more button) and expandable groups.
- attribute `side`: bottom | top | start | end
- attribute `align`: start | center | end
- attribute `open`: Two-way open state
- event `ayy-select`: { value: string, item: HTMLElement } — value is the item's data-value, else its text
- event `ayy-open-change`: { open: boolean }
- event `ayy-submenu-layout`: { open: boolean, width: number, height: number, side: FloatingSide }

**React** — `import { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuTrigger, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuRow, DropdownMenuMore, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuSubContent, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuSelectedItem, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, DropdownMenuRadioItem } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<DropdownMenu>` renders nothing (state provider). Props: `open / defaultOpen` boolean; `onOpenChange` (open: boolean) => void; `anchorPoint` { x: number; y: number }; `boundary` Element | Rect
- `<DropdownMenuTrigger>` renders Button. Props: `...ButtonProps` variant, size…; `asChild` boolean — clone custom trigger element without button styling
- `<DropdownMenuContent>` renders <div popover role="menu">. Props: `side` "bottom" | "top" | "start" | "end"; `align` "start" | "center" | "end"; `static` boolean; `boundary` Element | Rect; `subSide` "end" | "start"; `onSubmenuLayout` (layout) => void
- `<DropdownMenuRow>` renders <div role="presentation" class="ayy-menu__row">. Props: `children` A DropdownMenuItem and, beside it, a DropdownMenuMore inside a DropdownMenuSub
- `<DropdownMenuMore>` renders <button type="button" role="menuitem" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded>. Props: `icon` ReactNode — the button's icon (e.g. MoreHorizontal).; `aria-label` Required: name the row it belongs to, e.g. "More options for Duplicate project".
- `<DropdownMenuItem>` renders <button role="menuitem">. Props: `onSelect` () => void — runs when chosen; the menu then closes unless closeOnSelect=false; `destructive` boolean; `selected` boolean — reserves space on inline start for checkmark indicator; `shortcut` string — shortcut keys like "Mod+D" (shown as keycaps, ⌘D on a Mac, Ctrl+D elsewhere); `value` ReactNode; `description` ReactNode; `icon` ReactNode; `closeOnSelect` boolean
- `<DropdownMenuLabel>` renders <div role="presentation">.
- `<DropdownMenuSeparator>` renders <div role="separator">.
- `<DropdownMenuSub>` renders nothing (submenu state provider). Props: `open / defaultOpen` boolean; `onOpenChange` (open: boolean) => void; `inline` boolean
- `<DropdownMenuSubTrigger>` renders <button role="menuitem" aria-haspopup="menu">. Props: `icon` ReactNode; `value` ReactNode; `description` ReactNode; `selected` boolean — reserves space on inline start for checkmark indicator
- `<DropdownMenuSubContent>` renders <div popover role="menu"> or <div role="group"> (inline). Props: `side` "end" | "start"; `align` "start"
- `<DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>` renders <button role="menuitemcheckbox">. Props: `checked` boolean; `onCheckedChange` (checked: boolean) => void; `closeOnSelect` boolean
- `<DropdownMenuSelectedItem>` renders <button role="menuitemcheckbox">. Props: `selected` boolean; `onSelectedChange` (selected: boolean) => void; `closeOnSelect` boolean
- `<DropdownMenuRadioGroup>` renders <div role="group">. Props: `value` string; `onValueChange` (value: string) => void; `closeOnSelect` boolean
- `<DropdownMenuRadioItem>` renders <button role="menuitemradio">. Props: `value` string

**Accessibility**
- Opening moves focus to the first item; arrows move, Home/End jump, letters jump to matching items.
- ArrowRight / ArrowLeft open and close submenus (mirrored in RTL); Esc inside a submenu closes only that panel.
- Esc or Tab closes the menu and focus returns to the trigger.
- Icon-only triggers (⋯) need aria-label.
- A split row is two menu items: the action and its trailing More button, which arrows reach like any other item. Label the button with its row ("More options for Duplicate project"), not just "More".

**Do**
- Use a menu for an item's secondary actions (rename, duplicate, delete) and for overflow “⋯” menus in toolbars and table rows.
- Show an item's shortcut with shortcut="Mod+…" so Mac and Windows users each see their own keys as keycaps.
- Nest one level at most, for variants of one action. Don't hide frequent actions in a submenu.
- Use a split row (DropdownMenuRow with DropdownMenuMore) when one item has a second, related set of choices: the row runs the action, its ⋯ opens on click (not hover) with variants like "Duplicate as template".
- Put destructive actions last, after a separator.
- Keep item labels to a verb + noun: "Rename project".

**Examples**: Item actions. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/menu.md.

## Command palette

Category: Actions. A search box above a list of actions and places, so people can find and run things from the keyboard. It can sit inline on a page or in a popover, or open as a dialog from a shortcut. Also called: command, command-palette, command-menu, quick-switcher, quick-open.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-command` — Root: a card with the search field, the list and an optional footer. On a <div> inline, or with ayy-dialog on a <dialog> for the ⌘K palette (top-aligned, no padding).
- `.ayy-command__search` — The row with the magnifier icon and the input, over a hairline. A ring under it while the input has keyboard focus.
- `.ayy-command__input` — <input type="search" role="combobox" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="<list id>" aria-autocomplete="list" aria-label>. Keeps focus; aria-activedescendant points at the highlighted item.
- `.ayy-command__list` — role="listbox" with an id and aria-label; scrolls when long.
- `.ayy-command__group` — role="group" aria-labelledby its label. Hidden when none of its items match.
- `.ayy-command__label` — A group's name ("Go to"), muted, role="presentation" with an id.
- `.ayy-command__item` — role="option" with an id: an icon, the text, then a __meta. aria-selected="true" on the highlighted one; data-value is what it runs, data-keywords more words that find it.
- `.ayy-command__content` — Vertical stack for an item's title and optional description.
- `.ayy-command__title` — The primary label of an item.
- `.ayy-command__description` — One-line muted summary under the title, truncated with ellipsis.
- `.ayy-command__meta` — At an item's end: a .ayy-shortcut, a list name or a count, muted.
- `.ayy-command__empty` — "No results", shown only when nothing matches (hidden otherwise).
- `.ayy-command__footer` — Under the list after a hairline: key hints (↑↓ to move, ↵ to run) or a link.

**States**
- `focus` (`.ayy-command__search:has(> .ayy-command__input:focus-visible)`)
- `disabled` (`.ayy-command__item[aria-disabled="true"]`)
- `selected` (`.ayy-command__item[aria-selected="true"]`)
- `empty` (`.ayy-command__empty shown`)
- `filtered` (`.ayy-command__item[hidden], .ayy-command__group[hidden]`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Items are the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch); the field is the lg height.
- Width — Inline it fills its container. As a dialog (ayy-dialog ayy-command) it's 36rem wide, at most the viewport less 2rem, near the top of the screen; the list scrolls past 24rem.

**Custom element** `<ayy-command>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — 
- attribute `shortcut`: Opens and closes the dialog palette from anywhere. Default "Mod+K" (⌘K, Ctrl+K); "" for none.
- attribute `manual`: Don't filter: you change the items yourself on "input" (a search API), then call refresh().
- event `ayy-select`: { value, item } when an item runs: its data-value and the element.

**React** — `import { Command, CommandDialog, CommandGroup, CommandItem } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Command>` renders <div class="ayy-command"> search field, <div role="listbox" class="ayy-command__list">{children}</div>, footer. Props: `label` string — the field's and list's accessible name. Default "Search commands"; `placeholder` string — default "Type a command or search…"; `emptyText` ReactNode — when nothing matches. Default "No results"; `footer` ReactNode — key hints under the list; `filter` boolean — filter by the typed text. Default true; `onSearchChange` (text: string) => void — every keystroke (fetch results here with filter={false}); `onRun` (value?: string) => void — after an item runs, with its value; `inputProps` InputHTMLAttributes — more props for the <input>
- `<CommandDialog>` renders <dialog class="ayy-dialog ayy-command" aria-label> with the same parts; closes when an item runs. Props: `open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange` Like Dialog; `shortcut` string | null — toggles it from anywhere. Default "Mod+K"; `label / placeholder / emptyText / footer / filter / onSearchChange / onRun / inputProps` As on Command; `className` string — on the <dialog>
- `<CommandGroup>` renders <div class="ayy-command__group" role="group"> with an .ayy-command__label. Props: `heading` ReactNode — the group's name
- `<CommandItem>` renders <div class="ayy-command__item" role="option" data-value data-keywords data-title data-description>. Props: `onSelect` () => void — runs on Enter or a click; `value` string — passed to onRun; `keywords` string — more words that find it; `description` ReactNode — optional one-line summary under the title; `icon` ReactNode — an Icon before the text; `shortcut` string — its shortcut at the end ("Mod+N"); `meta` ReactNode — other text at the end: a count, a list name; `disabled` boolean — dimmed, skipped by the arrows

**Accessibility**
- The WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a listbox that is always shown: focus stays in the input, aria-activedescendant names the highlighted item, and the first match is highlighted as you type.
- Up/Down move (wrapping), PageUp/PageDown move five, Enter runs the highlighted item, Esc clears the field and a second Esc closes the dialog.
- Groups are role="group" named by their heading, so screen readers say "Go to" when the highlight enters one.
- Shortcuts in items are read as words ("Command N"); icons are hidden.
- The dialog palette is a modal <dialog> named by aria-label; focus goes to the input when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes.

**Do**
- Offer one in any app with more than a handful of screens or actions, on ⌘K / Ctrl+K, and show the shortcut on a Search button so people find it.
- Group items by what they do (Create, Go to, Appearance) and keep labels verb-first ("New task", "Switch theme").
- Add keywords for the words people might type instead ("preferences" for Settings).
- Show each item's own shortcut at its end so the palette teaches them.
- Use TextHighlight (<TextHighlight> in React, <mark class="ayy-text-highlight"> in HTML) to highlight matching terms in titles and descriptions.
- Show descriptions conditionally when matches occur in item descriptions, or keep descriptions always visible for items that need extra context.

**Examples**: Inline palette with groups and shortcuts, ⌘K dialog, Search with text highlight and descriptions. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/command.md.

## Floating action button

Category: Actions. A round floating button for the main action of a phone screen, like composing or adding something. It stays in the corner over the content and can show a label when extended. Also called: fab, floating-action, floating-button, float-button.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-fab` — A <button> (or <a>) with an icon and an aria-label: primary fill, a lifted shadow, size from data-density. position: fixed at the bottom inline-end corner. In an .ayy-app-shell, place it after __main and before the bottom nav.
- `.ayy-fab--extended` — Icon and a visible label: a wider pill ("Compose"). Needs no aria-label.
- `.ayy-fab--secondary` — A raised surface with a border instead of the primary fill: less emphasis.
- `.ayy-fab--sm` — Smaller (the control-lg size), for a second action stacked above the main one.
- `.ayy-fab--inline` — Not floating: in the flow, placed by its container (an empty state, a toolbar, a docs page).

**States**
- `hover` (`:hover (devices that hover)`)
- `pressed` (`:active`)
- `focus` (`:focus-visible`)
- `disabled` (`:disabled or [aria-disabled="true"]`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — The lg control height: 40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch. A second action stacked above the main one.
- `md` (default) — The lg control height plus 12px: 52px compact, 60 comfortable, 64 touch.
- Density — Its diameter follows data-density through the lg control height (the sizes above).
- Width — Square, a circle. extended (ayy-fab--extended) hugs its icon and label as a pill. Takes no room: it floats over the content (inline puts it back in the flow).

**React** — `import { Fab } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Fab>` renders <button type="button" class="ayy-fab">, or <a> with href. Props: `variant` "primary" | "secondary"; `size` "sm" | "md"; `extended` boolean — icon and a label; otherwise give it aria-label; `inline` boolean — not floating; `href` string — renders an <a>; `type` "button" | "submit" | "reset" — default "button"

**Accessibility**
- An icon-only FAB needs an aria-label that says the action ("New task"), not the icon ("Plus").
- Put it after the main content in the DOM so it comes after what it acts on in the tab order, not before the page.
- It must not cover content for good: the App shell keeps it out of the bottom nav, and lists need room at their end (padding-block-end of the FAB's height) so the last row can scroll clear of it.

**Do**
- Use one FAB for the screen's main, constructive action: create, compose, scan, add.
- Use extended when the action isn't obvious from an icon, or on the first screens of an app.
- Hide it on screens where the main action is already on screen (a form's Save) or while a sheet is open.

**Examples**: Icon, extended, secondary, small, In an app shell, above the bottom nav. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/fab.md.

## Navbar

Category: Navigation. The header at the top of a website, with the brand on one side and links and actions on the other. It stays in view as the page scrolls, and on phones the links fold into a menu. Also called: navbar, site-header, nav-bar, header-nav.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-navbar` — Root, usually a <header>. Sticky, 72px tall (--ayy-size-header), glass background with a hairline under it. Anchor jumps land below it.
- `.ayy-navbar__inner` — Centred row at page width (--ayy-size-container) with the page gutter.
- `.ayy-navbar__brand` — Logo / name link at the start.
- `.ayy-navbar__nav` — <nav> of links. It and everything after it sit at the end. Without a __toggle it scrolls sideways if the links don't fit; with one, below 48rem it becomes a panel under the bar, shown while the toggle has aria-expanded="true".
- `.ayy-navbar__link` — Top-level link. Hover adds a wash; aria-current="page" marks the page you're on with a stronger tint (High Contrast: the system highlight).
- `.ayy-navbar__actions` — Group of buttons (a theme menu, the call to action). Next to the brand, or at the end after the nav. Stays in the bar on phones, so keep it to one or two items.
- `.ayy-navbar__toggle` — The phone menu button, last in the inner row (combine with ayy-button ayy-button--ghost ayy-button--icon and a menu icon). Hidden from 48rem. Its aria-expanded is the menu's state; connectNavbar() / <ayy-navbar> / React Navbar manage it.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-navbar__link:hover`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-navbar__link:focus-visible, .ayy-navbar__brand:focus-visible`)
- `selected` (`.ayy-navbar__link[aria-current="page"]`)
- `open` (`.ayy-navbar__toggle[aria-expanded="true"] (below 48rem)`)

**Sizes**
- Density — The bar is --ayy-size-header (4.5rem) tall at every density; links are the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), lg in the phone panel.
- Width — Full width; content centred at --ayy-size-container with a 24px gutter (16px below 64rem). Below 48rem, with a __toggle, the links fold into a panel.

**Custom element** `<ayy-navbar>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — A <header class="ayy-navbar"> with a __toggle. The toggle opens and closes the links as a panel under the bar on phones; Esc, a click outside, a link in the panel or widening past 48rem close it. Without a toggle it does nothing.


**React** — `import { Navbar, NavbarBrand, NavbarNav, NavbarLink, NavbarActions, NavbarToggle } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Navbar>` renders <header class="ayy-navbar"><div class="ayy-navbar__inner">; wires the phone menu when it holds a NavbarToggle.
- `<NavbarBrand>` renders <a>.
- `<NavbarNav>` renders <nav>. Props: `aria-label` Defaults to "Main" (translate it).
- `<NavbarLink>` renders <a>. Props: `current` boolean — sets aria-current="page".
- `<NavbarActions>` renders <div>.
- `<NavbarToggle>` renders <button class="ayy-button ayy-button--ghost ayy-button--icon ayy-navbar__toggle"> with a menu icon. Props: `aria-label` Defaults to "Menu" (translate it).; `children` Replaces the default menu icon.

**Accessibility**
- Use <header> for the bar and <nav aria-label="Main"> for the links; one main nav per page.
- Mark the current page with aria-current="page", not only with colour.
- Put a .ayy-skip-link before the navbar so keyboard users can jump past it.
- The menu button is a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the nav (set for you). Focus stays on it when the panel opens; Tab moves into the links, Esc closes the panel and returns focus to the button.
- The closed panel is display: none, so its links are out of the tab order until it opens.

**Do**
- Use a navbar as the top bar of a website: logo, two to five top-level links, one call to action.
- Keep one call to action in the actions group (a ring button for marketing pages, size sm).
- Add a NavbarToggle (last) once the links don't fit a phone: they fold into a panel under the bar, and the brand and call to action stay visible.
- Put the theme switch (a DropdownMenu of themes that calls setTheme()) in the actions group.

**Examples**: Site header, Menu on phones. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/navbar.md.

## App shell

Category: Navigation. The frame around a web app: a sidebar for navigation next to a main area where the content lives. On phones the sidebar turns into a bottom tab bar or a drawer. The same frame also holds settings screens. Also called: app-shell, sidebar, side-nav, sidenav, nav-item, sidebar-item, nav-list.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-app-shell` — Root. A viewport-high (100dvh) grid: sidebar column (15rem) and a main column. Neither column grows the page; each scrolls on its own. Sets position: relative (the drawer and its scrim are placed inside it). To embed the shell in a box with a fixed height, set block-size: 100% on it. Below 48rem its phone layout follows its children: a .ayy-bottom-nav child shows as the tab bar and the sidebar hides; a __bar makes the sidebar a drawer; with neither, the sidebar becomes a sideways row.
- `.ayy-app-shell__sidebar` — The <aside>: surface background, hairline on its inline-end edge, brand at the top, nav below, footer pinned to the bottom. Scrolls vertically when its content is taller than the viewport. On phones it's hidden (bottom-nav layout) or a drawer, and keeps its full tree either way.
- `.ayy-app-shell__brand` — The logo link at the top of the sidebar: a mark (a direct-child svg, img or avatar) with the product name beside it, or with a __logotype. The mark takes the icon box of the size step, so its centre is on the same axis as the link icons, expanded and in the rail. A brand with no mark shows nothing in the rail.
- `.ayy-app-shell__logotype` — Modifier for a wide wordmark inside the __brand (an img, svg or text span) that only shows while the sidebar is open: in the rail it fades out and the mark stays. Without it an img or svg in the brand is taken for the mark.
- `.ayy-app-shell__nav` — <nav> holding the links, stacked vertically (side by side in the phone row).
- `.ayy-app-shell__link` — Destination link. aria-current="page" marks the page you're on: it gets a tint and a heavier weight.
- `.ayy-app-shell__row` — A row with its own menu, on the <li>: the __link keeps the row and a __more button sits at its end. The button is a sibling of the link, never inside it.
- `.ayy-app-shell__more` — Square icon button at the end of a __row that opens the link's menu (⋯). Give it an aria-label naming the row ("Project options"); it shows on hover and focus, always on touch screens, and hides in the rail.
- `.ayy-app-shell__group` — A headed section of the nav: a __group-label over a __list. Groups after the first get a hairline above them.
- `.ayy-app-shell__group-label` — The group's heading: a small muted <p>. Give it an id and point the list's aria-labelledby at it.
- `.ayy-app-shell__group--collapsible` — Makes a group optional to collapse: the group is a <details> and its label a <summary class="ayy-app-shell__group-label"> (give it an id; the list's aria-labelledby points at it). A chevron follows the label on hover and focus, and stays while the group is closed (always on touch screens). Add `open` to start open, and open it when it holds the current page. In the rail a closed group's links stay hidden.
- `.ayy-app-shell__link--action` — An action row such as "New": the link's icon sits in a filled circle (a spread shadow, so it stays in the icon column).
- `.ayy-app-shell__list` — The <ul> of a group. Each <li> holds a link, a link followed by a __sublist, or a __collapse.
- `.ayy-app-shell__sublist` — A nested <ul> of child links, indented along a guide line. One level only. Follows a parent link, or sits inside a __collapse. Give it an aria-label when it follows a link.
- `.ayy-app-shell__collapse` — A native <details> for a group of child links that opens and closes. Its <summary class="ayy-app-shell__link"> is the toggle, with a chevron at the inline end; put the links in a __sublist inside it. Add `open` when it holds the current page.
- `.ayy-app-shell__link--sub` — Modifier for a child link inside a __sublist: a smaller control and a lighter weight.
- `.ayy-app-shell__footer` — Pinned to the bottom of the sidebar (the end of the row on phones): settings, account, help link. Keep it short.
- `.ayy-app-shell__main` — The <main> content column. Scrolls on its own and has the page gutter. In a settings dialog it's a <div>: the page behind already has the one <main>.
- `.ayy-app-shell__bar` — Phone top bar, first child of the shell, hidden from 48rem: the brand, then one or two actions (search, account), which sit at the inline end. Add a __toggle to it when the sidebar should open as a drawer. With a bar or a bottom nav the phone sidebar is off-screen; it slides in from the inline-start edge over a scrim while a toggle has aria-expanded="true".
- `.ayy-app-shell--settings` — Settings mode, on the root of a shell inside a <dialog class="ayy-dialog ayy-dialog--full">, which it fills; the dialog's close button is the way out. The sidebar holds an __title and a nav of settings sections (groups of links, one aria-current="page"); the main holds the open section, starting with a Top bar whose title names it and whose back button shows on phones only; the section's content sits in a column of --ayy-size-measure, centred. On wide screens the top is roomy: "Settings" and the section title, both xl, sit on one line with space above them, and the section's Top bar has no divider. No __bar and no bottom nav. (On a page of its own instead of a dialog, start the sidebar with an __back.) Below 48rem: with no section link current the sidebar is the whole screen (a large title and rows with chevrons) and the main is hidden; with one current, the main is the screen and the sidebar is hidden.
- `.ayy-app-shell__back` — Only for a settings shell on a page of its own (in a dialog, the close button is the way out). First in the sidebar: an <a href> back to the page settings were opened from (or a <button>), with a directional arrow icon and "Back to <app name>". In settings mode, Esc follows it.
- `.ayy-app-shell__head` — The sidebar's top row for a collapsible sidebar: the __brand first, then any actions, and the __toggle, which is placed over the inline end of the row. In the rail the row is one icon wide: the brand's mark shows, and resting the pointer on it (or focusing the toggle) swaps it for the toggle, which expands the sidebar. A brand with no mark leaves the toggle showing. Mark and toggle icon sit on the same axis as the link icons. A Tooltip around the toggle takes its place at the end of the row.
- `.ayy-app-shell__title` — A settings sidebar's heading, an <h2> "Settings" that names the dialog (aria-labelledby). Large on the phone's section list.
- `.ayy-app-shell__toggle` — The button that opens the sidebar as a drawer on phones: in the __bar (with ayy-button ayy-button--ghost ayy-button--icon and a menu icon), or as the "More" tab of the bottom nav (<button class="ayy-bottom-nav__link ayy-app-shell__toggle">). Its aria-expanded is the drawer's state. In the sidebar (last in an __head, with a directional sidebar icon) it is a row-sized square at the inline end that collapses and expands the sidebar on wide screens, and its aria-expanded is whether the sidebar is open. There it shows a tooltip naming the action (Collapse / Expand) on hover and focus. connectAppShell() / <ayy-app-shell> / React AppShell manage it.
- `.ayy-app-shell--collapsed` — Collapsed sidebar mode on wide screens: the sidebar narrows to an icon rail, animating its width with the main column. Rows stay on one line and in place, so icons keep their spot while labels and group labels fade and clip (wrap a link's label in a <span> to fade it); links without an icon fade out and leave the tab order; sub-lists hide. The toggle's aria-expanded reflects the state.
- `.ayy-app-shell--hover-preview` — With --collapsed: resting the pointer on the rail (after a short pause) or moving keyboard focus into it widens the sidebar to full width over the main area with the overlay shadow, without moving the main content; it closes a moment after the pointer leaves, unless a menu or popover inside it (an account or settings menu) is open: then it stays open until that closes. A mouse click inside doesn't keep it open. Right after the sidebar's toggle collapses it, connectAppShell sets data-ayy-hold on the sidebar so it doesn't reopen under the pointer, until the pointer leaves or focus moves on.
- `.ayy-app-shell--drawer` — Root modifier: below 48rem the sidebar is a drawer even with no __bar and no bottom nav (instead of the sideways row), and the __toggle may sit in the main area, in an app's own top bar. Wide screens are unchanged.
- `.ayy-app-shell__detail` — A third column at the inline end (an <aside>), for what's picked in the main area: a task, a message. Surface background, hairline on its inline-start edge, scrolls on its own, --ayy-detail-w wide (22rem). Show and hide it with the hidden attribute: hidden, the shell is two columns again. Below 48rem it covers the screen, so start it with a Top bar and a back button.
- `.ayy-app-shell__resize` — A drag handle on the sidebar's inline-end edge, a direct child of the shell with role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical" tabindex="0" (added for you). Dragging, the arrow keys (Shift for big steps), Home and End set --ayy-sidebar-w on the shell; a double click resets it. Limits come from aria-valuemin / aria-valuemax in px (default 192 and 384), and the main area always keeps 320px. Hidden below 48rem and while the sidebar is collapsed.
- `.ayy-app-shell__resize--detail` — Modifier: the handle for the detail pane's inline-start edge, setting --ayy-detail-w (limits default 288 and 640). Shown only while the detail pane is.
- `.ayy-app-shell--resizing` — Set by connectAppShell while a handle is being dragged: columns follow the pointer without animating. Don't set it yourself.
- `.ayy-app-shell--md` — Medium size: 32px compact rows with 16px icons, 8px from the row edge to the icon.
- `.ayy-app-shell--sm` — Small size, for long navigation such as a docs tree: sm-height links with no gap between them, regular weight, sm icons and the control radius. Big (lg, no modifier) is the default for apps.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-app-shell__link:hover; a row's .ayy-app-shell__more:hover; on a collapsed shell with hover preview, .ayy-app-shell__sidebar:hover expands the sidebar as an overlay`)
- `focus` (`links, brand, a row's __more, sidebar and main :focus-visible`)
- `selected` (`.ayy-app-shell__link[aria-current="page"]`)
- `open` (`__toggle[aria-expanded="true"] (below 48rem, with a __bar or a Bottom nav); <details open> for a collapse; a row's __more[aria-expanded="true"]`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — Small: links at the sm control height (28px compact), sub-links sm, no gap between rows, regular weight, 16px icons (6px from the row edge), the control radius.
- `md` — Medium: links at the md control height (32px compact), sub-links sm, 16px icons.
- `lg` (default) — Big (default): links at the lg control height (40px compact), sub-links md, --ayy-space-0-5 between rows, medium weight, 20px icons (10px from the row edge), pill radius.
- Density — Big links are at least the lg control height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch) with lg control text, Medium ones md (32, 40, 44) with md control text, Small ones sm (28, 32, 40) with sm control text; sub-links one step down. Grows with data-density. Links, sidebar buttons, the logo row and the toggle share one row height, and every icon sits centred in a square that wide at the start of the row, so icons, the brand's mark and the toggle's icon line up in a column, in the full sidebar and in the rail alike. The sub-list's guide line runs down that column too. A row's __more button is the sm control size (28, 32, 40) with a 16px icon, so it fits inside the row at every size.
- Width — Fills the viewport (100dvh) or its box (block-size: 100%). Wide screens: 15rem sidebar or collapsed icon rail. Below 48rem: a top __bar, a Bottom nav and a drawer, or one scrolling row when it holds neither.

**Custom element** `<ayy-app-shell>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — A <div class="ayy-app-shell">. Wires the phone drawer when the shell has a __toggle in its __bar or its .ayy-bottom-nav: the toggle opens and closes the sidebar; Esc, the scrim, a link in the drawer or widening past 48rem close it. On wide screens, wires sidebar collapsing and optional hover-preview. On a settings shell, Esc follows the __back. A __row with a __more button is an ordinary button after the link: wire its menu with <ayy-menu>. A sidebar toggle's data-ayy-label-expanded / data-ayy-label-collapsed, also on its .ayy-tooltip__content, keep its label and tooltip text on the action it now performs.
- attribute `size`: lg | md | sm — Big (default), Medium (sets ayy-app-shell--md) or Small (sets ayy-app-shell--sm).
- attribute `collapsed`: boolean — collapse the sidebar to an icon rail on wide screens (sets ayy-app-shell--collapsed).
- attribute `hover-preview`: On by default: when collapsed, hovering or focusing the sidebar expands it as an overlay preview (sets ayy-app-shell--hover-preview). hover-preview="false" keeps the icon rail until the toggle opens it.
- event `ayy-collapse-change`: { collapsed: boolean } — fired when the sidebar is collapsed or expanded via a toggle button or the collapsed property.
- event `ayy-resize`: { edge: "sidebar" | "detail", width: number | null } — fired when a resize handle's drag or key press ends; width in px, null when reset to the default.

**React** — `import { AppShell, AppShellBack, AppShellTitle, AppShellHead, AppShellBar, AppShellToggle, AppShellSidebar, AppShellBrand, AppShellNav, AppShellLink, AppShellGroup, AppShellItem, AppShellMore, AppShellSublist, AppShellCollapse, AppShellFooter, AppShellMain, AppShellDetail, AppShellResize } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<AppShell>` renders <div class="ayy-app-shell">; wires the phone drawer when it holds an AppShellToggle (in the AppShellBar) or a BottomNavButton with className="ayy-app-shell__toggle". Props: `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg" — Big (lg, default, for apps), Medium (md) or Small (sm, for long navigation such as a docs tree).; `settings` boolean — settings mode (ayy-app-shell--settings), inside <DialogContent size="full">: the sidebar holds AppShellTitle and the sections.; `collapsed` boolean — collapse the sidebar to an icon rail on wide screens (ayy-app-shell--collapsed).; `hoverPreview` boolean, default true — when collapsed, hovering or focusing the sidebar expands it as an overlay preview (ayy-app-shell--hover-preview). false keeps the icon rail until the toggle opens it.; `onCollapseChange` (collapsed: boolean) => void — called when the sidebar is collapsed or expanded via a toggle button.; `drawer` boolean — below 48rem the sidebar is a drawer even without an AppShellBar or a BottomNav; the AppShellToggle may sit in the main area (ayy-app-shell--drawer).; `onResize` (edge: "sidebar" | "detail", width: number | null) => void — a resize ended (drag or key); width in px, null when reset. Save it and start the next session with style={{ "--ayy-sidebar-w": `${width}px` }}.
- `<AppShellBack>` renders <a class="ayy-app-shell__back" href> with a directional arrow and the children in a <span>; a <button type="button"> without href. Props: `href` string — where leaving settings goes. Without it, pass onClick.; `children` "Back to <app name>" (translate it).
- `<AppShellHead>` renders <div class="ayy-app-shell__head">. Props: `children` The AppShellBrand (a mark, then a name or an element with className="ayy-app-shell__logotype"), then an AppShellToggle (the collapse toggle, a sidebar icon).
- `<AppShellTitle>` renders <h2 class="ayy-app-shell__title">. Props: `children` "Settings". Give it an id and point the DialogContent's aria-labelledby at it.
- `<AppShellSidebar>` renders <aside class="ayy-app-shell__sidebar">.
- `<AppShellBrand>` renders <a class="ayy-app-shell__brand">. Props: `children` A mark (an Icon, img, svg or Avatar) and the name in a <span>, or a mark and a className="ayy-app-shell__logotype" element.
- `<AppShellNav>` renders <nav class="ayy-app-shell__nav">. Props: `aria-label` Defaults to "Main" (translate it).
- `<AppShellLink>` renders <a class="ayy-app-shell__link">. Props: `current` boolean — sets aria-current="page".; `sub` boolean — a child link (ayy-app-shell__link--sub).
- `<AppShellGroup>` renders <div class="ayy-app-shell__group"> (a <details> with collapsible) with a label <p> and a <ul>. Props: `label` The heading. Names the list.; `collapsible` boolean — renders a <details> with the label as its <summary> (ayy-app-shell__group--collapsible); a chevron shows on hover.; `defaultOpen` boolean — with collapsible, whether it starts open. Default true.
- `<AppShellItem>` renders <li>.
- `<AppShellMore>` renders <button type="button" class="ayy-app-shell__more">. Props: `aria-label` Required: name the row it belongs to, e.g. "Project options".; `children` The icon (e.g. a MoreHorizontal Icon).; `className` Add ayy-app-shell__row to the AppShellItem around it and the link; wrap the button in a DropdownMenuTrigger asChild to open a menu.
- `<AppShellSublist>` renders <ul class="ayy-app-shell__sublist">. Props: `aria-label` Required. Names the list.
- `<AppShellCollapse>` renders <details class="ayy-app-shell__collapse"> with a link-styled <summary> and a <ul>. Props: `label` The toggle row: an icon and a short label.; `open` Start open. Set it when the group holds the current page.
- `<AppShellDetail>` renders <aside class="ayy-app-shell__detail"> — pass the hidden attribute to hide it; the shell goes back to two columns.
- `<AppShellResize>` renders <div class="ayy-app-shell__resize" role="separator" tabindex="0"> — a direct child of AppShell. Props: `edge` "sidebar" | "detail", default "sidebar" — which edge it drags.; `aria-valuemin / aria-valuemax` Limits in px.; `aria-label` Defaults to "Resize sidebar" / "Resize detail pane" (translate it).
- `<AppShellFooter>` renders <div class="ayy-app-shell__footer">.
- `<AppShellMain>` renders <main class="ayy-app-shell__main">. Props: `as` "main" | "div" — "div" in a settings dialog, so the page keeps one <main>. Default "main".
- `<AppShellBar>` renders <header class="ayy-app-shell__bar"> — first child; brand, then actions.
- `<AppShellToggle>` renders <button class="ayy-button ayy-button--ghost ayy-button--icon ayy-app-shell__toggle"> with a menu icon; in an AppShellHead it is wrapped in a Tooltip (opening below) that names the collapse action. Props: `aria-label` Defaults to "Menu" in the phone bar, and to the action ("Collapse sidebar" / "Expand sidebar") in an AppShellHead (translate it).; `children` Replaces the default menu icon.; `tooltip` Tooltip text. In an AppShellHead it defaults to the action ("Collapse" / "Expand"); the phone drawer's menu has none. false disables it.; `tooltipSide` "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end", default "bottom" in an AppShellHead.

**Accessibility**
- The sidebar is an <aside> (a complementary landmark) and the content is a <main>: one <main> per page, and no other element with that landmark.
- Keep one <nav aria-label="Main"> in the sidebar. The bottom nav repeats its top destinations and only one of the two shows at a time, so it can use the same label. Give any other nav (a settings menu) its own label.
- Mark the current page with aria-current="page" in both the sidebar and the bottom nav. The link also gets a tint and a heavier weight, so colour is not the only cue; High Contrast mode fills it with the system highlight.
- Put a .ayy-skip-link before the shell, pointing at an id on <main>, so keyboard users can jump past the sidebar.
- A row's __more is a real button after the link, not inside it (buttons can't nest), and its aria-label names the row ("Project options") so a list of identical "More" buttons isn't ambiguous.
- Group with a heading and a list: the <p> label names the <ul> through aria-labelledby, so a screen reader announces "Workspace, list, 3 items".
- A collapse is a native <details>: Enter and Space toggle it, and the open state is exposed for you. Don't add aria-expanded to the <summary>.
- Mark the current child with aria-current="page" and open its collapse. A closed collapse that holds the current page is drawn bolder, so the location isn't hidden.
- Both columns are scroll containers. If a column can scroll but holds nothing focusable, give it tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it.
- The drawer's toggle is a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the sidebar (set for you). Opening moves focus to the first link in the drawer and makes the rest of the shell inert; Esc closes it and returns focus to the toggle.
- Settings mode: name the dialog by the sidebar title (aria-labelledby on the <dialog>), give the sections' nav its own label ("Settings"), mark the open section with aria-current="page", and make the section's Top bar title its <h1> (the sidebar title is an <h2>). Render the main as a <div> so the page keeps one <main>. On phones, opening a section moves focus to the main, and its back button returns it to the section's link.
- A collapsed sidebar with hover preview opens when keyboard focus moves into it (:focus-visible), so every link is reachable and readable from the keyboard; links without an icon are only in the tab order while it's open. Give rail links a title for a tooltip with the pointer.
- The sidebar's collapse toggle says what it does: in React, its aria-label and tooltip change between "Collapse sidebar" and "Expand sidebar" with the state, so the icon is never a guess. In plain markup, write the label and an <ayy-tooltip> for the state shown.
- In a dialog, Esc closes settings and focus returns to what opened them. A settings shell on a page of its own leaves through its __back on Esc, except when focus is in a text field or an open menu, popover or dialog has it.
- A resize handle is a separator you can focus: arrow keys move the edge by 16px (Shift 64), Home and End jump to the limits, and aria-valuenow / min / max are kept in px.
- The detail pane is an <aside>: label it (aria-label) for what it shows, and move focus into it when you open it from the main area.
- The phone sidebar (closed drawer) is visibility: hidden, and the bottom nav is display: none from 48rem, so hidden links are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree.

**Do**
- Use it as the outer layout of a signed-in app or dashboard.
- Keep the same destinations, icons and order on every screen.
- Use size="sm" for long navigation such as a docs tree.
- With more than five destinations, put the four most used in the bottom nav and end with a "More" tab that opens the drawer.
- Group destinations under headings once there are more than about six.
- Keep each link to one line: an icon and a short label. Put account and help in the footer.
- Give a destination that people manage (a project, a page, a folder) an ayy-app-shell__row with an AppShellMore at its end: the link still opens it, and the ⋯ opens rename, duplicate and archive.
- Give the brand a mark (an icon or your logo) and a name or a __logotype: the rail shows the mark, and resting the pointer on it reveals the expand button.
- Start each page in the main with a Page header.
- Add a __resize handle when people have long names to read, and save the width from onResize / ayy-resize.
- Open settings in a Dialog with size="full", sections grouped, each starting with a Top bar.

**Examples**: Playground — one shell, every variation, Parts — every piece of the shell in one frame. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/app-shell.md.

## Bottom nav

Category: Navigation. The tab bar of a phone app. It keeps the main destinations at the bottom of the screen where a thumb can reach them, each with an icon and a short label. Inside an App shell it replaces the sidebar on phones. Also called: bottom-nav, tab-bar, tabbar, bottom-bar.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-bottom-nav` — The <nav>. Equal-width columns, one per link. Sticky to the bottom of its scroll container (the page, or the box it scrolls in), with the safe-area inset added below. As a direct child of .ayy-app-shell it shows below 48rem only; from 48rem the sidebar carries the same links.
- `.ayy-bottom-nav--sm` — Small height (28px) with 16px icons and compact padding.
- `.ayy-bottom-nav--md` — Medium height (32px) with 20px icons and medium padding.
- `.ayy-bottom-nav--lg` — Large height (40px, default) with 20px icons and generous touch padding.
- `.ayy-bottom-nav--compact` — Compact layout with tighter padding and narrower pills so five or more tabs fit side-by-side without overflowing.
- `.ayy-bottom-nav--icon-only` — Icon-only layout, visually hiding tab labels while keeping them accessible for screen readers.
- `.ayy-bottom-nav__link` — A tab: icon over label. An <a> for a destination, or a <button> for a tab that acts ("More", which opens the app shell's drawer when it also has ayy-app-shell__toggle). aria-current="page" (or aria-expanded="true" on the button) draws a pill behind the icon and a heavier label.
- `.ayy-bottom-nav__label` — The tab's text, one line, cut with an ellipsis if it's too long.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-bottom-nav__link:hover`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-bottom-nav__link:focus-visible`)
- `selected` (`[aria-current="page"], or [aria-expanded="true"] on a More button`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — Small height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch) with 16px icons.
- `md` — Medium height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch) with 20px icons.
- `lg` (default) — Large height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch) with 20px icons and generous touch padding.
- Density — Each tab follows the control height scale (sm 28px, md 32px, lg 40px compact); the bar adds the safe-area inset at the bottom.
- Width — Full width, tabs share it equally (three to five in default, five to seven or more in compact).

**React** — `import { BottomNav, BottomNavLink, BottomNavButton } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<BottomNav>` renders <nav class="ayy-bottom-nav">. Props: `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg" — height scale (default "lg").; `compact` boolean — tighter horizontal footprint to fit more items.; `iconOnly` boolean — visually hides text labels while preserving screen reader text.; `aria-label` Defaults to "Main" (translate it).
- `<BottomNavLink>` renders <a class="ayy-bottom-nav__link"> with the icon and a <span class="ayy-bottom-nav__label">. Props: `icon` ReactNode — the icon above the label (an <Icon>).; `current` boolean — sets aria-current="page".
- `<BottomNavButton>` renders <button type="button" class="ayy-bottom-nav__link"> with the icon and a label <span>. Props: `icon` ReactNode — the icon above the label.

**Accessibility**
- It's a <nav>: give it an aria-label ("Main" by default in React). Inside an App shell only one of it and the sidebar shows at a time, so they can share the label.
- Mark the current page with aria-current="page". It also gets a pill and a heavier weight, so colour isn't the only cue; High Contrast mode fills the pill with the system highlight.
- Visible labels are recommended. When iconOnly is used, screen reader text is preserved via visually hidden labels.
- A "More" tab is a <button> with aria-expanded (set for you when it's an app shell toggle), not a link to "#".
- Each tab is at least the control height of its size tier (sm 28px, md 32px, lg 40px), maintaining comfortable touch targets.
- Outside an App shell, content above it needs bottom padding (or to end before it) so the last line isn't hidden behind the bar.

**Do**
- Use a bottom nav for top-level destinations of a phone app, so they're one thumb-tap away.
- Use compact mode or sm/md sizes when accommodating five or more destinations.
- Put it inside the App shell, after the main: it shows on phones and the sidebar takes over from 48rem, with no media query of yours.
- Give it the same destinations, icons and order as the sidebar's top-level links.
- Keep labels to one short word: Home, Search, Inbox, Account.
- With many destinations, end with a "More" tab that opens the sidebar as a drawer (a BottomNavButton with the ayy-app-shell__toggle class).

**Examples**: Phone tab bar. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/bottom-nav.md.

## Top bar

Category: Navigation. The header of a phone screen, with a back button, the screen title and a few actions. It stays at the top, and can hold a search bar or a segmented control beneath it. Also called: top-bar, topbar, app-bar, appbar, screen-header, header-bar.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-top-bar` — A <header>: sticky at the top of its scroll container, the page colour with a hairline under it. As the first child of an .ayy-app-shell__main it runs edge to edge over the main area's padding.
- `.ayy-top-bar--center` — The title centred between the back button and the actions.
- `.ayy-top-bar--large` — The buttons on the first line, a big title on its own line under them.
- `.ayy-top-bar__back` — An <a href> or <button> with a directional chevron (.ayy-icon--directional) and optionally the previous screen's name in a <span>. Chevron only: aria-label="Back".
- `.ayy-top-bar__title` — The screen's name, an <h1>; cut with an ellipsis when long.
- `.ayy-top-bar__heading` — Wraps the __title and a __subtitle when there is one.
- `.ayy-top-bar__subtitle` — A muted line under the title ("8 items", "Edited 2 min ago").
- `.ayy-top-bar__actions` — One to three icon buttons (.ayy-button--ghost.ayy-button--icon, each with an aria-label) or a short text button (Save), at the end.
- `.ayy-top-bar__row` — A second line across the bar: a Search bar, a Segmented control, Chips.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-top-bar__back:hover (devices that hover)`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-top-bar__back:focus-visible`)

**Sizes**
- Density — At least the lg control height plus 16px; the back button is the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch).
- Width — Full width of its scroll container (edge to edge as the first child of an App shell's main). large wraps the title onto its own line.

**React** — `import { TopBar } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<TopBar>` renders <header class="ayy-top-bar"> back + <h1 class="ayy-top-bar__title"> + actions; children go in a __row. Props: `title` ReactNode — the screen's name (an <h1>); `subtitle` ReactNode — a line under it; `backHref` string — the back button is a link there; `onBack` () => void — the back button is a <button> running this; `backLabel` string — the previous screen's name after the chevron; `backAriaLabel` string — the chevron's name when there's no backLabel. Default "Back"; `actions` ReactNode — icon buttons at the end; `center` boolean — centre the title; `large` boolean — a big title under the buttons

**Accessibility**
- The title is the page's <h1>, so a screen reader user knows where they landed after navigating.
- A chevron-only back button is named "Back" (translate it); with a visible name ("Lists") the text names it.
- Icon buttons in __actions each need an aria-label. Keep to three; put the rest in a Menu behind a More button.
- The chevron is directional, so it points right in RTL, where "back" is.

**Do**
- Use it at the top of every phone screen below the tab bar's first level, with a back button to where the user came from.
- Use large on a tab's first screen (Inbox, Notes), plain on the screens pushed from it.
- Put the screen's own search in the __row so it scrolls away with the bar or stays, as you choose.
- Start each section of a settings shell (App shell in settings mode, in a size="full" Dialog) with one: onBack (or backHref) to the section list, backLabel "Settings", the section's name as the title. Its back button shows on phones only, and on wide screens its title lines up with the section's column.

**Examples**: Back, title with subtitle, actions, Large title with a search bar, Centred title. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/top-bar.md.

## Footer

Category: Navigation. The bottom of a website page: the brand with a short line about the product, groups of links, and copyright and legal links. Also called: footer, site-footer.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-footer` — Root <footer>, a hairline above it.
- `.ayy-footer__inner` — Centred grid at page width (--ayy-size-container) with the page gutter: brand beside the link columns, one column below 64rem.
- `.ayy-footer__brand` — Brand link (first <a>) and a short line (<p>) under it.
- `.ayy-footer__nav` — <nav aria-label="Footer">: link columns, as many as fit (9rem minimum).
- `.ayy-footer__group` — One column: a __heading over a __list.
- `.ayy-footer__heading` — The column heading, a small muted <p> that names the list (aria-labelledby).
- `.ayy-footer__list` — The <ul> of links in a column.
- `.ayy-footer__link` — A footer link: soft text, underline on hover, focus ring.
- `.ayy-footer__bottom` — The last row across the whole footer, above a hairline: copyright at the start, legal links or a theme menu at the end.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-footer__link:hover`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-footer__link:focus-visible, brand link :focus-visible`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Doesn't follow data-density.
- Width — Full width; content centred at --ayy-size-container. Brand beside the columns; one column below 64rem.

**React** — `import { Footer, FooterBrand, FooterNav, FooterGroup, FooterLink, FooterBottom } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Footer>` renders <footer class="ayy-footer"><div class="ayy-footer__inner">.
- `<FooterBrand>` renders <div class="ayy-footer__brand">.
- `<FooterNav>` renders <nav class="ayy-footer__nav">. Props: `aria-label` Defaults to "Footer" (translate it).
- `<FooterGroup>` renders <div class="ayy-footer__group"> with a heading <p> and a <ul>. Props: `label` The column heading. Names the list.
- `<FooterLink>` renders <li><a class="ayy-footer__link">.
- `<FooterBottom>` renders <div class="ayy-footer__bottom">.

**Accessibility**
- Use <footer> once per page, outside <main>: it's the contentinfo landmark.
- The link columns are a <nav aria-label="Footer">, distinct from the navbar's "Main".
- Each column's heading names its list, so screen readers announce "Product, list, 4 items".

**Do**
- Use the footer at the end of every page of a website, after <main>.
- Group links into two to four columns with one-word headings (Product, Company, Resources, Legal).
- Put the copyright and legal links in FooterBottom, and a theme menu there too if the navbar doesn't have one.

**Examples**: Site footer. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/footer.md.

## Breadcrumb

Category: Navigation. A trail of links that shows where the current page sits in the site, from the top level down. It lets people jump back to any page above it. Also called: breadcrumb, breadcrumbs, crumbs.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-breadcrumb` — Root <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">.
- `.ayy-breadcrumb--pill` — Bordered, blurred capsule that stays readable over hero images and grids.
- `.ayy-breadcrumb__list` — The <ol>. Wraps on wide screens; one line on phones, ancestors cut with an ellipsis first.
- `.ayy-breadcrumb__item` — Each <li>. A slash separates items; screen readers skip it.
- `.ayy-breadcrumb__link` — Link to an ancestor page; its target is a small control tall (40px at touch density) without changing the line. The last item is a <span aria-current="page"> instead.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-breadcrumb__link:hover`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-breadcrumb__link:focus-visible`)
- `selected` (`[aria-current="page"] on the last item`)

**Sizes**
- Density — sm text at every density.
- Width — Hugs its items and wraps. pill puts it in a blurred, bordered capsule for heroes.

**React** — `import { Breadcrumb } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Breadcrumb>` renders <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"><ol>…. Props: `items` { label: ReactNode; href?: string }[] — top level first; the last one is the current page.; `pill` boolean; `aria-label` Defaults to "Breadcrumb" (translate it).

**Accessibility**
- Wrap it in <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> and use an <ol>, so it's announced as an ordered path.
- The current page is plain text with aria-current="page", not a link to itself.

**Do**
- Use a breadcrumb on pages that sit two or more levels deep: an index page, a case study, an article.
- Use the page titles as they appear in their own headings.
- Use pill over imagery or the ambient grid; plain elsewhere.

**Examples**: Plain and pill. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/breadcrumb.md.

## Pagination

Category: Navigation. Controls for moving between the pages of a long table or list: previous, next and page numbers. On phones it shrinks to the essentials. Also called: pagination, pager.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-pagination` — Root <nav aria-label="Pagination">. A wrapping row.
- `.ayy-pagination__link` — A page: <a href> when pages have URLs, <button> otherwise. aria-current="page" marks the current one (outlined tint, heavier). aria-disabled="true" (a link without href) or disabled dims an end you can't go past.
- `.ayy-pagination__size` — Optional page size picker: a <div> holding a <label> and a small Select. Goes first in the <nav>.
- `.ayy-pagination__size-label` — The picker's <label for>, "Rows per page". Visually hidden below 48rem, still the select's name.
- `.ayy-pagination__link--step` — Previous / next, with an arrow Icon (directional) and a word. Stays visible on phones, where the numbers hide.
- `.ayy-pagination__ellipsis` — The "…" for skipped pages, aria-hidden.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-pagination__link:hover`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-pagination__link:focus-visible`)
- `disabled` (`:disabled or [aria-disabled="true"] (a link without href at the first or last page)`)
- `selected` (`[aria-current="page"]`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Links are the sm control height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch) with sm control text.
- Width — Hugs its links and wraps. Below 48rem only previous, the current page and next show.

**React** — `import { Pagination } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Pagination>` renders <nav class="ayy-pagination"> with previous, pages from paginationRange() and next. Props: `page` The current page, 1-based.; `count` How many pages there are.; `siblings` Pages either side of the current one. Default 1.; `href` (page) => string — pages become links (?page=3).; `onPageChange` (page) => void — without href, pages become buttons; with it, links still work and the handler runs instead of navigating.; `pageSize` How many items a page holds. Shows the picker when onPageSizeChange is also set.; `pageSizeOptions` number[] — the sizes the picker offers. Default [10, 25, 50]; pageSize is added if missing.; `onPageSizeChange` (pageSize) => void — set the size and go back to page 1.; `labels` { nav?, previous?, next?, pageSize? } — text for translation. Defaults "Pagination", "Previous", "Next", "Rows per page".

**Accessibility**
- It's a <nav aria-label="Pagination">: give a second one on the page a different label.
- The current page has aria-current="page"; it's outlined and bolder as well as tinted.
- Previous and next say so in words; their arrows are decorative and mirror in right-to-left text.
- An end you can't go past is aria-disabled (or disabled): screen readers hear it's unavailable.
- After a page change in place, move focus to the top of the updated table or list, or announce the new range.

**Do**
- Use pagination under a table or list that has more rows than fit, when people need to reach a specific page or share its URL.
- Give pages URLs (href) when you can, so back and reload work.
- Offer a page size picker (pageSize, onPageSizeChange) on long tables so people choose how much they scan.
- Show the range next to it ("41–60 of 1,280") in muted text.

**Examples**: Under a table, With a page size picker. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/pagination.md.

## Steps

Category: Navigation. A progress indicator for a short flow like sign-up or checkout. It shows which step you're on, which are done and which are still to come. Also called: steps, wizard-steps, progress-steps.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-steps` — Root <ol>, a row of steps with lines between them. Numbers come from a CSS counter.
- `.ayy-steps--vertical` — A column, with the lines running down between the markers: for a side panel or a phone.
- `.ayy-steps__item` — A step <li>. aria-current="step" marks the current one (filled marker, bold label); every step before it is drawn as done (tick, solid line); the ones after as to do.
- `.ayy-steps__label` — The step's name, one line (cut with an ellipsis in the row).

**States**
- `selected` (`[aria-current="step"]`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Markers are the sm control height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch).
- Width — Fills its container. In a row narrower than 36rem only the current step keeps a visible label; vertical stacks them for a side panel or phone.

**React** — `import { Steps } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Steps>` renders <ol class="ayy-steps"> of <li class="ayy-steps__item">. Props: `steps` ReactNode[] — the step names, in order.; `current` Index of the current step (0-based).; `vertical` boolean — a column.; `doneLabel` Read before a finished step's name. Default "Done: " (translate it).

**Accessibility**
- It's an ordered list with aria-current="step" on the current item, so screen readers hear "step 2 of 4, current". Give the <ol> an aria-label ("Checkout progress").
- Done steps say so in text, not only with a tick: put an .ayy-sr-only "Done: " before their label (React does it).
- The markers are generated content with empty alt text, so numbers aren't read twice.

**Do**
- Use steps above a multi-page form or wizard with three to five steps, so people know how much is left.
- Name steps by what happens in them (Account, Team, Billing), in one or two words.
- Use the vertical version beside a long form on wide screens, or when the row wouldn't fit a phone.

**Examples**: Checkout, row and column. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/steps.md.

## Table of contents

Category: Navigation. A table of contents for long pages. It lists links to the sections beside the content and highlights the one being read. Also called: toc, table-of-contents, contents.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-toc` — Root <nav>. Accent from --ayy-spot.
- `.ayy-toc--sticky` — Stays in view below the navbar, scrolling on its own if it's taller than the screen. Put it before the content in a wrapping flex row (it takes 11rem) or give it its own grid column. Below 48rem it becomes a sticky pill bar showing the active section that opens the full table of contents in a dropdown menu.
- `.ayy-toc__title` — Small muted heading ("Contents" or "Table of contents"). Point the nav's aria-labelledby at it.
- `.ayy-toc__bar` — Mobile sticky bar holding the toggle pill (hidden above 48rem).
- `.ayy-toc__toggle` — Pill button on mobile showing the active section title and caret, toggling the dropdown menu.
- `.ayy-toc__toggle-icon` — Menu icon inside the mobile toggle pill.
- `.ayy-toc__toggle-current` — Truncated label of the section being read inside the mobile toggle pill.
- `.ayy-toc__toggle-caret` — Chevron icon inside the mobile toggle pill that rotates 180° when the menu is open.
- `.ayy-toc__list` — <ol> of <li>s with a hairline rail on desktop, or a floating dropdown card on phones. Nest one inside an <li> for sub-sections.
- `.ayy-toc__link` — Section link (href="#id"). aria-current (set by the scrollspy) shows the accent bar; its parent link lights up too.
- `.ayy-toc__number` — Optional section number (01, 02…) before the label, in the accent while current.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-toc__link:hover, .ayy-toc__toggle:hover`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-toc__link:focus-visible, .ayy-toc__toggle:focus-visible`)
- `selected` (`.ayy-toc__link[aria-current] (not "false"), kept in sync by <ayy-toc> or connectToc`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Links follow the control height scale (var(--ayy-size-control-sm)), so comfortable or touch density expands their tap target to 40px without changing the rail spacing.
- Width — Fills its column. sticky stays in view under the navbar and scrolls on its own when taller than the viewport.

**Custom element** `<ayy-toc>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — Goes inside <nav class="ayy-toc"> and wraps the title and list. Every .ayy-toc__link with href="#id" is spied; aria-current="location" is set and removed for you.
- attribute `offset`: Distance in px below the top of the viewport at which a section becomes current. Default: the page's scroll-padding-top (the navbar sets it) + 24.
- event `ayy-value-change`: { value: string } — id of the section now being read ("" above the first)

**React** — `import { Toc } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Toc>` renders <nav class="ayy-toc">. Props: `items` { id: string; label: ReactNode; children?: TocItem[] }[] — ids of sections on the page, in page order.; `title` ReactNode — visible heading; also becomes the nav's accessible name.; `toggleLabel` string — accessible label for the mobile toggle button. Default: "Table of contents".; `numbered` boolean — number top-level items 01, 02…; `sticky` boolean; `offset` number — px below the top of the viewport at which a section becomes current.; `onValueChange` (id: string) => void — the section being read changed.; `aria-label` Used when there's no title. Defaults to "On this page" (translate it).

**Accessibility**
- It's a <nav> with a name (the title via aria-labelledby, or aria-label="On this page"), so it shows up in landmark lists.
- The current section is aria-current="location", announced by screen readers, not only drawn as a colour bar.
- Links are ordinary in-page anchors: they work without JS, and the navbar's scroll-padding keeps targets clear of the sticky header.
- Links grow to a 40px target at touch density. On phones the visible title is hidden but still names the nav, and the sticky toggle pill is labeled via aria-label.

**Do**
- Use a table of contents on long pages with named sections: case studies, docs, articles, settings pages.
- List sections in page order; the scrollspy assumes it.
- Set --ayy-spot on the page (or the nav) to tint the bar and number with the content's accent.
- Make the page layout put it above the content on phones (a wrapping flex row does, as in the example); --sticky then turns it into a sticky pill with a dropdown menu.

**Examples**: Numbered, beside the content. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/toc.md.

## Tree

Category: Navigation. A hierarchical list of folders, files or records: groups that open and close with a chevron, one selected row and arrow-key navigation. Use it to browse a folder or file structure, or as a picker inside a card. Also called: tree, tree-view, file-tree, folder-tree, treeitem.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-tree` — Root <ul role="tree">. Its aria-label names it ("Folders"). <ayy-tree> wraps it with display: contents.
- `.ayy-tree__item` — One <li role="treeitem">. Carries aria-level, aria-selected on every node, aria-expanded only on parents, and a roving tabindex: exactly one visible item is 0, the rest -1. aria-disabled="true" makes it unselectable.
- `.ayy-tree__row` — The clickable row inside the item: toggle, optional icon and label. Hover and selected washes sit here, and so does the focus ring.
- `.ayy-tree__toggle` — The decorative <span aria-hidden="true"> holding the chevron. Clicking it opens or closes the group without selecting the row; the treeitem's aria-expanded carries the state.
- `.ayy-tree__icon` — An optional decorative icon before the label (an <svg class="ayy-icon ayy-tree__icon"> drawn by Icon or iconSvg). Muted, and text colour on the selected row.
- `.ayy-tree__label` — The node's label. It takes the leftover width, wraps anywhere so a long unbroken name never scrolls the tree sideways, and is not the accessible name: the item's aria-label is.
- `.ayy-tree__group` — A nested <ul role="group"> of child items, indented by --ayy-space-5 (--ayy-space-4 with --compact). Put hidden on it while its parent is aria-expanded="false"; connectTree keeps the two in step.
- `.ayy-tree--compact` — Tighter rows at the sm control height, small control text, a 16px indent and a 16px toggle.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-tree__row:hover on a device that hovers`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-tree__item:focus-visible`)
- `disabled` (`aria-disabled="true" on the treeitem`)
- `selected` (`aria-selected="true" on the treeitem, set by a click, Space, or your selectedId`)
- `expanded` (`aria-expanded="true" on a parent treeitem`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Rows are at least the md control height (32px compact, 40px comfortable, 44px touch) with --ayy-control-text-md; --compact uses the sm height (28, 32, 40) and --ayy-control-text-sm. The toggle is 20px (16px compact), so touch density keeps a comfortable target.
- Width — Fills its container. Child groups indent by --ayy-space-5 (--ayy-space-4 compact) using padding-inline-start, so they indent from the right in RTL. Labels take the leftover width and wrap anywhere.

**Custom element** `<ayy-tree>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — Wraps the <ul role="tree"> and makes it work: the toggle opens and closes a group, a row selects, double-click or Enter activates, and the arrow keys, Home and End move the roving tab stop. focus(id) moves to a node from code.
- event `ayy-select`: { id } — a row was clicked or Space was pressed on it.
- event `ayy-activate`: { id } — a row was double-clicked or Enter was pressed on it (open the file or folder).
- event `ayy-toggle`: { id, expanded } — a group was opened (true) or closed (false).

**React** — `import { Tree, type TreeNode } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Tree>` renders <ul class="ayy-tree" role="tree" aria-label> with a <li class="ayy-tree__item" role="treeitem"> per node, a __row inside it, and a nested <ul class="ayy-tree__group" role="group" hidden> for children. Props: `label` string — accessible name of the tree ("Folders"); `nodes` TreeNode[] — { id: string; label: string; icon?: ReactNode; children?: TreeNode[]; disabled?: boolean }, nested in display order; `expandedIds / defaultExpandedIds` string[] — open group ids; expandedIds makes it controlled, defaultExpandedIds sets the starting ones; `onExpandedChange` (ids: string[]) => void — a group opened or closed; `selectedId / defaultSelectedId` string — the selected node; selectedId makes it controlled, defaultSelectedId sets the starting one; `onSelectedChange` (id: string | null) => void — a row was selected; `onActivate` (id: string) => void — a row was double-clicked or Enter was pressed; `compact` boolean — tighter rows, a smaller indent and the small control text

**Accessibility**
- The tree is a <ul role="tree"> with a name (label in React, aria-label in HTML); each node is a <li role="treeitem"> with aria-level, and children sit in a <ul role="group">.
- aria-expanded is only on parents and aria-selected is on every node, so the state is announced rather than drawn only as a wash. The toggle is decorative (aria-hidden) and the item's aria-label is the node label, never the toggle.
- One visible item has tabindex="0" and the rest -1 (a roving tab stop). Tab enters the tree on the selected node, then the arrow keys, Home and End move through the visible nodes: Right closes an open group or opens a closed one and steps into its first child, Left closes an open group or moves to the parent.
- Enter activates a node and Space selects it. Double-click activates too. A composing IME and fields inside a row (a rename input) keep their keys.
- aria-disabled="true" keeps a node readable and reachable by the keyboard while it refuses selection and activation; colour is backed by opacity and, in High Contrast, GrayText.
- Long labels wrap inside the row instead of scrolling the tree sideways, and touch density raises the rows to the 44px target.

**Do**
- Use a tree to browse a nested structure: folders and files, a page hierarchy, categories or a project's contents.
- Keep ids stable and pass them as expandedIds/selectedId when the rest of the screen shows the same folder (a picker in a card, a split view).
- Pair the chevron with the label on the same row and let the label wrap; never truncate a folder name to make a narrow tree fit.

**Examples**: Project files, Choose a folder. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/tree.md.

## Field

Category: Forms. A wrapper that ties a label, an input and its hint or error message together with consistent spacing. Use it around any form control. Also called: field, form-field, form-row.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-field` — Wrapper, vertical stack.
- `.ayy-field--inline` — Label and control side by side (Switch, checkbox).
- `.ayy-label` — The <label>. Usable on its own too.
- `.ayy-field__hint` — Muted helper text under the control.
- `.ayy-field__error` — Error text under the control.

**States**
- `disabled` (`.ayy-field:has(:disabled), .ayy-label:has(> :disabled)`)
- `error` (`aria-invalid="true" on the control plus .ayy-field__error, linked with aria-describedby (React: FieldError)`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Label text follows control md, hint and error control sm, so they grow with data-density.
- Width — Fills its column; the control inside stretches to it. inline puts the control and label side by side (checkboxes, switches).

**React** — `import { Field, Label, FieldHint, FieldError } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Field>` renders <div>. Props: `inline` boolean
- `<Label>` renders <label>. Props: `htmlFor` id of the control
- `<FieldHint>` renders <p>.
- `<FieldError>` renders <p>.

**Accessibility**
- Label htmlFor/for must match the control id.
- Link hint/error to the control with aria-describedby; set aria-invalid="true" on the control when there's an error.
- The label dims automatically when the control inside the field is disabled.

**Do**
- Wrap every labelled form control in a Field: Input, Input group, Textarea, Select, Switch, Checkbox.
- Keep hints to one short sentence.
- Show errors after the user leaves the field or submits, not on every keystroke.

**Examples**: Form fields. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/field.md.

## Input

Category: Forms. A single-line text field for names, emails, passwords, search and other short text. It can hold icons, addons and buttons inside the field. Also called: input, text-field, textbox, text-input, input-group, input-addon, input-adornment.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-input` — Root, on the <input> itself.
- `.ayy-input--sm` — 28px tall.
- `.ayy-input--lg` — 40px tall.
- `.ayy-input-group` — Root for an input with inline addons, icons or buttons. Draws the field (border, fill, radius, height) and the focus ring while its .ayy-input is focused.
- `.ayy-input-group--sm` — Small height (--ayy-size-control-sm).
- `.ayy-input-group--lg` — Large height (--ayy-size-control-lg).
- `.ayy-input-group__addon` — Text beside the input: a prefix (https://), a suffix (USD, %) or a Kbd hint. Muted, one line.

**States**
- `hover` (`:hover`)
- `focus` (`:focus-visible, or .ayy-input-group:has(> .ayy-input:focus-visible)`)
- `disabled` (`:disabled, or .ayy-input-group:has(> .ayy-input:disabled)`)
- `error` (`aria-invalid="true" (with a FieldError)`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — Control sm height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), tighter padding, sm text.
- `md` (default) — Control md height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch).
- `lg` — Control lg height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), more padding, lg text.
- Density — Height and text size follow data-density; touch keeps md text at 16px so iOS doesn't zoom.
- Width — Fills its container (inline-size 100%); set a max-inline-size in rem for short values.

**React** — `import { Input, InputGroup, InputGroupAddon } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Input>` renders <input>. Props: `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg" (visual size; native size attr not exposed); `...rest` All native <input> attributes.
- `<InputGroup>` renders <div class="ayy-input-group">. Props: `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg"; `...rest` All native <div> attributes.
- `<InputGroupAddon>` renders <span class="ayy-input-group__addon">. Props: `...rest` All native <span> attributes.

**Accessibility**
- Every input needs a label: wrap in a Field with a Label (for/id), or aria-label for search boxes.
- The input inside an InputGroup still needs its own label; icons and addons do not name it.
- Errors: aria-invalid="true" + aria-describedby pointing at the error text.
- Action buttons inside an InputGroup (show password, clear) must have an accessible aria-label and aria-pressed where applicable.

**Do**
- Use an input for short free-text entry: names, URLs, search, API keys, passwords.
- Use an InputGroup when an input needs a leading icon, a prefix/suffix unit, or a trailing action button.
- Match the input size to neighbouring buttons in a toolbar (sm with sm).

**Examples**: Sizes, Input types, Input group & addons, Validation error. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/input.md.

## PIN input

Category: Forms. One box per character for verification codes, two-factor authentication tokens and passcodes. Typing advances to the next box, Backspace steps back, and pasting or SMS autofill fills the whole code at once. Also called: pin-input, otp-input, otp, pin-field, verification-code, passcode-input.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-pin-input` — Root group (role="group", direction ltr so codes always read left to right).
- `.ayy-pin-input--sm` — Small slots (--ayy-size-control-sm square, sm text).
- `.ayy-pin-input--lg` — Large slots (--ayy-size-control-lg square, lg text).
- `.ayy-pin-input__group` — Tighter cluster of slots when a code is split into halves (e.g. 3 + 3).
- `.ayy-pin-input__separator` — Muted dash between slot groups (aria-hidden="true").
- `.ayy-pin-input__slot` — Each character <input>: monospace, centred, tabular-nums.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-pin-input__slot:hover (hover devices)`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-pin-input__slot:focus-visible`)
- `disabled` (`disabled on the slots`)
- `error` (`aria-invalid="true" on .ayy-pin-input or .ayy-pin-input__slot (with a FieldError)`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — Square at --ayy-size-control-sm (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), sm text.
- `md` (default) — Square at --ayy-size-control-md (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), field text.
