**Custom element** `<ayy-popover>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — A trigger <button> (optionally data-ayy-trigger) and an element with the popover attribute.
- attribute `side`: bottom | top | start | end
- attribute `align`: center | start | end
- attribute `open`: Two-way open state
- event `ayy-open-change`: { open: boolean }

**React** — `import { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Popover>` renders nothing (state provider). Props: `open / defaultOpen` boolean; `onOpenChange` (open: boolean) => void
- `<PopoverTrigger>` renders Button. Props: `asChild` boolean — clone child element and merge trigger props; `...ButtonProps` variant, size…
- `<PopoverContent>` renders <div popover role="dialog">. Props: `side` "bottom" | "top" | "start" | "end"; `align` "center" | "start" | "end"

**Accessibility**
- Give the content an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing at its heading).
- The trigger gets aria-expanded automatically; Esc and click-outside close it and focus returns to the trigger.
- It's not a focus trap — use Dialog when the user must finish something first.

**Do**
- Use a popover for small forms or details next to their trigger (share link, filters, quick edit).
- Keep content short; if it scrolls, it probably wants to be a Dialog or a page.

**Examples**: Share link. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/popover.md.

## Tooltip

Category: Overlays. A short hint that appears when someone hovers or focuses an element, for naming icon buttons or giving a little extra detail. It stays inside the screen and never gets clipped. Also called: tooltip, tip.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-tooltip` — Wrapper around the trigger. Shows the content on :hover and :focus-within.
- `.ayy-tooltip__content` — The bubble (role="tooltip"). Placement via data-side="top|bottom|start|end" (start/end follow text direction).

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-tooltip:hover`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-tooltip:is(:has(:focus-visible), :focus-visible), unless data-ayy-input="pointer"`)
- `dismissed` (`[data-dismissed] (Esc, set by React Tooltip or <ayy-tooltip>)`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Text size follows data-density (var(--ayy-text-s)); padding is fixed.
- Width — As wide as its text, at most 16rem, then wraps.

**Custom element** `<ayy-tooltip>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — One focusable trigger and a .ayy-tooltip__content bubble. Ids and aria-describedby are wired for you.
- attribute `side`: top | bottom | start | end
- attribute `class`: Put ayy-tooltip on it.

**React** — `import { Tooltip } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Tooltip>` renders <span class="ayy-tooltip"> + child + <span role="tooltip">. Props: `content` ReactNode (required) — the hint; `side` "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end"; `children` One focusable element; aria-describedby is added for you

**Accessibility**
- Trigger must be focusable so keyboard users see it too.
- aria-describedby links trigger → tooltip (React does it automatically).
- Esc dismisses (WCAG 1.4.13); the bubble stays open while hovered.

**Do**
- Use a tooltip to name icon-only buttons visually (they still need aria-label) and for short clarifications: shortcuts, truncated values.
- Keep action tooltips general ("Edit", "Delete", "More actions", "Copy"), never specific to an item ("Edit Lumen Labs") — leave the specific item in aria-label for screen readers.
- Show a shortcut with <Shortcut keys="Mod+…" /> (or .ayy-shortcut in HTML) so Mac and Windows users each see their own keys as keycaps.
- Keep it under ~60 characters.
- Use side="start"/"end", not left/right, so RTL works.
- Inside overflow:hidden containers, use the React component or <ayy-tooltip> — the CSS-only version can be clipped there.

**Examples**: Sides. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/tooltip.md.

## Alert

Category: Feedback. A message placed in the flow of a page to tell someone something they should notice, like a warning, an error or a confirmation. It can carry a title, a short explanation and actions. Also called: alert, banner, callout, notice, admonition.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-alert` — Root. Neutral by default.
- `.ayy-alert--info` — Blue tint.
- `.ayy-alert--success` — Green tint.
- `.ayy-alert--warning` — Amber tint.
- `.ayy-alert--destructive` — Red tint.
- `.ayy-alert__title` — Bold first line.
- `.ayy-alert__description` — Supporting text.
- `.ayy-alert__actions` — Row of buttons.

**States**
- `error` (`destructive (ayy-alert--destructive), role="alert" when it appears after an action`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Padding and sm text are fixed.
- Width — Fills its container.

**React** — `import { Alert, AlertTitle, AlertDescription, AlertActions } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Alert>` renders <div>. Props: `variant` "default" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "destructive"
- `<AlertTitle>` renders <p>.
- `<AlertDescription>` renders <p>.
- `<AlertActions>` renders <div>.

**Accessibility**
- Static alerts need no role. If it appears in response to an action, add role="alert" (urgent) or role="status" (polite).
- The icon is decorative: aria-hidden="true". The text must carry the meaning.

**Do**
- Use an alert for page- or section-level messages that stay until they're resolved: a billing issue, read-only mode, maintenance.
- Lead with what happened, then say what to do about it.

**Examples**: Variants. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/alert.md.

## Toast

Category: Feedback. A short message that appears briefly to confirm something happened. It shows above everything else on the page, including dialogs, and can carry images or previews as well as text. Also called: toast, snackbar, notification, card-toast, quick-access.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-toaster` — The shared region toast() creates (aria-live). Position via data-position; data-expanded on hover or focus.
- `.ayy-toaster__clear` — "Clear all" button in the open stack's top-end corner (bottom-end under a top-positioned stack); shown only while the stack is open with two or more toasts.
- `.ayy-toast` — One toast; stacked card with swipe-to-dismiss.
- `.ayy-toast--success` — Success variant with checkmark icon.
- `.ayy-toast--warning` — Warning variant with alert icon.
- `.ayy-toast--destructive` — Destructive variant with cancel icon; announced with role="alert".
- `.ayy-toast--info` — Info variant with information icon.
- `.ayy-toast--card` — Card toast variant with media preview and action scrim.
- `.ayy-toast--card-split` — Split card toast variant with media preview thumbnail and text content details.
- `.ayy-toast--card-split--vertical` — Vertical split card toast variant with media preview stacked above text details.
- `.ayy-toast--long` — Long text variant with normal text size and copy button.
- `.ayy-toast--inline` — Inline feedback pill embedded in a card, toolbar, or form without a toaster region.
- `.ayy-toast--inline--success` — Success tone for inline toast.
- `.ayy-toast--inline--busy` — Busy tone for inline toast with spinner.
- `.ayy-toast--inline--error` — Error tone for inline toast with alert icon.
- `.ayy-toast__icon` — Leading status icon.
- `.ayy-toast__content` — Message and description container.
- `.ayy-toast__title` — Message.
- `.ayy-toast__description` — Optional second line.
- `.ayy-toast__actions` — Action button row.
- `.ayy-toast__copy` — Copy button to copy message to clipboard.
- `.ayy-toast__close` — Close button.
- `.ayy-toast__backdrop` — Blurred backdrop image behind preview.
- `.ayy-toast__image` — Foreground preview image or video frame.
- `.ayy-toast__thumb` — Thumbnail container for split card toast preview image.
- `.ayy-toast__media` — Video or GIF duration badge.
- `.ayy-toast__scrim` — Action overlay visible on card hover or focus.
- `.ayy-toast__center` — Center primary and secondary action buttons.
- `.ayy-toast__corner` — Corner action button container.
- `.ayy-toast__corner--top` — Top corner action buttons.
- `.ayy-toast__corner--top-start` — Top start corner action buttons.
- `.ayy-toast__corner--bottom-start` — Bottom start corner action buttons.
- `.ayy-toast__corner--bottom-end` — Bottom end corner action buttons.
- `.ayy-toast__action` — Icon action button inside scrim.
- `.ayy-toast__status` — Inline feedback pill after an action.
- `.ayy-toast__status--success` — Success status tone with checkmark.
- `.ayy-toast__status--busy` — Busy status tone with spinner.
- `.ayy-toast__status--error` — Error status tone with alert icon.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-toaster[data-expanded]; .ayy-toast--card:hover`)
- `pressed` (`.ayy-toast--card:active`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-toast__close:focus-visible`)
- `error` (`toast({ variant: "destructive" })`)
- `leaving` (`[data-leaving] (set by toast())`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Doesn't follow data-density.
- Width — min(22rem, viewport minus 2rem) or min(28rem, viewport minus 2rem) for long text toasts, stacked in the corner given by position; card toasts are min(17.5rem, 100%).

**React** — `import { toast, Toaster, NotificationToast, Toast, InlineToast, CardToast, CardToastThumb, CardToastBackdrop, CardToastImage, CardToastMedia, CardToastScrim, CardToastClose, CardToastCorner, CardToastCenter, CardToastAction, CardToastStatus } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Toaster>` renders nothing — configures the shared region. Props: `position` "bottom-end" | "bottom-start" | "bottom-center" | "top-end" | "top-start" | "top-center"; `label` string — region name (translate); `closeLabel` string — close button name (translate); `clearLabel` string — "Clear all" button text (translate)
- `<NotificationToast>` renders div.ayy-toast. Props: `variant` "default" | "success" | "warning" | "destructive" | "info" | "card" | "long"; `title` ReactNode — message text; `description` ReactNode — optional second line; `icon` ReactNode — leading icon; `action` { label: string, onClick?: () => void }; `copyable` boolean — show copy button (default true for long variant); `copyText` string — custom text to copy; `onClose` () => void — dismiss handler; `closeLabel` string — accessible dismiss name
- `<Toast>` renders div.ayy-toast — alias of NotificationToast. Props: 
- `<InlineToast>` renders div.ayy-toast--inline. Props: `tone` "default" | "success" | "busy" | "error"; `icon` ReactNode — leading icon
- `<CardToast>` renders div.ayy-toast.ayy-toast--card. Props: `split` boolean | "horizontal" | "vertical"; `ratio` number | string — the picture's shape, width ÷ height (1.6, or "1440 / 900"): the card follows it between 6.75rem and 14rem tall (sets --ayy-ratio). Default 16 / 10
- `<CardToastThumb>` renders div.ayy-toast__thumb. Props: 
- `<CardToastBackdrop>` renders img.ayy-toast__backdrop. Props: 
- `<CardToastImage>` renders img.ayy-toast__image. Props: 
- `<CardToastMedia>` renders span.ayy-toast__media. Props: 
- `<CardToastScrim>` renders div.ayy-toast__scrim. Props: 
- `<CardToastClose>` renders button.ayy-toast__close inside a Tooltip. Props: `label` string — accessible name and tooltip. Default "Dismiss"; `tooltip` boolean — false drops the tooltip (the label stays the accessible name). Default true; `side` "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end" — tooltip side. Default "bottom"
- `<CardToastCorner>` renders div.ayy-toast__corner. Props: `position` "top" | "top-start" | "bottom-start" | "bottom-end"
- `<CardToastCenter>` renders div.ayy-toast__center. Props: 
- `<CardToastAction>` renders button.ayy-hover-action.ayy-toast__action inside a Tooltip (a Hover action). Props: `label` string — accessible name and tooltip; `hint` ReactNode — after the label in the tooltip, e.g. <Shortcut keys="Mod+C" />; `tooltip` boolean — false drops the tooltip (the label stays the accessible name). Default true; `side` "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end" — tooltip side. Default "bottom"
- `<CardToastStatus>` renders div.ayy-toast--inline. Props: `tone` "default" | "success" | "busy" | "error"; `icon` ReactNode — status icon

**Accessibility**
- The region is aria-live="polite"; destructive toasts use role="alert".
- Timers pause while the toaster stack or a toast is hovered or focused, so there's time to read it and reach its action.
- Messages are set with textContent — never HTML.

**Do**
- Use NotificationToast (or toast()) to confirm something happened (Saved, Deployed) or report an async receipt needing no decision.
- Say what happened in 2–5 words: "Project deleted".
- Offer one Undo-style action instead of a confirmation dialog for reversible actions.
- Use CardToast (toast.card()) for content previews that are visual — screenshots, screen recordings, video frames, GIFs, and image downloads.
- Use the split CardToast variation when the user needs both an image preview thumbnail and file metadata (filename, dimensions, size) with direct actions.
- Use InlineToast for localized contextual feedback (e.g. "Copied to clipboard", loading spinner) embedded directly within a card, toolbar, or form without triggering the toaster region.

**Examples**: Trigger toast, Toast types, Inline toast. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/toast.md.

## Progress

Category: Feedback. A bar that shows how far along something is, or that work is happening when the end isn't known. Also called: progress, progress-bar, progressbar, meter.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-progress` — Track. Set --ayy-value (0–100) on it.
- `.ayy-progress__bar` — Fill (only child).
- `.ayy-progress--sm` — 4px tall.
- `.ayy-progress--lg` — 10px tall.
- `.ayy-progress--success` — Green fill.
- `.ayy-progress--warning` — Amber fill.
- `.ayy-progress--destructive` — Red fill.
- `.ayy-progress--ai` — Purple fill.
- `.ayy-progress--indeterminate` — Looping animation; omit aria-valuenow.

**States**
- `error` (`destructive (ayy-progress--destructive)`)
- `loading` (`.ayy-progress--indeterminate without aria-valuenow`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — 4px track.
- `md` (default) — 6px track.
- `lg` — 10px track.
- Density — Doesn't follow data-density.
- Width — Fills its container.

**React** — `import { Progress } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Progress>` renders <div role="progressbar">. Props: `value` number 0–100; omit/null → indeterminate; `variant` "default" | "success" | "warning" | "destructive" | "ai" — the same prop name as Alert and Badge; `tone` Deprecated alias of variant.; `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg"

**Accessibility**
- role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max (React sets them).
- Give it an accessible name: aria-label or aria-labelledby.

**Do**
- Use a progress bar when you know how far along something is: an upload, an import, a quota, a goal.
- Use indeterminate for work of unknown length that takes more than ~1s.
- Show the percentage or step as text nearby for anything longer than a few seconds.
- For quotas or meters that aren't progress, the look still works — set role="meter" instead of progressbar.

**Examples**: Values, tones, indeterminate, Task progress with status, Usage quotas and limits, Interactive simulation. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/progress.md.

## Progress ring

Category: Feedback. Progress shown as a ring that fills up, for goals, timers and uploads in small spaces. It can show a known amount or an unknown one, with a value or an icon in the middle. Also called: progress-ring, circular-progress, progress-circle, radial-progress, ring-progress, timer-ring.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-progress-ring` — Root: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max, an accessible name and --ayy-value (0–100). Clockwise from the top in every direction, like a clock. 2.5rem.
- `.ayy-progress-ring__svg` — First child: <svg viewBox="0 0 36 36" aria-hidden="true"> holding the track and the bar circles (cx=18 cy=18 r=16 pathLength=100). progressRingSvg is the markup.
- `.ayy-progress-ring__track` — The full circle behind the fill.
- `.ayy-progress-ring__bar` — The fill: a round-capped arc as long as --ayy-value. Hidden at aria-valuenow="0".
- `.ayy-progress-ring__label` — Optional, in the middle: the value ("3/5"), a time, or an Icon. Scales with the ring; leave it out at sm.
- `.ayy-progress-ring--sm` — 1.25rem, next to a line of text.
- `.ayy-progress-ring--lg` — 4rem.
- `.ayy-progress-ring--xl` — Up to 16rem (70% of a phone's width): a timer.
- `.ayy-progress-ring--success` — Green fill.
- `.ayy-progress-ring--warning` — Amber fill.
- `.ayy-progress-ring--destructive` — Red fill.
- `.ayy-progress-ring--ai` — Purple fill.
- `.ayy-progress-ring--indeterminate` — A quarter arc going round (still under reduced motion); omit aria-valuenow and --ayy-value.

**States**
- `error` (`variant destructive`)
- `loading` (`indeterminate (ayy-progress-ring--indeterminate), no aria-valuenow`)
- `empty` (`aria-valuenow="0"`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — 20px, a thicker stroke: next to a file name or in a list row.
- `md` (default) — 40px: a goal or a habit's day.
- `lg` — 64px: a card's main figure.
- `xl` — min(16rem, 70vw), a thin stroke and a lighter label: a focus timer's whole screen.
- Density — Doesn't change with data-density; pick a size.
- Width — Square at its size; the label in the middle scales with it.

**React** — `import { ProgressRing } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<ProgressRing>` renders <div role="progressbar" class="ayy-progress-ring"><svg class="ayy-progress-ring__svg">…</svg><span class="ayy-progress-ring__label">{children}</span></div>. Props: `value` number 0–100; omit/null → indeterminate; `variant` "default" | "success" | "warning" | "destructive" | "ai" — as on Progress; `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"

**Accessibility**
- role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max (React sets them). Give it a name with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
- What the label in the middle says isn't read (a progressbar's content is presentational): put it in the name too ("Habit: 3 of 5 days this week").
- The fill is drawn with the system highlight in High Contrast, the track in GrayText.

**Do**
- Use a ring where a circle means something or a bar has no room: a timer, a daily goal, a habit's week, a file's upload in a list row.
- Put the number or time in the middle at md and up; next to the ring at sm.
- Use success when a goal is reached, with a tick in the middle.

**Examples**: A timer, a goal, inline. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/progress-ring.md.

## Spinner

Category: Feedback. A small loading indicator for short waits, like inside a button or beside some text. For loading a larger area, use a skeleton instead. Also called: spinner, loader, throbber, loading-ring.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-spinner` — The ring, 1.25em (matches an icon beside text), in the current text colour. Spins; stops still under reduced motion.
- `.ayy-spinner--sm` — 16px (--ayy-size-icon-sm).
- `.ayy-spinner--lg` — 32px (--ayy-size-icon-xl), for a panel that's loading.

**States**
- `loading` (`always (it is the loading state); give it role="status" and a label, or aria-hidden inside a busy Button`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — 16px (--ayy-size-icon-sm).
- `md` (default) — 1.25em, matching an icon beside text.
- `lg` — 32px (--ayy-size-icon-xl), 3px ring.
- Density — Doesn't follow data-density; md follows the font size around it.
- Width — Square.

**React** — `import { Spinner } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Spinner>` renders <span class="ayy-spinner" role="status" aria-label="Loading">. Props: `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg"; `label` What's loading, for screen readers. Default "Loading" (translate it). "" makes it decorative (aria-hidden) when nearby text already says it.

**Accessibility**
- A spinner on its own is a role="status" with an aria-label that says what's loading ("Loading invoices").
- Inside a button, hide it (aria-hidden) and set aria-busy="true" on the button; the button's text still names it.
- Mark the region that's refreshing with aria-busy="true" until the new content is in.
- Under reduced motion it stops as a still ring; the label and aria-busy still say it's working.

**Do**
- Use a spinner for waits under a few seconds on a small area: a button that's saving, a panel refreshing, a lazy menu.
- Put it inside the button that started the work (<Button loading>), not somewhere else on the page.
- Pair a large spinner with a line of text when the wait may be longer ("Importing 2,400 contacts…").

**Examples**: Sizes and a loading button. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/spinner.md.

## Skeleton

Category: Feedback. A placeholder shaped like the content that's loading, so the page doesn't jump when the real content arrives. Also called: skeleton, shimmer.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-skeleton` — Block placeholder. Set its size to match the content.
- `.ayy-skeleton--text` — Text line (0.75em tall).
- `.ayy-skeleton--circle` — Circle (avatars, icons).

**States**
- `loading` (`always; set aria-busy="true" on the region it fills and aria-hidden on the skeletons`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Doesn't follow data-density.
- Width — Size it like the content it stands in for. block fills the width at 1rem tall; text is 0.75em tall; circle is 2.5rem (an avatar).

**React** — `import { Skeleton } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Skeleton>` renders <div aria-hidden="true">. Props: `shape` "block" | "text" | "circle"

**Accessibility**
- Skeletons are aria-hidden. Put aria-busy="true" on the container while loading, and remove it when content arrives. To name the loading region, give it role="status" and an aria-label — aria-label on a plain div is ignored.
- The shimmer stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

**Do**
- Use a skeleton for content that takes more than ~300ms and has a predictable layout (cards, lists, profile headers).
- Match the real layout closely so nothing jumps when content arrives.

**Examples**: Loading card. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/skeleton.md.

## Empty state

Category: Feedback. What a list, table or page shows when it has nothing to display yet, or nothing matches a search. It explains why it's empty and offers the action that fills it. Also called: empty-state, empty, blank-slate, no-results.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-empty-state` — Root. Centred column with generous block padding.
- `.ayy-empty-state--bordered` — A dashed outline around the empty area (a board column, a drop target).
- `.ayy-empty-state--compact` — Less padding: inside a card, a table body or a side panel.
- `.ayy-empty-state__title` — What's empty, as a heading ("No projects yet").
- `.ayy-empty-state__description` — One sentence: why it's empty, or what will appear here.
- `.ayy-empty-state__actions` — The button that fixes it (primary), maybe a secondary link.

**Sizes**
- Density — Doesn't follow data-density.
- Width — Fills its container. compact has less padding (in a card, table cell or sidebar); bordered adds a dashed card outline for an area that will hold content.

**React** — `import { EmptyState, EmptyStateTitle, EmptyStateDescription, EmptyStateActions } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<EmptyState>` renders <div class="ayy-empty-state">. Props: `bordered` boolean — dashed outline.; `compact` boolean — less padding.
- `<EmptyStateTitle>` renders <h2 class="ayy-empty-state__title">.
- `<EmptyStateDescription>` renders <p class="ayy-empty-state__description">.
- `<EmptyStateActions>` renders <div class="ayy-empty-state__actions">.

**Accessibility**
- The title is a real heading at the level that fits the page (h2 under the page's h1, h3 inside a card).
- The icon tile is decorative: the title carries the meaning.
- When results change because of a search or filter, put the empty state inside a role="status" region (or announce the count) so screen reader users hear that nothing matched.

**Do**
- Use an empty state wherever a list, table or page can have nothing in it: first run, a finished inbox, a search with no results.
- Say what will be here and give the one action that fills it (Create project, Import contacts, Clear filters).
- Use the compact version inside a Card or a Table's body; the full one when it's the whole page.
- Match the icon to the thing that's missing, in an IconTile.

**Examples**: First run, No results, compact. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/empty-state.md.

## Badge

Category: Data display. A small label that marks the status, category or count of something, like "New" or "Paid". It can include a status dot for things that are live. Also called: badge, pill, status-pill, count-badge.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-badge` — Root. Neutral by default.
- `.ayy-badge--muted` — Quieter neutral.
- `.ayy-badge--outline` — Border only.
- `.ayy-badge--success` — Positive status.
- `.ayy-badge--warning` — Caution status.
- `.ayy-badge--destructive` — Error / failed.
- `.ayy-badge--info` — Informational.
- `.ayy-badge--ai` — AI-related.
- `.ayy-badge__dot` — Leading status dot (first child). Pulses. Colour follows the variant, or set --ayy-dot.
- `.ayy-badge__dot--static` — Dot without the pulse.

**States**
- `error` (`destructive (ayy-badge--destructive)`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Text size follows data-density via --ayy-text-s.
- Width — Hugs its text, never wraps.

**React** — `import { Badge } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Badge>` renders <span>. Props: `variant` "default" | "muted" | "outline" | "success" | "warning" | "destructive" | "info" | "ai"; `dot` boolean | "pulse" | "static" — leading status dot

**Accessibility**
- Colour is never the only signal — the label text must say the status.
- The dot is aria-hidden; it's decorative.

**Do**
- Use a badge for the status of an item (Synced, Error, Beta), a category or tag next to a title, or a live indicator (dot).
- Keep labels to one or two words.
- Use the status variants for status, accent spotlights for categories.

**Examples**: Variants, Status dot. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/badge.md.

## Status dot

Category: Data display. A small coloured dot that shows the state of something, like someone being online, a live stream or a server's health. Also called: status-dot, status-indicator, presence-dot, live-dot, health-dot.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-status-dot` — Root inline-flex dot.
- `.ayy-status-dot--sm` — Small dot (6px).
- `.ayy-status-dot--lg` — Large dot (10px).
- `.ayy-status-dot--neutral` — Muted status dot (var(--ayy-color-muted)).
- `.ayy-status-dot--success` — Green status dot (var(--ayy-color-success)).
- `.ayy-status-dot--warning` — Amber status dot (var(--ayy-color-warning)).
- `.ayy-status-dot--destructive` — Red status dot (var(--ayy-color-destructive)).
- `.ayy-status-dot--info` — Blue status dot (var(--ayy-color-info)).
- `.ayy-status-dot--pulse` — Animated pinging ring for live/active statuses (keyframes ayy-status-dot-ping).

**Sizes**
- `sm` — 6px diameter for dense table rows or nested badges.
- `md` (default) — 8px diameter standard dot for status rows and presence.
- `lg` — 10px diameter prominent dot for live indicators and headers.
- Density — Fixed dot dimensions (6px, 8px, or 10px); does not scale with data-density.
- Width — Fixed square footprint matching dot dimensions.

**React** — `import { StatusDot } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<StatusDot>` renders <span>. Props: `variant` "neutral" | "success" | "warning" | "destructive" | "info"; `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg"; `pulse` boolean — animated pinging ring for live/active status; `label` string — accessible label (sets role="status" and aria-label; without it, aria-hidden="true")

**Accessibility**
- Colour is never the only signal — accompany standalone status dots with a text label or pass the label prop so screen readers announce it.
- When label is provided, sets role="status" and aria-label; when omitted, aria-hidden="true" treats the dot as decorative.

**Do**
- Use a status dot to indicate online presence, server or service health, or active streaming status.
- Place the status dot beside a descriptive label or table cell value.
- Use the pulse modifier for active or real-time statuses like live streams or ongoing recordings.

**Examples**: Variants, Live pulsing. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/status-dot.md.

## Keyboard hint

Category: Data display. A small keycap for showing a keyboard key or shortcut in help text, menus and tooltips. Shortcuts adapt to the platform, so Mac users see their own symbols. Also called: kbd, keyboard-hint, keycap, hotkey, shortcut-key.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-kbd` — The <kbd>: monospace, 0.75em of the surrounding text, a hairline border with a heavier bottom edge.

**Sizes**
- Density — Scales with the text around it (1.6em tall); scales when surrounding text uses --ayy-text-s.
- Width — At least 1.6em wide, grows with the key name.

**React** — `import { Kbd, KeyboardHint } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Kbd>` renders <kbd class="ayy-kbd">. Props: `keyName` string — a modifier or key drawn for the platform ("mod", "meta", "alt", "ctrl", "shift", "enter", "backspace"). Symbols get an aria-label with the key's name. The server and first render draw Windows names, then the user's platform.; `platform` "mac" | "windows" | "linux" — force a target platform instead of detecting it
- `<KeyboardHint>` renders <kbd class="ayy-kbd">. Props: `keyName` string — optional modifier/key name to adapt ("mod", "meta", "alt", "ctrl", "shift"); `platform` "mac" | "windows" | "linux" — force a target platform instead of detecting it

**Accessibility**
- Use the <kbd> element: screen readers and search know it's a key.
- Write modifier names out where symbols may not read well ("Ctrl" rather than "^"), or add aria-label="Command K" to a <kbd>⌘K</kbd> (screen readers pronounce "⌘" as "place of interest sign").
- A shortcut hint doesn't replace aria-keyshortcuts on the control it triggers.

**Do**
- Use a kbd for keys people press: "Press / to search", shortcuts in a menu or tooltip, a hint in a search field (InputGroupAddon).
- Use one kbd for a whole shortcut (⌘K), or one per key with a plus between them (Ctrl + Shift + P).
- Adapt modifiers to the user's OS: ⌘ / ⌥ / ⇧ / ⌃ on macOS, Ctrl / Alt / Shift / Win on Windows, and Ctrl / Alt / Shift / Super on Linux (or use <Shortcut keys="Mod+K" /> / <Kbd keyName="mod" />).
- Listen to event.code (physical key like 'KeyE') or use matchShortcut(event, 'Mod+E') rather than event.key === 'e' so hotkeys work across keyboard layouts and languages (e.g. Russian Cyrillic Cmd+У).

**Examples**: Shortcuts in text, Platform adaptation (macOS, Windows, Linux), Multi-language hotkey handling. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/kbd.md.

## Text highlight

Category: Data display. A way to mark text inside a sentence, for search matches or phrases that need attention. It's subtle by default, with colour variants for warnings, errors, successes and info. Also called: text-highlight, highlight, mark, search-highlight.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-text-highlight` — Inline highlighted span or <mark>: subtle gray wash with clean underline.
- `.ayy-text-highlight--warning` — Amber/yellow tint for cautions and warnings.
- `.ayy-text-highlight--destructive` — Red tint for errors and danger callouts.
- `.ayy-text-highlight--success` — Green tint for positive results or matches.
- `.ayy-text-highlight--info` — Blue tint for informational emphasis.
- `.ayy-text-highlight--orange` — Orange tint for spotlight callouts.

**Sizes**
- Density — Follows the text it wraps.
- Width — Inline, wraps with text.

**React** — `import { TextHighlight } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<TextHighlight>` renders <mark class="ayy-text-highlight">. Props: `text` string — text to search and highlight within (or provide as string children); `query` string — search substring or space-separated words to highlight; `variant` "default" | "warning" | "destructive" | "success" | "info" | "orange" — highlight tint colour; `as` ElementType — HTML tag (defaults to mark for callouts, Fragment for queries)

**Accessibility**
- Uses the standard <mark> HTML tag for search and text highlights, recognised by assistive technology.
- Maintains readable contrast across light, dark, and high-contrast themes via color-mix() and light-dark().
- Under Windows High Contrast mode (forced-colors), highlights switch to the system Highlight and HighlightText colours.

**Do**
- Use TextHighlight to show matched search terms in command palettes, comboboxes, and search results.
- Use the default subtle gray highlight with underline for search results so text remains calm and readable.
- Use color variants (warning/yellow, destructive/red, success/green, info, orange) for specific semantic callouts.

**Examples**: Search match and callout, Semantic color variants (yellow, red, green, blue, orange). Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/text-highlight.md.

## Avatar

Category: Data display. A small picture that stands for a person or a workspace. When there's no image, or it fails to load, it shows initials instead. Also called: avatar, profile-pic, user-pic.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-avatar` — Root (role="img" + aria-label). 32px circle.
- `.ayy-avatar--sm` — 24px.
- `.ayy-avatar--lg` — 40px.
- `.ayy-avatar--xl` — 56px.
- `.ayy-avatar--square` — Rounded square (workspaces, teams).
- `.ayy-avatar__fallback` — Initials, underneath the image.
- `.ayy-avatar__image` — The <img alt="">. Covers the initials when it loads.
- `.ayy-avatar-group` — Overlapping stack of avatars.

**States**
- `error` (`a broken image (React and @danitesler/ayywi/elements set hidden on it)`)

**Sizes**
- `sm` — 1.5rem (24px).
- `md` (default) — 2rem (32px).
- `lg` — 2.5rem (40px).
- `xl` — 3.5rem (56px).
- Density — Doesn't follow data-density. Initials are 38% of the size.
- Width — Square. A group overlaps them by 20% with a page-colour ring.

**React** — `import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Avatar>` renders <span role="img">. Props: `name` string (required) — accessible name and initials; `src` string — image URL; `fallback` string — custom initials; `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"; `shape` "circle" | "square"
- `<AvatarGroup>` renders <div role="group">.

**Accessibility**
- The name goes on the root (aria-label); the <img> has alt="" and the initials are aria-hidden, so it's announced once.
- Give an AvatarGroup an aria-label like "5 collaborators".
- A failed image is hidden by React or @danitesler/ayywi/elements so the initials show. With CSS alone it renders as a plain disc.

**Do**
- Use avatars for people and workspaces in lists, headers and comments.
- Use AvatarGroup for a stack of collaborators: show at most 4–5 and a "+3" badge for the rest.

**Examples**: Sizes, Fallback, Group. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/avatar.md.

## Icon

Category: Data display. A single icon from the Hugeicons library that ayywi uses. It follows the colour and size of the text around it. Also called: svg-icon.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-icon` — On the <svg>. 1.25em square, so it follows the surrounding text; centred on capital letters; never shrinks in a flex row.
- `.ayy-icon--sm` — 16px (--ayy-size-icon-sm).
- `.ayy-icon--md` — 20px (--ayy-size-icon-md).
- `.ayy-icon--lg` — 24px, Hugeicons' native grid (--ayy-size-icon-lg).
- `.ayy-icon--xl` — 32px (--ayy-size-icon-xl).
- `.ayy-icon--directional` — Mirrors the icon in right-to-left text (the nearest dir attribute decides). For icons that point along the reading direction: arrows, chevrons, send, undo.

**Sizes**
- `auto` (default) — 1.25em: follows the text size.
- `sm` — 16px (--ayy-size-icon-sm).
- `md` — 20px.
- `lg` — 24px.
- `xl` — 32px.
- Density — Default 1.25em scales with surrounding text including --ayy-text-s; inside buttons, menu items and alerts the component sets the size.
- Width — Square. directional mirrors it in RTL.

**React** — `import { Icon } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react"; import { Search01Icon } from "@hugeicons/core-free-icons";`
- `<Icon>` renders <svg class="ayy-icon">. Props: `icon` IconData (required) — any icon from @hugeicons/core-free-icons or a Hugeicons Pro package; `size` "auto" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" — auto follows the text; the rest are 16/20/24/32px; `directional` boolean — mirror in right-to-left text; for arrows and other icons that point along the reading direction; `label` string — accessible name; without it the icon is decorative (aria-hidden); `strokeWidth` number — stroke width on the 24px grid (Hugeicons default 1.5)

**Accessibility**
- Icons are decorative by default (aria-hidden): the text next to them carries the meaning.
- When the icon is the only thing saying something (a status, a verified mark), give it a label: <Icon label="Deployed">, or role="img" + aria-label on the <svg>.
- Icon-only buttons: aria-label goes on the button, the icon stays decorative.
- Strokes use currentColor, so icons follow the theme and Windows High Contrast colours with no extra CSS.

**Do**
- Use an icon next to its text to help people recognise an action or item: buttons, menu items, list rows.
- Use an icon with an accessible label for compact status where a word would be too long.
- Import icons one by one from @hugeicons/core-free-icons; named imports tree-shake.
- Let the component size icons inside buttons, menu items and alerts; use size for icons on their own.
- Colour an icon through its text colour: .ayy-muted, or color: var(--ayy-color-success) on the <svg>.
- Mark icons that point along the reading direction (arrows, chevrons, send, undo) directional so they mirror in RTL. Leave the rest alone: a clock or a check mark reads the same both ways.

**Examples**: Sizes, Decorative and meaningful, Directional icons in RTL. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/icon.md.

## Icon tile

Category: Data display. A rounded app-icon tile that gives a product, plugin or service a recognisable mark, with the glyph tinted in its accent colour. Also called: icon-tile, app-icon.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-icon-tile` — Root, usually a <span> around one <svg> drawn in currentColor. 48px. Accent from --ayy-spot.
- `.ayy-icon-tile--sm` — 32px.
- `.ayy-icon-tile--lg` — 64px.

**Sizes**
- `sm` — 32px, lg radius.
- `md` (default) — 48px, xl radius.
- `lg` — 64px, 2xl radius.
- Density — Doesn't follow data-density.
- Width — Square; the glyph is 55% of it.

**React** — `import { IconTile } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<IconTile>` renders <span class="ayy-icon-tile">. Props: `size` "sm" | "md" | "lg"; `spotColor` CSS colour for the glow and glyph, e.g. "var(--ayy-accent-system)". Else inherits --ayy-spot.; `aria-label` Makes the tile an image with this name; without it the tile is aria-hidden.

**Accessibility**
- Usually decorative next to the product's name: aria-hidden="true" (React does this unless you pass aria-label).
- Standing alone, give it role="img" and an aria-label.

**Do**
- Use an icon tile for the icon of a product, plugin, platform or service in a card or list row.
- Draw glyphs in currentColor so they take the accent; brand marks with their own colours can keep them.
- Use one accent per product and reuse it wherever that product appears.

**Examples**: Accents and sizes. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/icon-tile.md.

## Stat

Category: Data display. A big number with a short label, for headline figures like downloads, views or revenue. Also called: stat, metric, kpi, stat-card.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-stat` — Root.
- `.ayy-stat--sm` — Smaller number (28px instead of 48px), for rows of several stats or inside cards.
- `.ayy-stat__value` — The number, pre-formatted ("4.2k"). Tabular figures.
- `.ayy-stat__unit` — Muted word after the number, inside the value.
- `.ayy-stat__label` — Short context, above or below the value.

**Sizes**
- `md` (default) — Value at 4xl (3rem).
- `sm` — Value at 2xl (1.75rem), for cards and dense dashboards.
- Density — Doesn't follow data-density.
- Width — Hugs its content; the value wraps its unit below when narrow.

**React** — `import { Stat } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Stat>` renders <div class="ayy-stat">. Props: `value` ReactNode (required) — the formatted number.; `unit` ReactNode; `label` ReactNode; `labelFirst` boolean — label above the number.; `size` "md" | "sm"

**Accessibility**
- Write abbreviations the way they should be read, or add the full number: <span aria-hidden="true">200k</span><span class="ayy-sr-only">200,000</span>.
- Keep the unit as text, not only an icon.

**Do**
- Use a stat to show a result or reach at a glance: "200k downloads", "+34% conversion".
- Line several up with .ayy-grid or .ayy-cluster for the key numbers in a case study or dashboard header.
- Format the number before it gets here (4.2k, 87%).

**Examples**: Row of stats. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/stat.md.

## List

Category: Data display. Rows of people, records or settings, each with an image or icon, a title, a description and something at the end like a value or a control. A row can be a link. Also called: list-item, list-row.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-list` — Root <ul>. Rounded rows with a small gap between them.
- `.ayy-list--divided` — Flush rows with hairlines between them: settings rows, records inside a card.
- `.ayy-list--compact` — Tight rows without padding and a small icon: an icon checklist (plan perks, what's included, requirements). Rows here usually hold an Icon and plain text.
- `.ayy-list__item` — The <li> row: a flex row of leading media, __content and trailing items, vertically centred. Everything but __content keeps its size.
- `.ayy-list__content` — The column that holds __title and __description; it takes the free space and can shrink (add .ayy-truncate to cut long text).
- `.ayy-list__title` — The row's main text, medium weight. Holds the __link when the row opens something.
- `.ayy-list__description` — Supporting text under the title, muted.
- `.ayy-list__meta` — Short trailing text: a time, a count, a size. Small, muted, tabular numbers.
- `.ayy-list__link` — The <a> inside __title. Its ::after covers the row, so the whole row is one tab stop; other controls in the row stay clickable above it. The row gets a wash on hover, a ring on focus, and a stronger tint and heavier title with aria-current="page" (or "true").

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-list__item:has(.ayy-list__link):hover`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-list__item:has(.ayy-list__link:focus-visible)`)
- `selected` (`.ayy-list__item:has(.ayy-list__link[aria-current="page" | "true"])`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Padding and sm text are fixed; row meta text follows data-density via --ayy-text-s; controls in rows follow data-density.
- Width — Fills its container; titles and descriptions wrap, meta stays on one line.

**React** — `import { List, ListItem, ListContent, ListTitle, ListDescription, ListMeta, ListLink } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<List>` renders <ul class="ayy-list">. Props: `divided` boolean — hairlines between flush rows.; `compact` boolean — tight rows for an icon checklist.
- `<ListItem>` renders <li class="ayy-list__item">.
- `<ListContent>` renders <div class="ayy-list__content">.
- `<ListTitle>` renders <p class="ayy-list__title">, or <label> with htmlFor. Props: `htmlFor` The id of the row's Switch or Checkbox: the title becomes its <label>.
- `<ListDescription>` renders <p class="ayy-list__description">.
- `<ListMeta>` renders <span class="ayy-list__meta">.
- `<ListLink>` renders <a class="ayy-list__link">. Props: `current` boolean — sets aria-current="page".

**Accessibility**
- It's a real list: screen readers announce how many rows there are.
- One link per row, in the title, so a row is one tab stop with a meaningful name. Buttons and switches in the row are separate tab stops after it.
- Mark the open row with aria-current="page" (it's a page) or "true" (a selection in a list-detail view); it gets a tint and a heavier title, not just colour.
- A switch or checkbox in a settings row needs its label: make the title a <label for> pointing at it.
- Avatars and icons in the leading slot are decorative when the title names the row.

**Do**
- Use a list for a feed of similar things people scan and open: conversations, notifications, files, members, search results.
- Use List divided for settings: a title and description per row, the Switch or Button at the end.
- Use List compact for a short checklist with an icon per row: plan perks, what's included, password rules.
- Keep the same slots on every row: if one row has an avatar, they all do.
- Put the time or count in ListMeta, and a status in a Badge at the end.
- Cut long descriptions to one line with .ayy-truncate in inboxes and pickers.

**Examples**: Conversations, Settings rows. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/list.md.

## Property list

Category: Data display. A record's attributes as a definition list: a muted term (an icon and a label) and its value, side by side, wrapping under each other when the value doesn't fit. Also called: property-list, description-list, key-value, details-list, metadata-list.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-property-list` — Root <dl>. Rows stack with no gap; the rows own the padding.
- `.ayy-property-list--compact` — Tight rows: 6px block padding instead of 12px and a 7rem term basis instead of 8rem.
- `.ayy-property-list__row` — The <div> that holds one <dt> and one <dd>: a wrapping flex row with the term at an 8rem basis and the value taking the rest.
- `.ayy-property-list__term` — The <dt>: a decorative icon and the label, at an 8rem basis and in --ayy-color-muted. The term never grows; the value takes the remaining width.
- `.ayy-property-list__label` — The label inside the term. Wraps inside the term's column.
- `.ayy-property-list__icon` — An optional Icon before the label: 16px, muted, never shrinks. Decorative, so the label names the row.
- `.ayy-property-list__value` — The <dd>: the value in --ayy-color-text. Long words wrap inside it (overflow-wrap: anywhere) instead of overflowing.
- `.ayy-property-list__empty` — What an empty value reads ("Not set"): muted, in place of the value.

**States**
- `empty` (`PropertyRow empty (emptyText, default "Not set")`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Row text follows data-density through --ayy-text-s (13px compact and comfortable, 14px touch). compact swaps the 12px block padding for 6px.
- Width — Fills its container. The term takes an 8rem basis (7rem compact) and the value 10rem; when they don't fit together the value wraps under its term. Long unbroken values wrap inside the value.

**React** — `import { PropertyList, PropertyRow } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<PropertyList>` renders <dl class="ayy-property-list">. Props: `compact` boolean — tight rows with a shorter term column, for a dense summary.
- `<PropertyRow>` renders <div class="ayy-property-list__row"> <dt class="ayy-property-list__term"> (icon and label) <dd class="ayy-property-list__value">. Props: `label` ReactNode (required) — the term's text.; `icon` ReactNode — an Icon before the label (give it className="ayy-property-list__icon").; `empty` boolean — there is no value: show emptyText muted instead of children.; `emptyText` ReactNode — what an empty value reads. Default "Not set".

**Accessibility**
- It's a real <dl>: screen readers announce a definition list and pair each term with its value.
- Each row is a <div> inside the <dl> (valid HTML) with exactly one <dt> and one <dd>, so the rows can wrap and flex.
- Icons in the term are decorative; the label names the row.
- An empty value says "Not set" in text, not a dash or a blank cell.
- A value edited in place keeps the nested InlineEdit's own label ("Change the version"); the term names the attribute, the control names the action.

**Do**
- Use a property list for a record's attributes: a project, a server, an order, a person.
- Keep terms short and values plain; nest a control only for a value edited in place.
- Use PropertyRow empty and emptyText when there is no value, so the row stays and reads as empty.
- Use compact inside a card header or a dense summary.

**Examples**: Record, Compact. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/property-list.md.

## Swipe actions

Category: Data display. A list row that slides sideways to reveal actions, the way phone mail and task apps do. It works with touch, mouse and keyboard, and follows the reading direction. Also called: swipe, swipe-row, swipeable, swipe-actions, slide-actions.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-swipe` — The row: clips its content and holds the trays. Vertical drags still scroll the page (touch-action: pan-y).
- `.ayy-swipe__content` — What slides: the row's own content (often with .ayy-list__item). Opaque, with --ayy-swipe-bg (default the page colour) so the trays stay hidden under it.
- `.ayy-swipe__actions` — A tray of buttons under the row, after the content in the DOM. Shows over the row while it holds keyboard focus.
- `.ayy-swipe__actions--start` — At the inline start: revealed by swiping toward the inline end (right in English). One positive action (Done, Read).
- `.ayy-swipe__actions--end` — At the inline end: revealed by swiping toward the inline start. Up to three (Pin, Snooze, Delete), the destructive one last.
- `.ayy-swipe__action` — A <button> filling the tray's height: an icon over a short label, on a tint of its colour.
- `.ayy-swipe__action--primary` — Solid primary fill.
- `.ayy-swipe__action--success` — Green tint (Done).
- `.ayy-swipe__action--warning` — Amber tint (Snooze).
- `.ayy-swipe__action--info` — Blue tint (Move, Label).
- `.ayy-swipe__action--destructive` — Red tint (Delete).

**States**
- `focus` (`.ayy-swipe__action:focus-visible; .ayy-swipe__actions:has(:focus-visible)`)
- `open` (`[data-open="start"] or [data-open="end"], set by the script`)
- `dragging` (`[data-dragging]`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Actions are at least 4.5rem wide and as tall as the row; the row keeps its own density.
- Width — Fills the list's width, like the row it wraps.

**Custom element** `<ayy-swipe>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — 
- event `ayy-open-change`: { side } — "start", "end" or null when the row closes.

**React** — `import { Swipe, SwipeAction } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Swipe>` renders <div class="ayy-swipe"><div class="ayy-swipe__content">{children}</div> trays…</div>. Props: `startActions` ReactNode — SwipeActions revealed by swiping toward the inline end; `endActions` ReactNode — SwipeActions revealed by swiping toward the inline start; `onOpenChange` (side: "start" | "end" | null) => void; `contentProps` HTMLAttributes — props for the sliding content (className="ayy-list__item")
- `<SwipeAction>` renders <button type="button" class="ayy-swipe__action">. Props: `variant` "default" | "primary" | "success" | "warning" | "info" | "destructive"; `icon` ReactNode — an Icon above the label

**Accessibility**
- Swiping is a shortcut, never the only way: offer the same actions in the row's page or a Menu, since many people can't or don't swipe.
- The actions are real buttons after the content in the tab order; a tray with focus shows over the row, and Esc closes an open row.
- Labels stay visible under the icons, so the tint isn't the only cue.
- Undo destructive actions (a Toast with Undo) rather than asking for confirmation in the middle of a gesture.

**Do**
- Use it on phone lists for the two or three things people do to rows most: Done, Snooze, Delete.
- Put the positive action at the start and the destructive one last at the end, as mail apps do.
- Set --ayy-swipe-bg to the surface the list sits on (a card) so the row hides its trays.

**Examples**: Task rows: Done, Pin, Snooze, Delete. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/swipe.md.

## Timeline

Category: Data display. A list of events in time order, like a history, a changelog or a project's milestones, joined by a vertical line with status markers and timestamps. Also called: timeline, event-log, activity-feed, history-feed, audit-trail.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-timeline` — Root <ol> or <ul> list container for ordered events or history.
- `.ayy-timeline--alternate` — Alternates timeline items between start and end sides across a centered vertical track.
- `.ayy-timeline__item` — Single event entry row containing the track and content.
- `.ayy-timeline__track` — Vertical connecting rail line between items with the marker positioned along it.
- `.ayy-timeline__marker` — Circle dot, icon or avatar placed on the track representing the event anchor point.
- `.ayy-timeline__marker--pulse` — Pulsing active status ring indicating a current, in-progress or live event.
- `.ayy-timeline__content` — Container holding the event details (time, title, body).
- `.ayy-timeline__time` — Muted timestamp or date with tabular numbers.
- `.ayy-timeline__title` — Heading or summary of the event.
- `.ayy-timeline__body` — Supporting text, description, or status badge for the event.

**States**
- `pulse` (`ayy-timeline__marker--pulse`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Markers and spacing are fixed; timestamp text follows data-density via --ayy-text-s; controls or badges inside event content follow data-density.
- Width — Fills its container. In alternate mode, centers the track with 1fr columns on either side above 36rem, collapsing to a single start-aligned column below 36rem.

**React** — `import { Timeline, TimelineItem, TimelineMarker, TimelineContent, TimelineTime, TimelineTitle, TimelineBody } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Timeline>` renders <ol class="ayy-timeline">. Props: `alternate` boolean — alternate items between start and end sides across a centered vertical track.
- `<TimelineItem>` renders <li class="ayy-timeline__item">. Props: `marker` ReactNode — the marker dot, icon or avatar placed on the track.
- `<TimelineMarker>` renders <span class="ayy-timeline__marker">. Props: `pulse` boolean — pulsing active status ring for in-progress or live events.
- `<TimelineContent>` renders <div class="ayy-timeline__content">.
- `<TimelineTime>` renders <time class="ayy-timeline__time">.
- `<TimelineTitle>` renders <div class="ayy-timeline__title">.
- `<TimelineBody>` renders <div class="ayy-timeline__body">.

**Accessibility**
- Rendered as an ordered list (<ol>) by default so screen readers announce the item count and sequence.
- Timestamps use the semantic <time> element with tabular numbers for consistent alignment and screen reader comprehension.
- Decorative markers and track lines are marked aria-hidden="true" to prevent screen reader noise; important status information should be in the title or body.
- Active pulse rings are visual enhancements; screen readers receive the active status via text in the title, body, or an accessible badge.
- Supports Windows High Contrast mode via @media (forced-colors: active) with system CanvasText, Canvas, and Highlight colors.

**Do**
- Use a timeline to show a chronological log or sequence of events: deploy history, shipment tracking, audit trails, activity feeds.
- Use TimelineMarker pulse on the latest or currently active event in a running process.
- Use Timeline alternate for milestones, company history, or changelogs on wide marketing or overview pages.
- Include TimelineTime with a semantic timestamp so users can anchor events in time.
- Keep markers consistent within a timeline: all dots, or all icons, or all avatars.

**Examples**: Deployment history, Alternating product milestones. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/timeline.md.

## Frame

Category: Data display. A browser window drawn around a screenshot, a video or a demo, for showing a product in context on marketing pages and in docs. Also called: browser-frame, window-frame, mockup.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-frame` — Root: bordered, rounded, with the frame shadow.
- `.ayy-frame__bar` — Top bar with the three window dots.
- `.ayy-frame__title` — Optional address or page name in the bar, centred.
- `.ayy-frame__body` — Holds the <img>, <video>, <picture> or <svg>, edge to edge.

**Sizes**
- Density — Title text follows data-density via --ayy-text-s; window geometry is fixed.
- Width — Fills its container; the media inside scales to its width.

**React** — `import { Frame } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Frame>` renders <div class="ayy-frame"> with the bar and body. Props: `title` ReactNode — text in the address bar.

**Accessibility**
- The screenshot is the content: give the <img> alt text that says what it shows, or wrap the frame in a <figure> with a <figcaption>.
- The dots are decoration (a pseudo-element).

**Do**
- Use a frame to show product screens in a case study, landing page or portfolio card, so they read as product and not decoration.
- Give images width and height so the frame keeps its size while loading.
- Blur real names and customer data in production screenshots, and say so in the caption.

**Examples**: Screenshot in a window. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/frame.md.

## Chat

Category: Data display. The layout of a conversation, with other people's messages on one side and the reader's own on the other. It includes a typing indicator and quick-reply buttons, for assistants and support chats. Also called: chat, bubble, message-bubble.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-chat` — Root. role="log" when messages arrive live, so they're announced.
- `.ayy-chat__message` — One message row: an optional avatar and its bubble.
- `.ayy-chat__message--out` — Sent by the reader: end edge, primary colours.
- `.ayy-chat__bubble` — The bubble. The corner by the avatar is squared off.
- `.ayy-chat__typing` — Three pulsing dots inside a bubble while a reply is written. Give it role="img" and an aria-label.
- `.ayy-chat__replies` — Quick replies under the conversation: small outline buttons, at the end edge.

**States**
- `loading` (`.ayy-chat__typing inside a bubble`)

**Sizes**
- Density — sm text; doesn't follow data-density.
- Width — Fills its container; bubbles wrap and break long words.

**React** — `import { Chat, ChatMessage, ChatTyping, ChatReplies } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Chat>` renders <div role="log" class="ayy-chat">.
- `<ChatMessage>` renders <div class="ayy-chat__message"> with the avatar and a bubble around children. Props: `direction` "in" | "out"; `avatar` ReactNode — e.g. an Avatar size sm.
- `<ChatTyping>` renders A message whose bubble holds the typing dots. Props: `label` Screen-reader text. Default "Typing" (translate it).; `avatar` ReactNode
- `<ChatReplies>` renders <div class="ayy-chat__replies">.

**Accessibility**
- Use role="log" on the conversation when messages arrive while the reader watches; they're announced politely, in order.
- The typing dots are an image with a name ("Dani is typing"); remove the element when the message lands.
- Quick replies are real buttons; after one is chosen, move focus to the next sensible place, not back to the top.

**Do**
- Use chat for AI assistants and agents, and for support or feedback widgets.
- On a marketing page, use it for a scripted "say hi" section that hands off to email or LinkedIn.
- Keep bubbles short; split long answers into several messages.
- Pair incoming messages with the sender's avatar the first time.

**Examples**: Conversation with quick replies. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/chat.md.

## Code block

Category: Data display. A container for showing code, with a header, a file name, a copy button and optional line numbers. It styles syntax highlighting without tying you to a particular highlighter. Also called: code-block, codeblock, syntax-highlighter, code-snippet, code-view, code-box.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-code-block` — Bordered container for code with rounded corners and surface background.
- `.ayy-code-block--numbered` — Adds line numbers using CSS counters.
- `.ayy-code-block__header` — Top toolbar with filename and copy button.
- `.ayy-code-block__filename` — File title, path, or language indicator.
- `.ayy-code-block__actions` — Container for header controls such as language selector and copy button.
- `.ayy-code-block__selector` — Language selector trigger button in the top toolbar.
- `.ayy-code-block__chevron` — Chevron icon inside the language selector button.
- `.ayy-code-block__menu` — Dropdown menu listing supported languages for the code block.
- `.ayy-code-block__copy` — Copy button with icon, copied feedback, and tooltip.
- `.ayy-code-block__pre` — Scrollable preformatted text container.
- `.ayy-code-block__code` — Code element with monospace font and preformatted whitespace.
- `.ayy-code-block__line` — Line wrapper inside the code element; receives line numbers when numbered.
- `.ayy-token-keyword` — Syntax token for language keywords.
- `.ayy-token-string` — Syntax token for string literals.
- `.ayy-token-comment` — Syntax token for comments.
- `.ayy-token-function` — Syntax token for function and method names.
- `.ayy-token-number` — Syntax token for numeric literals.
- `.ayy-token-operator` — Syntax token for operators and punctuation.
- `.ayy-token-tag` — Syntax token for HTML/JSX element tags.
- `.ayy-token-attribute` — Syntax token for HTML attributes and JSX props.
- `.ayy-token-property` — Syntax token for object keys and CSS properties.
- `.ayy-token-punctuation` — Syntax token for punctuation, braces, and delimiters.
- `.ayy-token-boolean` — Syntax token for boolean literals and nullish values.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-code-block__copy:hover, .ayy-code-block__selector:hover`)
- `pressed` (`.ayy-code-block__copy:active`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-code-block__copy:focus-visible, .ayy-code-block__selector:focus-visible`)
- `copied` (`.ayy-code-block__copy[data-copied="true"]`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Padding and copy button follow data-density.
- Width — Fills its container width; code pre scrolls horizontally when lines overflow.

**React** — `import { CodeBlock, CodeBlockHeader, CodeBlockFilename, CodeBlockActions, CodeBlockSelector, CodeBlockCopy, CodeBlockPre, CodeBlockCode } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<CodeBlock>` renders <div class="ayy-code-block">. Props: `numbered` boolean — display line numbers with CSS counters
- `<CodeBlockHeader>` renders <div class="ayy-code-block__header">. Props: 
- `<CodeBlockFilename>` renders <span class="ayy-code-block__filename">. Props: 
- `<CodeBlockActions>` renders <div class="ayy-code-block__actions">. Props: 
- `<CodeBlockSelector>` renders <button class="ayy-code-block__selector"> and <div class="ayy-menu ayy-code-block__menu">. Props: `value` string — currently selected language ID; `defaultValue` string — initial language ID when uncontrolled; `onValueChange` (value: string) => void — callback fired when a language is selected; `onChange` (event: { target: { value: string } }) => void — change event handler for compatibility; `languages` LanguagePreset[] — optional array of languages to populate options; defaults to SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES; `className` string — additional CSS class names for the trigger button; `disabled` boolean — whether the selector is disabled
- `<CodeBlockCopy>` renders <button class="ayy-code-block__copy">. Props: `code` string — code string to copy; if omitted, copies text from the nearest code element; `timeout` number — duration in ms to show the copied state (default 2000); `onCopy` (code: string) => void — callback fired when code is copied; `label` string — accessible label and tooltip before copy (default "Copy code"); `copiedLabel` string — accessible label and tooltip after copy (default "Copied!")
- `<CodeBlockPre>` renders <pre class="ayy-code-block__pre">. Props: 
- `<CodeBlockCode>` renders <code class="ayy-code-block__code">. Props: `language` string — language name or file extension for syntax highlighting (e.g. tsx, html, css, json, bash, md, python); `code` string — code content to highlight and display; if omitted, renders children

**Accessibility**
- Pre element is scrollable via keyboard by adding tabindex="0".
- Copy button has an accessible label (aria-label) and announces state changes.
- Line numbers use CSS counters with user-select: none to avoid being copied into the clipboard.
- Syntax token classes maintain WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast against the surface background in light and dark themes.

**Do**
- Use CodeBlock to display snippets, examples, configs, and commands with syntax highlighting.
- Include a CodeBlockFilename in the header when showing multiple files or language context.
- Include CodeBlockCopy so readers can easily copy snippet contents to clipboard.
- Use numbered on multi-line snippets when referencing specific lines in accompanying text.

**Examples**: Code block with filename and copy, Numbered lines, Language selector. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/code-block.md.

## Table

Category: Data display. Data table with quiet hairlines, muted sentence-case headers and hover rows, styled on plain table elements under .ayy-table. Optional frame with toolbar and pager; densities, column lines, sticky header, pinned and resizable columns; sortable, selectable (including drag-to-select across rows), expandable, grouped, linked and disabled rows; column menus with icons, insertion and wrapping; inline editable, empty, truncated and media cells; row actions. Cell content stays inside its column and ends in … unless the column wraps. Also called: table, data-table, datagrid.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-table-container` — Optional bordered frame on the page colour: .ayy-table__toolbar, the .ayy-table-wrap, a .ayy-table__pager. With a max-block-size its table scrolls inside.
- `.ayy-table__toolbar` — Bar above the table: a __heading and __tools.
- `.ayy-table__heading` — Stack of __title and __description.
- `.ayy-table__title` — The table's <h2>.
- `.ayy-table__description` — Muted line under the title.
- `.ayy-table__tools` — Toolbar's end cluster: search, filters, a columns menu, a button.
- `.ayy-table__pager` — Bar under the table: the range shown and a Pagination.
- `.ayy-table-wrap` — Scroll container around the table.
- `.ayy-table` — On the <table>. Styles thead/tbody/tfoot/tr/th/td/caption inside.
- `.ayy-table--compact` — Tighter rows (2rem headers).
- `.ayy-table--spacious` — Roomier rows and columns.
- `.ayy-table--bordered` — Lines between the columns too.
- `.ayy-table--sticky` — Header and footer rows stick while the wrap or container scrolls.
- `.ayy-table--fixed` — table-layout: fixed.
- `.ayy-table--reorderable` — Draggable header cells that reorder columns on drop.
- `.ayy-table__draggable` — On a th: indicates this column header can be dragged to reorder columns.
- `.ayy-table__column-header` — Flex row holding the column label, optional icon and column menu.
- `.ayy-table__column-label` — Column label or sort button; takes the room the menu leaves and ends in … when the column is narrower.
- `.ayy-table__column-icon` — Optional icon before a column's label.
- `.ayy-table__add-column` — Narrow trailing column with an accessible add-column button.
- `.ayy-table__wrap` — On th/td: content wraps within the column instead of staying on one line and ending in ….
- `.ayy-table__num` — On th/td with numbers: end-aligned, tabular digits.
- `.ayy-table__sort` — A <button> inside a sortable <th> (or, with aria-haspopup="menu", the title that opens the column menu), its label in a __column-label, the whole header cell clickable, an arrow after the text only once sorted. aria-sort on the <th> marks the sorted column.
- `.ayy-table__resize` — Column resize separator (<span tabindex="0">) at a header cell's end: drag, arrow keys; double-click resets.
- `.ayy-table__select` — On the th/td holding a row's checkbox (and the select-all box): as narrow as the box.
- `.ayy-table__reorder` — On the th/td holding a row's .ayy-drag-handle: as narrow as the handle. The row drags by it; a primary line shows where it lands.
- `.ayy-table__pin` — On a column's th/td: sticks to the inline start when scrolling sideways.
- `.ayy-table__pin--end` — With __pin: sticks to the inline end.
- `.ayy-table__truncate` — On a <span> in a cell: one line ending in …, at most --ayy-table-truncate (16rem).
- `.ayy-table__edit` — On an Inline edit (.ayy-inline-edit) in a cell: editable text that reads like cell text at rest, outlines on hover, turns into a field in place with the text where it was, saves on Enter or blur and reverts on Escape.
- `.ayy-table__media` — Flex row in a cell: an Avatar or icon, then text.
- `.ayy-table__secondary` — Muted second line in a cell.
- `.ayy-table__expand` — Chevron <button aria-expanded> that shows the __detail row after its row.
- `.ayy-table__detail` — The <tr> after an expandable row; hidden while its __expand is aria-expanded="false".
- `.ayy-table__group` — A <tr> heading a group: one <th colspan scope="rowgroup"> with its label in a <span>. One per <tbody>.
- `.ayy-table__empty` — On the <td colspan> of a body's only row when nothing matches.
- `.ayy-table__row-link` — The row's main <a>; its ::after covers the row. Other controls stay above it.
- `.ayy-table__actions` — On the trailing th/td holding row actions: end-aligned, narrow.
- `.ayy-table__row-actions` — Cluster of row action buttons and the ⋯ menu trigger.
- `.ayy-table__row-actions--reveal` — Shows only on row hover, focus, selection or open menu (always on touch).

**States**
- `hover` (`tbody tr:hover; the sort, expand, resize and edit controls; a row link`)
- `focus` (`:focus-visible on the sort button, expand button, resize handle or row link; :focus-visible on the .ayy-table__edit field`)
- `disabled` (`tr[aria-disabled="true"]`)
- `selected` (`tr[aria-selected="true"] (set by ticking a checkbox, Shift+click, or dragging and holding the cursor across rows)`)
- `error` (`.ayy-table__edit[aria-invalid="true"]`)
- `loading` (`aria-busy="true" on the <table>`)
- `sorted` (`th[aria-sort]`)
- `expanded` (`.ayy-table__expand[aria-expanded="true"]`)
- `resizing` (`.ayy-table__resize[data-dragging]`)
- `reordering` (`th[data-dragging] or th[data-drop-edge]`)
- `row-reordering` (`tr[data-dragging] or tr[data-drop-edge]`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Headers 2.25rem, cells padded 12px; compact 2rem headers, tighter rows; spacious 2.75rem, 16px. Text follows data-density.
- Width — Fills its wrap, which scrolls when columns don't fit. After a column resize it stays at least as wide as its wrap, even with no data columns.

**Custom element** `<ayy-table>` (@danitesler/ayywi/elements) — 
- event `ayy-sort`: { column, key, direction } before the rows move (key: data-sort-key). preventDefault() to sort them yourself.
- event `ayy-selection-change`: { rows } — the selected <tr>s.
- event `ayy-expand-change`: { row, expanded }
- event `ayy-column-resize`: { column, key, width } when a resize ends (width null after a reset).
- event `ayy-cell-edit`: { row, cell, column, key, value } when an inline edit in a cell saves a change.
- event `ayy-column-reorder`: { from, to, key, targetKey } when a column is dragged to a new position.
- event `ayy-row-reorder`: { from, to, id } when a row is dropped, or moved with the arrow keys on its handle. from and to count rows with a handle; to is what Array.splice wants after removing the row. id is the row's data-id.
- event `ayy-column-action`: { action, column, key, value } before a column action. Cancel to handle it in application state. data-column-action: sort-ascending, sort-descending, duplicate, hide, delete, freeze, wrap, icon (data-column-value), insert-before/insert-after (logical order), insert-left/insert-right (physical direction), add, filter, group, group-by (data-column-value). Filter/group open the toolbar button with data-table-control=filters/groups.

**React** — `import { Table, TableContainer, TableToolbar, TableHeading, TableTitle, TableDescription, TableTools, TablePager, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell, TableEdit, TableResize, TableExpand, TableGroup, TableEmpty, TableRowLink, TableMedia, TableSecondary, TableRowActions, TableCaption } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";`
- `<Table>` renders <div class="ayy-table-wrap"><table>. Props: `compact` boolean; `spacious` boolean; `bordered` boolean; `sticky` boolean; `fixed` boolean; `reorderable` boolean; `onColumnResize` ({ column, key, width }) => void; `onCellEdit` ({ row, cell, column, key, value }) => void; `onColumnReorder` ({ from, to, key, targetKey }) => boolean | void; `onRowReorder` ({ from, to, id }) => boolean | void — a row's DragHandle was dropped or moved by key. React doesn't move rows itself: reorder your data and return false.; `onColumnAction` ({ action, column, key, value }) => boolean | void — return false to update application state; `wrapperProps` props for the .ayy-table-wrap (a max-block-size for sticky)
- `<TableContainer>` renders <div class="ayy-table-container">.
- `<TableToolbar>` renders <div class="ayy-table__toolbar">.
- `<TableHeading>` renders <div class="ayy-table__heading">.
- `<TableTitle>` renders <h2 class="ayy-table__title">.
- `<TableDescription>` renders <p class="ayy-table__description">.
- `<TableTools>` renders <div class="ayy-table__tools">.
- `<TablePager>` renders <div class="ayy-table__pager">.
- `<TableHeader>` renders <thead>.
- `<TableBody>` renders <tbody>.
- `<TableFooter>` renders <tfoot>.
- `<TableRow>` renders <tr>. Props: `selected` boolean; `disabled` boolean — aria-disabled; `detail` boolean — the row under an expandable row
- `<TableHead>` renders <th scope="col">; a sort <button> when sortable; a TableResize when resizable. Props: `numeric` boolean; `select` boolean; `actions` boolean; `pin` boolean | "start" | "end"; `sort` "ascending" | "descending" | "none"; `onSort` () => void — flip with nextSortDirection(); `resizable` boolean; `reorderable` boolean; `icon` ReactNode — before the label; `menu` ReactNode — a composed DropdownMenu beside the label; `wrap` boolean — wraps the header label instead of ending it in …
- `<TableCell>` renders <td>. Props: `numeric` boolean; `select` boolean; `reorder` boolean — the narrow column holding a row's DragHandle; `actions` boolean; `pin` boolean | "start" | "end"; `truncate` boolean — wraps content in a .ayy-table__truncate span; `wrap` boolean — wraps long cell content instead of ending it in …
- `<TableEdit>` renders <InlineEdit className="ayy-table__edit"> — a display button and an <input>, or a <textarea> when multiline. Props: `value` string — controlled cell text; `defaultValue` string — uncontrolled starting text; `aria-label` string — names the button and the field: "Plan for Northwind"; `displayValue` ReactNode — what the cell shows at rest when it isn't the value (a formatted price); `multiline` boolean — textarea; Shift+Enter adds a line, ⌘Enter or Ctrl+Enter saves; `disabled` boolean; `placeholder` string — shown when the cell is empty; `className` string — extra classes on the root; `inputMode` string — the input's virtual keyboard; `onValueCommit` (value: string) => void — called on Enter or blur when the value changed
- `<TableResize>` renders <span class="ayy-table__resize" role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical" tabindex="0">.
- `<TableExpand>` renders <button type="button" class="ayy-table__expand" aria-expanded>. Props: `expanded` boolean
- `<TableGroup>` renders <tr class="ayy-table__group"><th colspan scope="rowgroup"><span>. Props: `colSpan` number
- `<TableEmpty>` renders <tr><td colspan class="ayy-table__empty">. Props: `colSpan` number
- `<TableRowLink>` renders <a class="ayy-table__row-link">.
- `<TableMedia>` renders <div class="ayy-table__media">.
- `<TableSecondary>` renders <span class="ayy-table__secondary">.
- `<TableRowActions>` renders <div class="ayy-table__row-actions">. Props: `reveal` boolean
- `<TableCaption>` renders <caption>.

**Accessibility**
- Use real <th> cells with scope (React sets scope="col"); a cell naming its row can be <th scope="row">.
- Name the table: a <caption>, or aria-labelledby pointing at the .ayy-table__title.
- Sort buttons are reachable by Tab and announced with aria-sort; only the sorted column carries it.
- Row checkboxes, expand buttons and row action buttons need aria-labels naming their row ("Select INV-1042", "Show details for INV-1042"); point an expand button's aria-controls at its detail row.
- Resize handles are focusable separators with aria-valuenow in px: arrow keys resize (Shift: bigger steps), Home/End jump to the limits.
- Set aria-busy="true" while rows load, and aria-disabled="true" on rows that can't be acted on (disable their controls too).

**Do**
- Use a table to compare items across the same attributes.
- End-align numbers with numeric; a cell keeps to one line, so put the full text in its title and add wrap to a column that must show it all.
- Make scanned columns sortable; put the raw value in data-sort-value when the cell shows a formatted one.
- Frame a working table with TableContainer: title, search and a columns menu above, Pagination below.
- Compose a column menu with TableHead menu and icon, or make the title itself the trigger (a .ayy-table__sort button with aria-haspopup="menu" as the TableHead child, set aria-sort on the th): clicking the title opens the menu, which holds a Sort submenu, Duplicate, Hide and Delete, and dragging it still reorders. data-column-action wires sort-ascending/sort-descending (a Sort submenu), duplicate, hide, delete, freeze, wrap, icon, insert-before/after, add and shared filter/group controls. Return false from onColumnAction or cancel ayy-column-action to own the data changes.
- Pin the name column on wide tables; use sticky with a max-block-size on long ones.
- Use expandable rows for details that don't deserve a column, and group rows to split a list by status or date.
- Put quick actions and a ⋯ DropdownMenu in a trailing actions cell; pair selection with an ActionBar for bulk actions.
- Show TableEmpty with an EmptyState when a search matches nothing.

**Examples**: Simple, Medium, Playground. Copy-ready HTML and React in llms/table.md.

## Grid

Category: Data display. A grid of cards that can be selected, for media, projects, posts and records. It combines card selection, quick actions on each item and a select-all control, and works with the Action bar. Also called: data-grid, card-grid, media-grid, asset-grid, gallery-grid, tile-grid.

**Classes**
- `.ayy-grid-wrap` — Stack wrapper grouping the grid toolbar, the card grid and the floating Action bar.
- `.ayy-grid__toolbar` — Header bar above the grid holding the select-all checkbox, count and sorting or view controls.
- `.ayy-grid__select-all` — Labelled select-all checkbox control in the grid toolbar.
- `.ayy-grid` — Responsive CSS grid container: as many card columns of at least --ayy-min (16rem) as fit.
- `.ayy-grid--compact` — Dense variant (--ayy-min: 13rem, tighter gap and card padding) for media libraries and directories.
- `.ayy-grid__item` — Selectable record card (<article>). Highlights with a 2px text-colour border and tint when aria-selected="true".
- `.ayy-grid__media` — Top preview frame for images, screenshots, social post visuals or video thumbnails. Floating glass corners when .ayy-grid__select or .ayy-grid__actions sit inside.
- `.ayy-grid__header` — Top block of the card holding the checkbox, avatar/icon, title, description and item actions.
- `.ayy-grid__select` — Wrapper for the card's selection Checkbox (inline in the header or floating in the top-start corner of .ayy-grid__media).
- `.ayy-grid__actions` — Cluster of quick action buttons (Edit, Copy) and the ⋯ DropdownMenu trigger (inline in the header or floating in the top-end corner of .ayy-grid__media).
- `.ayy-grid__actions--reveal` — Reveals item actions when the card is hovered, focused within, selected or has an open menu (stays visible on touch screens).
- `.ayy-grid__title` — Card heading (<h3>).
- `.ayy-grid__description` — Muted subtitle, handle or supporting metadata line.
- `.ayy-grid__body` — Card body content between header and footer.
- `.ayy-grid__footer` — Bottom bar for status Badges, timestamps or avatars, pinned to the bottom of stretched cards.

**States**
- `hover` (`.ayy-grid__item:hover`)
- `focus` (`.ayy-grid__item:focus-within`)
- `selected` (`.ayy-grid__item[aria-selected="true"] (with a Checkbox in .ayy-grid__select)`)

**Sizes**
- Density — Card padding is fixed (16px, 12px when compact); checkboxes and action buttons inside follow data-density.
- Width — Fills its container with auto-fitting columns at least --ayy-min wide (16rem default, 13rem compact).
